The microphone easily attached to my camera. I did like that there was a replacement camera mount included (the red piece) as I’ve heard of people breaking those for similar looking mics. This one DID come attached to the red mount so there were no issues and I have a spare. The red piece is fairly flexible which has both pros and cons as the mic can move a little and not stress this piece, but the con being the mic can move.

As far as the mic audio, there was a good improvement when about 3 feet away and a major improvement when up closer. The audio is cleaner than the on mic camera which makes this a nice minor cost improvement.

There are different cables which allow you to attach the camera to a standard audio port or a TRRS port like on some iPhones.

The mic does not need batteries so there are no issues with needing the check the batteries before each use. This does seem to have a downside somewhat in that the mic doesn’t really have a power boost which would come from the batteries.

The mic comes with a pop filter screen as well as a wind screen filter which are nice additions for recording audio in any condition.

The mic can be sensitive with some light wind so if there is a breeze do not forget the wind screen filter.

I would definitely recommend this as a low cost alternative to the similar Rode mic.

I am not going to cover every feature in detail since other reviews have some an excellent job of that. My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015.

This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015.

I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected.

What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality.

review_title: Cloning? This is probably not your best option
review_text:
I thought that I'd save a few bucks and grab this instead of the Crucial SSD in approximately the same size that was about ten bucks more. Unfortunately I did not read the full description and discovered that this does not come with cloning software or any software. The Crucial drive comes with cloning software that is easy to use and effective.

All is not lost, however. Although this is listed as an internal drive, the case is sturdy enough to use as an external drive without purchasing a separate enclosure. All you need is a SATA to USB cable and a spare USB port on your device, and you are good to go. I am using a StarTech cable that supports USB 3.0 and everything works like a charm.

For the price and the capacity this is a decent deal if you are looking for extra storage. If you are thinking about cloning, though, look elsewhere. Make sure that whichever brand that you get comes with bundled software. A number of other brands, including that one that I ultimately purchased for the cloned drive, come with OEM versions of an app called Acronis True Image. The bundled version will only work with the brand of SSD that it comes with, but for replicating a drive for safety, upgrading, etc. it works well.

review_title: Beautifully made from quality materials (and NO split leather or other shortcuts)
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Frankly, this is probably the best crafted bag I have owned in the past twenty years (and I have one from Booq.) The reason for the high rating is the leather parts are the real thing. Too often these days you get split leather, which is a thin veneer of leather over polyurethane. Not the case here - the leather is not only the real thing, but is generously cut.

The construction is excellent in every respect. The canvas is high quality, all of the stitching and seams are straight and tight, and reinforcement points are heavy-duty. Moreover, the zippers are as heavy-duty as the other parts.

Unlike many bags (even high end ones) that have a chemical odor when you unpack them for the first time, this one does not. The lining is synthetic, which resists water (but I would not claim this to be waterproof.) The snaps, reinforcing rivets and other metal are designed to look like brass, but are probably steel since a magnet will stick to them.

The pockets and compartments make this an excellent work bag that can accommodate smaller laptops. I use mine for my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet]], which is an easy fit. That leaves me room to spare for other odds and ends, as well as music charts. The main interior pocket is about 13 7/8 inches wide by 10 inches tall. If you are purchasing this for a laptop use those dimensions to determine if this bag will work for you.

Overall, I am not only pleased, but surprised by how well this is made and the quality of the materials. I want to emphasize that this may not fit many of the larger laptops on the market, but is still a great bag for books, tablets and assorted other gear. I hate gushing, but in this case I think the bag warrants it.

review_title: Inexpensive DAC that is easy to install and performs nicely
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I actually had a need for one of these because I wanted to run an audio signal out of my Yamaha receiver to an older analog reel-to-reel recorder. The receiver had a toslink out, and the recorder had RCA in. This box was the perfect DAC.

My signals were noise free, but understand that I was not running the analog cable more than a meter. So in that respect I did not have an adequate test of noise characteristics for longer cable runs. Moreover, I did not really use the volume feature. I set it mid way and used controls on the recorder for volume level. However, for my needs this worked perfectly.

The instructions are a little weak, but anyone who knows what a DAC is should be able to connect and use this without them. The power supply is a standard 5V DC at 1 Amp with a center positive connector. I ran it for an extended length of time and it did not overheat (I have learned from experience to test power supplies because of occasional failures and issues.)

Overall, this is a reasonably priced DAC that I found to be easy to use. The performance was what I had hoped, so am pleased with it.

For my needs, though, this is all I require and I am very pleased with it.

review_title: Superior sound, but not so good app and instructions
review_text:
I received one of these as a free review sample. Up front, the reason I subtracted a star is the set-up using the libratone app is maddening (to say the least.) On the other hand the sound quality is simply the best I have come across for a wireless speaker. That means I have to eat some recent words along the lines of there is no bluetooth speaker that is truly audiophile quality. This speaker disproves that.

Out of the box this quickly pairs and connects to bluetooth devices. I tested mine with a Note 4 phone and it took literally seconds to have it up and running. I was so blown away by the fact that this speaker reproduces music in a neutral manner by default that I was ready to sit down and give it a glowing review. Then I downloaded and installed the app.

The app is the Achilles heel. It had trouble finding the speaker, and the scant instructions were not very helpful either. Some how, some way it finally found the speaker, then was totally confusing when it came to setting up my personal profile (speaker location, bias and other features.) It also presented me with radio stations that were accessible via WiFi, and after connecting to my router I was able to access those. However, I am not personally interested in those offerings so did not explore them too deeply.

Basically, the app is good for linking multiple speakers, and some basic controls. Since I still cannot get the profiles set correctly I cannot speak about those. I will say that out of the box, without the libratone app and just connecting from my phone via bluetooth this speaker is spectacular. That is why I gave it the four stars that I did.

Bottom line: if you are looking for [possibly] the best bluetooth speaker on the market (and, yes, that includes Bose), this is it. If you want a speaker that can do everything this one is supposed to do, including fine tuning it for your room and musical tastes, you may be disappointed or frustrated. With a more intuitive app and more detailed instructions this would easily be a solid five star product that would keep Bose engineers and marketing up late at night. Until that happens, though, it's merely a superior bluetooth speaker that has crossed over into audiophile country.

review_text:
I received this cable with a keyboard bundle similar to [[ASIN:B014G8W338 Casio Privia PX-360 Digital Piano - Black TMS CABLE Bundle]]. While I have not used it with the keyboard, I have used it for other connections. It has proven to be reliable and noise-free in a number of roles and environments.

The outer sheath is actually pretty beefy, but does not hamper the flexibility of the cable. The strain reliefs did give me pause because I was initially unsure if they would allow for a decent bend radius, but after literally dozens of times of using this cable as a patch or primary connection cable between amplifiers and bluetooth receivers, and other connections it has not failed. It has proven to be so reliable that it's now in my gig bag and I am planning to purchase a few spares for my home studio and other uses.

Bottom line: I go through a lot of cables. Some because they are cheaply made and fail (unlike this one), and others because I either misplace them or need more than one. For minijack cables I have settled on this brand and model for patch and short connection cables.

review_title: Outstanding protection, although bulky and heavy
review_text:
I purchased this solely because of how happy I am with the [[ASIN:B00NF4SXSO OtterBox Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Case Defender Series]] that I have been using for the past five months. That case has saved my Note 4 twice from falls, so I did not hesitate to purchase this along with my Tab Pro 8.4.

This case WILL add a lot of bulk and weight to your tablet, so if you are looking for sleek, this is NOT the case you want. For me I wanted the assurance that my tablet would be protected and this is the only case that I have found that will do that. The way the rim around the screen is beveled and how it recesses the screen is a nice level of protection. I am guessing that the included screen protector is effective, since I did not use the included one with my Note 4 case (I opted for the Zagg for that phone, but I am using the protector that came with this case and it does allow complete sensitivity. Time will tell.

Installation is straightforward and easy. I had mine completely installed in about five minutes. Of course I had prior experience with the Note 4 case, and there was a learning curve because the instructions are a little terse. All of the cutouts are also precise. The case does not hamper access to any feature or interfere with the camera. Ports have tabs that seal them against water and dust. Frankly I do not need that level or protection and actually cut off the tab protecting the charging port. However, if you work in harsh environments those are nice features. Also, I do not use the back cover that has the kickstand for propping the tablet up. Mine spends most of its time on a music stand, but if I were to use it outdoors or in harsh environments, the back cover is an additional layer of protection.

Bottom line: if you want protection this is a great case. If you want slim and trendy you will probably not like it, though.

review_text:
I've been using Sabrent products for a few years - most were free review samples. When I needed a SATA enclosure I was happy to spend my own money on this model because I have come to trust the brand.

This is simple and straightforward. I literally unscrewed the panel with the supplied screwdriver, mated my [[ASIN:B013J7PP96 ADATA USA Premier SP550 120GB 2.5" SATA III Solid State Drive]] to the connector, attached the supplied USB A cable and was up and running. No fuss and the entire set up took mere minutes.

I did need the instructions to make sense of the supplied USB cable because it was a Y on one end. The USB A connector in the Y end, on the thicker part of the split cable, goes to the target machine and the single USB A connector attaches to the enclosure's USB port.

One thing I truly like is the small, blue LED that indicates that the SATA drive is powered and operational. Also, a quick examination of the printed circuit board revealed a clean design with no issues. For the price this is perfect for 2.5" SATA drives and for the ease of use earned five solid stars from me.

review_title: This has come a long way since the Roku 2
review_text:
I'll keep my review brief because there are a number of excellent ones that go into the features and benefits. I am approaching this as someone who owned a Roku 2 and was on the fence about moving up.

Here are the features I personally like: integrated YouTube access. When I got the Roku 2 a few years ago that was only possible with a third party service and forced me to also purchase a Chromecast to conveniently access YouTube. So for me, this feature alone justified the upgrade because that particular channel is important to me.

Another improvement - for me - is you can now select Paypal in lieu of a credit card. I do not use credit cards, and had to purchase a prepaid one to install the earlier model. You cannot get through the install process without some payment method. There are no hidden charges, but the payment method is required to be on file in case you may want to pay for a premium service. If you have Paypal and do not want to (or cannot) give a credit card number, you can still proceed with the installation process.

Installation, like the earlier model, is a breeze. I had mine up and running in practically five minutes.

As for the voice feature - I honestly never bothered with it so cannot say one way or the other if it's good or bad. Check other reviews for that. I will say that the upgrade was worth it to me. If you are still on a Roku 2 and are happy with it in all respects this is not going to be a bargain. If you want expanded features and channels and faster response this is a good choice.

If you are new to Roku and are considering cutting the cable this is worthwhile - I am using Netflix at less than ten bucks per month and am getting all the entertainment I want from just that. It's certainly a bargain for me compared to local cable services, which I deem to be way overpriced. This may be the first step in 'cutting the cable' if Netflix, Prime Movies or other inexpensive services have offering that satisfy your needs.

review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I'll spare you a regurgitation of the product specs or paraphrasing the previous two reviews, but will focus on what sets this one apart from the pack.

The biggest surprise I had was volume. This is a relatively small speaker and most bluetooth speakers in this one's size and price range are designed as personal speakers that are meant to be nearby on a desk, night stand or counter top. I can clearly hear this one two rooms away indoors and even outdoors in areas with high ambient noise this can cut through and project sound.

Sound quality is neutral, and I mean that in a good way. While there is some bias towards the mid range frequencies it does not 'color' the sound of music being streamed to it. To be honest, this is not going to crank out heavy bass, so if you listen to bass-centric music you may be disappointed. On the other hand, the highs and lows are practically seamless, with a slight emphasis towards the mid range, so if you listen to jazz, blues or some forms of rock and Americana this speaker will probably please you.

One review discussed bluetooth range issues so I specifically tested that. Even two rooms away, which normally causes drops in quality, I was able to get crystal clear streaming with no drops in the music quality streamed from a Samsung Note 3. The distance is approximately twenty feet, but definitely not line of sight, so I am happy with that aspect.

While the product specs claim six hours of music, you can realistically expect somewhere between four and four and a half hours if you have the volume cranked. If you drop it to about a quarter - perfect for near listening up to two or three meters - you will get the claimed play time.

review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. This is not a zoom type telescope. You can adjust focus for your objective (the 52mm end) as well as the eye lens (the 16mm end), but you will not be able to zoom in. Think of this as a mono scope that can bring a far object into sharp focus.

Another thing to note is the field of vision is less than the 18 degrees marked on the body. It's about half that, and the night and day marking does not imply that this is a night vision scope. You will still need an external light source in low level lighting conditions. For example, moonlight will work, but in total darkness you will not be able to see a thing.

For me this is very useful for a hobby of mine, which is reptile spotting. Where I live there is an abundance of species, especially turtles and snakes, but we also have alligators and many interesting lizards. I prefer observing gators from a distance, and when walking down trails in parks (and there are many in my area) it's nice to be able to sit in a stationary point and scan for gators on banks as well as swimming. Same for various snakes, both land and water.

What I love about this scope is it's rugged. There are no lens caps, but the nylon case that comes with it makes it ideal for outdoors activities in harsh environments. It's outer material appears to be rubber, and I have dropped mine a few times without damaging it.

When you do bring an object into focus it's sharp and crystal clear. The field of vision may seem narrow, but you can actually take in a lot of details by slow scanning. It may take a little time to get accustomed to viewing wide fields of vision with it, but once you do, it's easy to use.

review_title: Allowed me to use a condser mic with my Samsung tablet
review_text:
I purchased this specifically to connect a condenser mic to my Samsung Tab 3 10.1. I needed two other devices to make it work - an XLR M to F cable and a phantom power source (for the latter I am using an [[ASIN:B00KAPGLQC InnoGear® 1- Channel 48V Phantom Power Supply]] and the combination works like a charm.

The cable itself is not especially heavy gauge, but the connectors and strain reliefs are high quality. I live the precise fit of both the 3.5mm and XLR connectors, and the strain reliefs are such that the critical areas on both ends will not be subjected to bends that will fray or harm the inner conductors.

Of course, the main point for me is this works with my tablet, and it not only does for it, but also for my Note 3 phone. I use my tablet as a video camera for recording musical performances and until I added a condenser mic (an MXL 551R) the sound quality was poor. Since using the mic - made possible in part by this cable - the sound quality has dramatically improved.

Basically, I carefully checked out a number of similar cables and this is the one that had the best reviews and specs. I paid more for it, but feel that I also received commensurate value because of the construction and overall solid performance.

review_text:
I received this as a review sample. I had low expectations regarding the sound quality, but was pleasantly surprised. In particular, the mid range response is rich and full, with a decent high end that does not break up, and a low end that turned out to be unexpectedly boomy. Not in your face boomy, but not anemic either.

Also, this paired and connected easily to my Note 3 phone. I did not make test calls with it so cannot credibly discuss that feature. I also only wear it occasionally and normally for an hour or two in the evening or morning if I am outside, so cannot validate the battery life claims. Even if those are in the ballpark (and I suspect they are) then their specs are excellent for any speaker in this price range.

Finally, the cap keeps my head and ears warm in thirty and forty degree weather, which we actually have in central and north Florida Granted it is not many days out of the year, but when we do have sub thirty degree weather a cap such as this is greatly appreciated, and is a key feature in my opinion.

Regarding the speakers protruding as claimed by another reviewer, that is true to a point. But they do not look horrible (or not to me anyway). My high rating is based on the sound quality, ease of pairing and play time, and the fact that they keep my ears warm.

review_title: Perfect for reading new and legacy cards
review_text:
I received one of these as a review sample and as soon as I plugged it into an old ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP it was recognized and operational. What I love is you can read the newer SDXC cards, as well as the legacy TF ones.

Although I did not test this with USB 3.0, on my 2.0 laptop it was a lot faster than older card readers when I opted to write. Reading seems to be about the same speed as other readers.

This page has a full set of product specs and I normally do not regurgiutate them, but I do want to rememphasize one bit of information that will set your expectations: 'SD card and TF card sharing one channel can not be read simultaneously.' By channel I am guessing that these two slots share the same bus since they are ajacent to one another on the bottom of the reader chassis. 

One thing that I love that is not technical is the form factor and the looks. This is small enough to fit in a shirt pocket (pigtail and all), and the brushed metal look is gorgeous. In fact I own a hub from a different brand that looks like this reader's cousin, and it's perfect paired with a Macbook or even a [[ASIN:B00F2ENU92 Lenovo Yoga Multimode 10-inch Tablet]] via an OTG connection.

review_text:
Capacity is more than adequate for my needs, and the price is right. But the real reason why I gave it five stars is this drive is absolutely reliable. I have tried other brands only to experience premature death of the drive, data loss and other frustrations. In fact, one would get so hot in large transfers that it was uncomfortable to touch. This one does not have those flaws.

I use a pair of these. One for backing up my documents on my ThinkPad T61 running Win XP, and the other as a portable music library. For the latter use I've plugged it into my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Samsung tablet via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]], as well as a number of PCs and laptops of fellow musicians.

Just about every operating system, from my Android phone to a friend's Win 8 laptop immediately recognized this as a drive as soon as it was inserted in the USB port.

I did not bother measuring the transfer speed because I mostly use this for streaming music via USB. I have never experienced a freeze or lag in playing, so, again, I am very pleased with it. The final reason why I am happy is the small form factor, which is about the size of a bluetooth dongle.

Bottom line is you can save a few bucks by purchasing a competing brand, but you will get what you pay for in my opinion. I've been using this brand for literally decades and have never had to worry about failure or other issues.

review_title: New life for my ancient router
review_text:
Since there are detailed specs in the product description I will not repeat them here. Instead I'll use my personal experience with this kit to explain why I rated it five stars.

I used the review sample I received to extend the range of my ancient [[ASIN:B000BTL0OA Linksys WRT54GL Wireless-G Broadband Router]] (which is still working as well as when I purchased it ten years ago!) I removed one antenna from the Linksys, used a [[ASIN:B005IKGTXY Bluecell SMA female to TNC male Coaxial Adapter/Converter]] to adapt the included cable to the antenna connector, plugged it into the power supply and checked my home dead spot.

My dead spot is the master bedroom and my phone is always complaining about 'unstable WiFi connections' when I am in the room. I used an app called [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]] to perform the before and after tests.

Before I installed this booster kit I was getting a strong reading of -45 dBm near the router and an absymal -80 dBm in the dead room. After installing this kit the signal boosted to -55 dBm in the bedroom, so this booster kit works as advertised.

It's practically worth its weight in gold if you do have dead areas in your WiFi coverage. Based on my experience and how easy and fast this is to install I rate this as a five star product.

review_text:
Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

review_text:
I had the opportunity to directly compare my review sample to the [[ASIN:B001EZYMF4 Sennheiser CX 300 II Precision Enhanced Bass Earbuds]], which is a highly regarded IEM (in ear monitor) in the same price range. This one actually sounded better to my ears although both were nearly identical in specifications.

This is my third Brainwavz phone model, and I have quickly come to regard this brand as a real contender in the market. I will not lie - I much prefer the [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]] model because I love over-the-hear style phones. However, this set of phones, at about a third of the cost, is also close in sound quality as the HM9. In fact, the bass in this one is much better than the HM9 (or the Sennheiser CX 300 II to which I am directly comparing these.)

For me comfort is everything because I listen to music much of my time. These are perfect for both pleasure listening where I sit back and enjoy the music for its own sake. These are also good enough for me to hear every nuance when I am transcribing or studying a track to learn. In that respect these phones are good enough for professional musicians, but I will admit that they would not be my first choice for plugging into a high-end sound system.

Since I spend more time listening to MP3 tracks than off vinyl these do the job since MP3 files lose some fidelity by their very nature. I will say, though, that these phones passed my basic test suite, which includes Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]]. That is my reference model for sound because it contains high, mid and low frequency instruments that exercise any sound system. I listened to that album both from CD and from an MP3 file. Reproduction was superb.

Not only do these phones have respectable sound and comfort, the package is complete. They come with a zippered hard shell case, which protects the phones. However, they come with more extras that add to the value and provide versatility: a 1/4 adapter for plugging directly into standard headphone jacks, and an airplane adapter.

If you are in the market for mid-range IEMs give these serious consideration. In my opinion they are easily the equal of better known brands like the Sennheiser I mentioned and can be a better value if you need the extras that this set includes.

review_title: As good as the OEM cable that shipped with my Note 3
review_text:
I wanted a spare charging cable for my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and took a chance on this one. By that I mean that that other USB 3.0 cables that I have tried with the phone would charge it, but would not support full speed data transfers and synching. This one performed without issues and identically to my OEM Samsung cable that came with my phone.

The blue outer jacket is much thicker than the Samsung cable. Although it is slightly stiffer it's also pliable and easy to bend and coil. Part of the reason for the extra thickness is probably from the the foil and braid shielding. In fact, the shielding is one factor in this cable's ability to transmit data at such high speeds without error. Another factor is the gold plated connectors.

The bottom line is this cable seems to be the equal of the more expensive Samsung OEM cable. In my experience anyway. I have owned it for three months and it has been problem free in every respect.

review_text:
I have tested this card in both a Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and a [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch]] and it was immediately recognized by both devices. As I write this review the card has been running in my Tab 3 and constantly used for over a week.

I use a few pairs of these to rotate backups on my laptop, so I always have a daily snapshot of my documents. For that purpose alone these cards are well worth it.

review_title: Superior construction and extra long cable
review_text:
I received a review sample of this cord and charger combination and have been testing it thoroughly. The most striking feature is the three meter cable, which is the longest I have seen for any iPhone (or Android phone for that matter.)

My first inclination was to test the cable for failures because the length seemed excessive. It performed every data transfer and synching operation flawlessly. It also fast-charges like an Apple OEM cable. I was a bit surprised that this and the charger were not MFi certified (Made for iPhone/iPod/iPad). Other cables and chargers that I have received from the manufacturer were, but this is indistinguishable from the MFi and Apple OEM cables that I have tested - both visually and from a performance perspective.

The contacts on both the USB and Lightning connector ends are precision made and mate perfectly to the ports to which they were designed to connect. The outer jacket is thick, but not too stiff to make handling it a problem. There are strain reliefs on both ends to ensure a long service life.

This set includes a bonus wall charger with folding prongs. This has the same well made construction, and also puts out a steady 2.1A for fast charging. This charger is perfect for iPads too because of the output rating. If I had one wish it would have a second 1.0A port for those of us who want to simultaneously charge a phone and tablet - perhaps the next generation of this product will have that feature.

Bottom line: when size (in the form of cable length) matters this is one of the very few on the market that is a full three meters long. Add in the fact that this one is made to perform like an Apple OEM cable and the value should be apparent.

review_title: Great product that is being marketed to the wrong demographic
review_text:
When I accepted a review sample of this holder I had visions of using it to entice my constant companion to sit in the back and play with her iPad. Indeed, this hooked right onto the two posts of the front seat headrest that would allow a backseat passenger to watch movies and do whatever else they use the iPad for. My companion did not take the bait, so I was left with a review sample that, frankly, I could not give away.

Necessity is the mother of invention and the best use for this mount was in my music room. This hooks into my [[ASIN:B000CDUDQG Belmonte Orchestra Stand Deluxe Black]] to mount an iPad and still have room left for sheet music and a [[ASIN:0961470143 The New Real Book - Volume 1]]. I have uploaded customer-supplied photos to show how this securely attaches to the stand and holds an iPad in place (it will work with any tablet up to 10 inches.)

I love how this holder allows you to place your tablet at practically any viewing angle, and also how it positively and absolutely holds the tablet in place. For the record, these claims apply equally to the dual headrest posts in my 2014 Outlander and to the music stand cited above.

Personally, the manufacturer is missing a major market because tablets are now common on stages and in studios and I suspect that there is a much larger market for this holder than significant others who refuse to be relegated to the back seat. I am so pleased with this holder that I have already recommended it to fellow musicians.

review_text:
This review is of the 64GB SDHX card. I use it for a specific purpose: backing up my document folders on my two laptops. It works perfectly with my Windows XP systems over ancient USB 2.0 ports. I can still back up a full card in less than an hour, and if I were on a more modern system with USB 3.0 it would take only a fraction of that time.

This particular card will NOT work in my Samsung Galaxy Note II (I had to try anyway). In fact, make sure your device will actually accept SDHX cards before purchaing this 64GB model or you may be disappointed. Most Microsoft Windows systems running XP service pack 2 or later, Windows CE and Server 2003 will recognize this card, as will Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6.5 or later. Phones, tablets and devices running Microsoft Windows RT will also recognize this card. Beyond that check first.

Back to how I use this card: the price for this card is around forty bucks at the time of this review. I could have gotten an exernal hard drive in the terabyte range for twice that, but this has no moving parts, fits in my wallet and with a [[ASIN:B00FSDKBYY Sabrent SuperSpeed USB 3.0 Flash Memory Card Reader]] plugs into any computer (with an operating system that supports the format) via USB ports. For me it's convenient, especially since I am only backing up working documents and never come close to the 64GB capacity (which is closer to 56GB formatted.) In fact I use two of these in rotation for safety, overwriting the older one completely since it takes less than an hour. I always keep the other one on my person.

As the SDHX standard becomes more established and ubiquitous this type of card may work with more devices. At 64GB this is probably the smallest size since the SDHX format was designed to accomodate up to two terabytes. So unless you have a device that is compatible with this format, or you are using it for a single purpose on a supported operating system, you may want to get an SDHC card instead.

review_title: Works perfectly in my Note II
review_text:
Like others I opted for this more expensive card because I wanted peace of mind that it would work without problems with my Note II. I literally popped this in and it was immediately recognized and works like a charm.

I upgraded from a 32GB card that I managed to outgrow in six months (music junkie). Transfer from my old card to this one was simple. I used the following steps:

(1) Removed the old card from my Note II and placed it into the USB adapter which came with it.

(2) Plugged the USB adapter into my Windows XP laptop and mounted it as a drive. Marked the drive as sharable on my WiFi network.

(3) Inserted the new card into the Note II - it was recognized with no need to format.

(4) Connected to the shared drive (old card connected to my laptop) over WiFi and copied the contents to the new card.

For some reason I lost my playlists, but all of my music and other media came over perfectly. It's as though my storage magically doubled.

One thing I noticed is unlike my older card that heated up when i did the same procedure moving up from 16GB to 32GB is this one runs cool. The older card was a Sandisk, which was otherwise flawless and reliable. I just did not want to push the envelope with a 64GB card buy using anything but a genuine Samsung card because I heard there could be issues with cards in that capacity range. To me it was worth the extra bucks to be safe.

As for speed, I am going to take the lower numbers reported by others at face value. Assuming that this card is nowhere near as fast as Samsung claims, it's still fast enough for me.

If you have a Note II I highly recommend this card if you need the extra storage on your phone. It's a safe choice and works perfectly out of the box.

Highly recommended if you want a high-capacity flash drive that will work on older Windows 98 SE systems, or just a reliable and easy-to-install flash drive for any system. It will not work on Windows 95 and below systems (none of the flash drives of which I am aware will).

review_title: Finally - something that works for me
review_text:
This device isn't for everyone, but it fits my needs perfectly. It represents my third attempt to find an affordable, easy-to-use solution to getting scribbled meeting and design notes and drawings into my computer for quick dissemination to interested parties and stakeholders. I've previously tried the A.T. Cross-Pad (no longer made) and the Logitech IO Personal Digital Pen (ASIN B00006JP23), each of which fell short for various reasons.
Here is how I use it - during meetings I take notes, do sketches (user interfaces, high-level system design diagrams, etc.), and list follow-up items. This material is automatically beamed to my Palm Vx as pictures of the sketches and/or notes. I upload these to my PC and email them as attachments. This gets information out quickly, which can be followed up later with more refined notes transcribed into a word processor (by hand) or better drawings (I use Visio).
It does one thing only - captures pictures of what you write on plain paper - and it does that exceptionally well.
I liked the easy set-up, the fact that it comes with a QWERTY tap keyboard (it's under the pad), and performs as advertised. If your needs are similar to mine stated above and you have either a Palm or Pocket PC PDA you will probably love this notepad. However, it does not perform optical character recognition, so it that is what you're seeking you need to keep looking.

Definitely plug and play once you put in the USB receiver.

I think this is a quality item for the price and I will continue to purchase, as needed. I highly recommend its reliability.

A couple of times, I tried to use the radio with the so called back up battery that had been more than charged, but the radio doesn't operate with it. Also: You get static on the radio if your cordless phone activation is too close to the radio, but any microwave or radio wave (including flourescent lights) affect all radios, not just this one (that's the nature of transmission).

I bought the green model from Amazon, which is fine for me because I'm not fashion conscious about most things. After purchasing them, I discovered that Acorn sells them in different colors: red, yellow, etc.

In summation, I like this radio and all the little connections that come with it for the cellphone or computer tablet.

review_title: Belkin Easy Transfer Does Not Transfer Programs
review_text:
If you're looking for a cable that will transfer your programs as well as your files, this isn't it. I didn't expect it to do that when I bought it, but I hoped that it would. Shame on me, because I bought it without doing the research first. There are two products on the market that will migrate your programs as well as your files: one is Zinstall, which offers two versions, and the better of the two (XP7) is presently on sale - you can view a nice video on their website; the other is LapLink, which has received lukewarm or not so warm reviews.

If you have all your old programs on CD's as well as their product keys on hand, however, you might be able to install the programs manually and still use the Belkin Transfer Cable to transfer your files from the old computer. When I tried to manually install my MS Office 2007, which was an upgrade that I could use on up to two computers and for which I had the product key, the Windows 7 on the new computer would not accept it because it couldn't detect a previous copy on the new computer. The new computer came with an incomplete version of MS OFfice 2010, which isn't a PREVIOUS copy, but a more advanced copy, so it appeared that I was out of luck. I solved the problem with Zinstall XP7, which cost me $89 and allowed me to transfer files, settngs, and programs without needing any special cables. With Zinstall, you can use any type of computer cable- DSL, USB, whatever you have available. When the files are transfered, you're actually placing fresh copies of them onto the new computer; the original files remain on the old computer. So, if you plan to toss that old computer or donate it, and don't want anyone to inherit your personal business, you still need to delete those files from the old machine.

The Belkin Easy Transfer Cable for Windows 7 allows you to transfer the files from an XP, Vista, or 7 computer to a Windows 7. It comes with a CD that, similar to Znstall, you have to install onto the old computer and the target computer. You then follow very easy steps before you connect the cable. After you're instructed to connect the cable, you do just that and follow a few more steps. Because I used Zinstall, the Belkin software and cable were of no use to me.

UPDATE: On Windows Vista, I recently noticed an entry for transferring files and settings in the Control Panel. I haven't tried it, but I mention it in case readers are interested in following that link.

review_text:
This is an update of this Acer Iconia Tab W500-BZ467 tablet, which seemed promising at first, but after nearly three months of use, we're singing a different tune and lowering the rating from "I like it" to "Don't like it". I chose it for a friend who needed it for her medical practice. Now that patient records need to be digitized, she hoped to use this less expensive tablet alternately with the Asus Eee Slate EP 121-1A010 to keep track of all her business's management needs, which include patient vitals, records, and billing. In the doctor's own words:

"I log into Athena, which is our electronic medical record and practice management, and then all the info regarding a patient gets put in. So, the girls will use the tablet to populate BP, pulse, etc, past medical history, chief complaint, etc. Some of it is clicking onto specific fields and it will auto-populate with a touch. I think the ASUS Eee Slate is the perfect size screen by the way. I really like that one. The Acer is good but, screen is small so it's difficult to maneuver over fields."

The doctor purchased the recommended digital pen for the Acer, but it didn't provide the accuracy or manueverability that the ASUS has. It was also impossible to get the Acer to interface with her printer.

The Asus has the added advantage of a wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a digital pen, which I believe can be an asset for anything that requires a signature, e.g. a prescription or an MS Office Word business letter. It can also interface with the recommended HP wireless printer. The Asus also comes with a mediocre MS Office program that can be upgraded for a better version.

My initial favorites were the Apple iPad2 or a Toshiba tablet. However, neither of them comes with a Windows operating system (OS), which the folks at Athena.com, the doctor's business out sourcers, had recommended. Toshiba uses Google's Android and Apple uses its own system. While you can change Toshiba's OS to a Windows OS, I wouldn't recommend it if you're not technically savvy.

Even in the web browser, where clicking the scroll wheel will open a link in a new tab, or clicking the scroll wheel on a tab will close that tab, I'm constantly being faced with this irritating limitation.

1. Easy to set up - no tools required. Just attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew. (And recheck ever so often that it's tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. No neck burn or awkward carrying positions.

upside down,
from ONE screw,
in ONE spot,
on the bottom of the camera,
is a bit nerve-wracking. (But regular straps can malfunction also)

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

review_text:
This weird little tripod is a useful addition to the gear of any amateur or hobby photographer with a DSLR and the inspiration to take breath-taking and/or unusual photographs. (I'm using it with a Nikon D7000)

Pros:

1. Light and portable. If you don't have a side pocket on your camera bag, just wrap it around a strap or loop.
2. Flexible. As advertised, the legs can be bent into loops and angles for getting shots from weird angles. It can also be wrapped around posts, tree branches, bench rails etc.
3. Convenient. An easy way to get shots requiring a stable camera almost level with ledges or sideways attached to a tree. However, you can only shoot in landscape format unless you get the accessory BH1 ball head. Naturally, with its little legs, you'll be pretty close to the ground if there's nothing available for wrapping around, but you'll be sure to get great camera angles from a worm's eye view.

Cons:

1. Attaching your camera to the tripod is a bit of a pain, requiring a coin (any currency) or a strong fingernail. A better bet is to get the accessory Joby BH1 Ball Head with Bubble Level and attach the quick release clip to your camera beforehand.
2. You need to practice with it a bit to get the stability right, and if you have the legs in an unbalanced position, or on a smooth surface, you can get sagging and camera movement.
3. Trying to get the camera level without the ball head can be quite challenging, and you may well miss the shot. (Of course you can always do the straightening with software, but it's better to get it right the first time.)
4. Can't shoot in portrait format unless you get the ball head.

Included is a lens hood, manual and sturdy drawstring carrying case. For the price, weight and what it can do, this lens is highly recommended for portraits, low-light, general and street photography.

review_title: I do not like them, Sam-I-am
review_text:
I would not, could not,
on a plane.
Not in the park. Not on a train.
Not in a car. Not on CD.
I do not like them, Sam, you see.
Not in my bed. Not on a boat.
Not on my head. Too big to tote.
I will not use them here or there.
I do not like them anywhere!

Pros:

1. Looks and feels like the more expensive models
2. Nicely padded and sturdy
3. Comes with a handy drawstring carrying bag, or you can get the optional hard case, which is extremely durable
4. Folds up much smaller than it looks
5. Comes with an adapter so that two headphones can be connected to the same audio source
6. Comes with a nice long cord, so you can use it at your desktop comfortably
7. Cancels out noise from your surroundings to a certain extent
8. Reasonably priced

Cons:

1. No instructions. However, it only takes minutes to figure out where the battery goes (right side), how it folds and adjusts, and where the cord plugs in. (I had to figure this out right away, because it arrived with the switch in the "on" position and a dead AAA battery)
2. For the noise cancelling feature, the on/off button is located quite inconveniently behind your right ear
3. While it muffles some of the background noise, it still lets through quite a lot, and the hissing noise can bother some users. You can still hear the sound of the keys on a keyboard when you type, but when you take it off there is a noticeable difference. A loud party in the neighborhood became a lot more bearable with them on.
4. As a regular headphone this one is unfortunately not very good. You can hardly hear anything with the noise cancelling feature off, and when you put it on, it manages to remove all the bass resulting in a tinny sound.
5. Even folded, it's still quite bulky to tote around

Conclusion:

Rugged and expensive looking, this headphone promises effective noise-cancelling features and good audio sound.
Unfortunately, it falls short in both categories.
I do not like them, Sam-I-am

review_text:
This camcorder is a simple way for you to share videos with friends and family, make and share mini-movies, capture special moments, or film your next masterpiece for YouTube or Amazon.com.

Pros:
1. The "cool" factor is off the scale. Every time I showed it to somebody, they said "COOL!!!"

2. It uses two AA batteries that are easy to install. There's a latch at the bottom of the camera - one side has a picture of a closed lock, and the other has a picture of an open lock. It doesn't get simpler than that, does it? Push towards the open lock and slide off the panel on the front of the camera from just under the lens. After you put in the batteries, slide the panel back into place and push the latch back to the locked position. You're now ready to start filming.

3. There are very few buttons required to operate the camera. Turning it so that the side with the big red button is facing you, the on/off switch is on the right side of the camera. After powering up, the screen will light up with the Flip logo and then it will indicate that it's ready. At this stage you'll be looking at whatever's in front of you, with a time check at the bottom telling you how much video time you have left.

4. Filming is easy - just press the red button to start, and press it again to stop. The camera will save your creation, tell you how long it is and how much time you have left. You can zoom in and out by pressing the + and - signs on top of and below the red button. The microphone will pick up and record whatever's going on at the time.

5. Playback is a one button operation.

6. Deleting your mistakes is a one button operation.

7. You can scroll through your videos by using the arrow keys to the left and right of the red button.

8. Getting it on your computer is the easiest part. With the red button facing you, pull down on the latch on the left side, and - surprise!!! Out pops a USB arm which you then connect to your computer. Once you're linked up, the Flip Video software will show you the way home. (It takes a while to pop up) Choose the option to view your videos, and agree to the terms and conditions, and then the "Muvee Video Mixing Software" begins loading. This is a one time installation. From there you can easily play, name, edit and share your videos.

9. You can also capture still shots from your videos, but you can't use these when making your movies with the software provided.

10. There is an option for making a movie, where you can arrange your edited videos, choose from a selection of six movie styles and music, or even add your own music. Choose your style, click on the "Make Mix" button, and the computer does the rest. If you're happy with the results, you can save the file.

11. The camera comes with a wrist strap, a velvet drawstring case, and also the necessary cables to connect it to your television for a bigger view. There's also a place to connect a tripod.

12. There is a "Help" feature included with the software.

Cons:
1. Being a simple "point and shoot" camera, the resolution isn't fantastic, but quite good enough for action shots. Forget detail close-ups such as words and logos - zooming in and out will just get you various degrees of blurry.

2. You'll need to be careful with background noise, as the microphone will pick up the sound of your fan or your stomach growling.

3. The video editing capability is limited to the length of the video you want to save, and the order you want to save it. There are no options for titles, fade ins or outs or any bells and whistles. If you're filming yourself giving a speech, you'll pretty much have to get it right in one complete take.

4. As with all videos, if your hands shake, you'll need to get a tripod, or you may make a lot of people seasick.

5. If you have big fingers, you may have some problems with the red button. Once your finger covers the area around the button, you'll have trouble starting and stopping the video. If you can't get it to work, you may have to use just a fingernail, because if you press anywhere other than dead center of the red button it won't start or stop.

Overall, this is a very good camcorder if used for the purpose for which it is intended. It isn't going to make you the next Stanley Kubrick, but it's a good start.

Amanda Richards, October 9, 2007

review_title: How to look like a pro (even if you're not)
review_text:
This Targus notebook case is a great way to carry around all your stuff and still look cool, professional and ready for action.

The good stuff:

1. It can fit notebooks up to 17" securely and safely. There's a strap to hold your equipment in place, it's nicely padded and has an adjustable inner wall for extra snugness. It even opens like a briefcase for easy packing.
2. The same compartment has three pockets with Velcro closures, a zippered mesh pocket and some slots for letters, warranty cards or other documentation. There's ample space for a mouse (optical, cordless, furry with tail), flash drives, cds and dvds, cords, headphones, bells and whistles.
3. The zipper for the notebook section can be locked with a padlock.
4. The front flap has an easy fastener, and also has a zip pocket, right at the front of the bag, perfect for passport and tickets when traveling
5. Lift the flap for another compartment, and more pockets, with slots for pens, glasses, keys, and whatever else you like to carry around.
6. The back has a padded Velcro-closing pocket for newspapers, magazines or other reading matter.
7. Yet another zippered compartment has two slots for important documents and not so important documents.
8. The handle is tough rubber, defying you to mess with it, and the bottom and sides are protected with a corrugated rubber strip. You can set this one down on the floor - it can take it.
9. Even if you aren't carrying around a laptop all the time, this case works fine as a large briefcase for work or travel, with lots of room for a change of clothes, product samples, toiletries (make sure they adhere to airline safety regulations), files, manuals, snacks, extra undies and more.

The other stuff:
1. If you have a 17" laptop, there's not enough space in the padded section to hold your power cord, but there are so many other compartments and pockets that this shouldn't pose a major problem - other than remembering where you put it. (There's plenty of space for a bottle of Ginkgo Biloba)
2. It's pretty durn heavy to lug around, especially for those already having to contend with a full handbag, cup of coffee and high heeled shoes
3. The generous number of compartments encourages you to carry around more stuff than you need - just in case of emergencies. (And then of course you can't remember where you packed them in the first place)
4. It tends to fall over if you don't put it down carefully or lean it against something.
5. The strap looks a little cheap compared to the rest of the case, and keeps spinning around, so you always have to check that the padded piece is on the inside, but it's easier to carry it by the handle anyway.

Sturdy, roomy, comfy and a tad bit clunky, but overall a good case for larger notebooks, work or travel.

Amanda Richards, September 22, 2007

review_title: Sirui K-40x Ball Head Outstanding Quality/Value for Rock Solid results
review_text:
I was looking to purchase a gimbel head for a Nikon D750/Nikkor 200-500mm lens that was rock solid with my older heavy duty Bogen 3011 legs. A salesperson at Pro-Photo in Portland guided me over to this and I was wowed at first sight. Sitting next to the $400 ball heads I could immediately see the quality and value at about 30% of the cost. That translates to me as part of another lens or a few B&W filters. I have also recently paired a Fuji S5Pro body and Sigma 50-100mm Art lens. Both of these combos are just too heavy to get tack sharp shots handheld... and my attempts with a heavy mono-pod have been ok.. but less than perfect. This is not a tripod head/leg combo I envision carrying on my next vacation or on a hike through the mountains... I am 60 and have been buying and using tripods since I was 15. I believe in the heaviest tripod I can carry when I'm shooting photos out at 300-500mm and further. When I pop a spotting scope on and try and track targets out at 300-400-500 yards, a solid, pin point image saves a whole lot of walking. There is always a little creep with that last twist to maximum tightness...but once you get the hang of the tension wheel... I have yet to see my focus point move even slightly when locked in on an eagle nest for 10 days. As with other reviews I find the panning a little stiff... but if I was filming and airshow or Indy Race I'd probably put on a fluid video head instead. I anticipate many years of service and it will still be working long after I am. Today I ordered a Sirui K-30 from Amazon because while the K-20 is probable adequate for a D300 and D7100 with smaller lenses... who knows what I will come to own in the future... That's the one I'll carry to Hawaii with the light carbon-fiber legs. There is a great review on DPREVIews called Battle of the Titans.. Excellent quality with the bonus of an outstanding price point. I also have a lightweight Sirui carbon mono-pod that travels in my suitcase. 5 stars because the pros overwhelm the small cons.. I can live with those

George B Sitka, Alaska

review_title: Beautiful matte screen is so easy to see
review_text:
We have a high end Sony 55" in the living room and a sub three hundred buck off brand tv in the guest room and the difference between the two is instantly noticeable - image quality and sound are in two different lanes entirely. This Samsung Frame is in the master bedroom and I am in love.

The matte screen means almost no reflective glare at night with lights on in the bedroom. That's something I did not realize bothered me about our other two tvs until there was no more glare. No matter where I look at the screen, it's clear and I don't see the reflection of my bedside lamp.

This tv does weigh more than the other two we own in the same size. I would definitely not try to move this or wall mount it alone. The box has a complete wall mount ready to install, but I don't want this that high since it's a bedroom television, so we installed the feet and set it on a table. This also comes with an old school box for connections rather than just plugging everything in directly to the television. That's a little old school, but it makes sense because they intended for the tv to be used on the wall as an art display as well and you don't want visible cables hanging off that.

As far as the art viewing goes, that's really nice if you are willing to pay for the subscription. I am not, but viewing the samples is pretty cool. This is a Google and Alexa friendly voice control set up and I do like that. The free Samsung TV app is very nice - it's sort of like Pluto TV, but proprietary to this television brand. Lots of free channels and a ton of choices at no cost. We use Netflix, Prime, HBOMax, and Paramount Plus as our paid streaming options - no cable or satellite here, just streaming. Everything works seamlessly and smoothly. My favorite thing here though, is so simple and small and I can't understand why every tv doesn't have this - the remote control is SOLAR powered!! No more buying batteries and it works well.

review_title: Temperature monitor warning is an hour delayed
review_text:
My original Echo, purchased when the first invitations were sent out, was much beloved for years. She finally began to have performance problems last month. Stuttering, failing to perform tasks and simply not hearing her name anymore. Definitely time for an upgrade.

I like this Echo Plus, but I'm not thrilled with the short, fat, squatty shape over the tall, slender original Echo. This one doesn't fit in the same spot and just looks like any generic, knockoff speaker rather than Alexa. However, the sound quality of music and Audible books is superior and can be clearly heard at lower volumes than my old Echo.

I will say the coordination/communication between the physical Plus and the Alexa app is spotty and slow. In particular when using the Plus's built in temperature monitor. I had hoped specifically to use this to monitor our RV temperature when traveling for the safety of our dogs. Alexa does tell me the temperature has reached the preset warning level - an HOUR later!!! That's useless. I ended up spending more money to but a dedicated Wifi temperature/humidity monitor that alerts my phone via text and email literally within 90 seconds of the preset parameters. I love Alexa in general and we have 3 Dots, the Auto and this Plus, so we're fully integrated in the ecosystem, but this Plus isn't as good as the original, 1st generation Echo.

Supposedly we have three towers with a total of 14 stations in two towns within 45 miles of us. I have a clean line of sight for two of them within 15 miles and should get at least 8 stations. After messing around with this antenna for four days and moving it eight times, we never pulled in more than two stations. One is the local ABC affiliate and the other is some Spanish only channel.

In comparison, I borrowed a different indoor antenna from our next door neighbor and within minutes of attaching it, we had 8 different stations without a bunch of position drama. It's also smaller and less intrusive visually than this one. I think I will just buy one like my neighbor has instead and put this one away as a last resort backup.

review_title: Ok picture, tinny sound and only one HDMI port
review_text:
We've never had a projector before and this is a reasonable beginner/introductory projector. It helped us realize that we're not really projector people for a couple of reasons. It works best in a completely dark room or outside with no residual daylight or street lights. We found the best picture came from using the the included screen out on the patio around 9pm. The picture wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't really 1080p using the Roku stick. Going outside in the summer here for a movie is a cute idea, but this is Texas and it's just too humid and miserable for that.

The projector has speakers built in, but they are small and the sound is tinny. You can connect a sound bar if yours uses the RCA type cables - niether of my bars do. review_title: UPDATE REDUCED TO 2 STARS Beautiful sound, amazing with the 500 as a group.
review_text:
UPDATED REVIEW REDUCED TO TWO STARS JUNE 2019

We've had trouble with the remote for three months now. It works sporadically at best and has finally died entirely. This is a major problem because you cannot do important stuff with the sound bar without the original remote control. Such as.... rebooting it. If you change your WiFi network like.... getting a new router, then you cannot simply go to the app and update the connection. You must reboot the entire sound bar via the remote control only. WHICH DOES NOT WORK AT ALL. This design flaw has rendered the entire sound bar none functional because it cannot connect to the new Wi-Fi - going back to our old router isn't an option because it died. So now I have a sound bar that technically is operational, yet cannot be used. Our Bose 500 sound bar was able to be reconfigured for the Wi-Fi swap because it's remote works like a champ - it's also significantly simpler in design than the 700 remote. (I'll end up spending fifty bucks for a new 700 remote and that really aggravates me)

******* Original review before the drama*******

We've had an older Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System in our living room for a couple of years and we've been pretty happy overall. I recently put the Bose 500 version of this sound bar in our master bedroom and was amazed at the difference, so getting this 700 for the living room was a no brainer. I mostly just expected them to connect as a group and have the same sound, but this 700 is better than the 500.

It's a long, narrow, sleek looking unit with glass finishes that makes it almost invisible in front of the Tv. Our Roku fits alongside without drama. The connections are via digital optical cable or the HDMI. Just turn off your TV speakers - not mute, off from the tv settings. You need to use the included wired headset to fully set the speakers for your room's accoustics. I'm using this bar with a 55", 3 years old, Sceptre dumb tv and a Room streaming stick - the connection was immediate and drama free.

You must use the Bose app to get full functionality out of the sound bar. The app let's you connect two or more Bose speakers with the tech and use them all simultaneously as a group to play music or audiobooks etc. The app also starts the set up for the Alexa link and the streaming services like Prime, Tune In, Bluetooth streaming and others. You can also set 6 favorites as one touch launch options.

Alexa works fine through the sound bar, but the response speed is noticably slower than through a regular Echo. I get a glitchy message saying "This unit is unable to perform routines" every time I say "Good morning". Good morning triggers a specific set of actions from Alexa to turn on our bedside lamps, the bathroom lights, turn off our porch lights, give me the weather and then our daily news brief. Despite that glitchy message, every morning, the Bose performs our routine flawlessly. It's weird, but not a big deal really.

The sound quality is excellent and immersive in multiple settings from music to a movie. The app let's you adjust the sound quality and balance with bass, treble and center. You can also set it for dialogue mode to enhance/clarify voices and reduce background noise - this is very handy for the news or a talk show. Take some time to adjust the settings for what your ear really likes and you'll be amazed at the fullness of sound and all the background details.

After two weeks, I'm incredibly pleased with the build quality, looks, sound and full functionality of both the 500 and 700 units. The 700 wins out by a nose over the 500 for us because the sound is bigger, but mostly because the remote control is better. The remote lights up when you lift it and you can find the buttons instantly. I programmed our TV to the Bose remote and it controls the sound bar, channels up and down and power for both the tv and the sound bar. Bottom line is that I am now looking at buying another 700 for the master bedroom and moving the 500 to our guest suite so we'll have the full set.

review_title: Work well in high humidity working outside - stay in place without pinching
review_text:
I normally avoid in ear earbuds and use wireless headphones or do without. My ears are small and most earbuds hurt within minutes, but I have one really inexpensive set that works ok, but if I'm outside working in the horse barn, they can get sweaty and slippery. These are far better than I expected.

They come with three different size ear bud attachments so you can get the right fit - the smallest set fits me well and they don't pinch or hurt even after an hour of wearing them. The over ear hook isn't hard and it's thin enough to fit over each ear love when with my glasses on. I work with horses and the associated barn chores so that means sweat and lots of movement which can be a problem with earbuds. These have impressed me. After daily use for a week, they haven't fallen off, slipped out of place or lost the connection to my phone despite sweating, shoveling, riding and high heat.

The sound quality is fine for my needs. I listen to mostly audiobooks and some classical music while out with the horses. I can clearly hear the violins vs a harp or French horn without distortion. The only real complaint is when I get a call. I can hear the caller clearly, but they say I sound like I'm in a tin can.

review_title: Fine craftsmanship, high quality materials. Really good sound quality and comfortable
review_text:
I'm not an audiophile by any means, but I do appreciate excellent quality recreation of certain types of music and full cast production audiobooks. I don't like earbuds for more than a few minutes at a time for a number of reasons so I try to always have a good set of wireless headphones around. My older Sonys are very good, but beginning to show their age after three years of regular, reasonably hard use. I think these will serve nicely as replacements.

The form factor here is just as nice as the actual function and that's not always the case with high dollar electronics. The materials are very nice and put together flawlessly - the entire unit is really gorgeous. These are actually quite heavy in the hand, yet balanced so perfectly that I don't notice the weight at all wearing them. The ear pieces are attached with magnets to the arch piece of you can remove them for cleaning or swaps in the future. The lambskin is very soft and doesn't cause excess heat build up for my ears.

Pairings with my Sony Xperia phone, my Samsung tablet and a Fire tablet were all easy and painless. I've used these headphones for streaming music via Amazon, Pandora and my own stuff from my cloud files plus Audible books for a couple of weeks now. I'm currently using them on vacation right now with the included travel case - they fold up a bit and the charging cable & 3mm direct connect cable fit in the case as well. Sound quality is excellent as well here for my types of music - primarily classical, country, and 80s pop. I can clearly hear the French horns, flute, or soft cellos in Hans Zimmer compositions or a Beethoven concerto. Aretha Franklin sounds great with these BTW. (I can't speak to thumping bass reproduction because I detest that style and don't listen to it.)

I do appreciate the full integration of the Fire Stick with my other devices through our Amazon account - I can pick up a show on Prime with my tablet, phone or tv exactly where I left off. Regardless of which streaming stick we use, we're still incredibly happy we dumped the cable.

For my needs this will work fine though.

review_title: Easy to install, much prettier picture than with cable. Cutting the cord is totally worth it
review_text:
After three price increases in two years from Suddenlink, we said Enough and cut the cord to streaming only. We had two Fire Sticks already, but needed something for the living room television. I picked up the Roku Express plus at a local store and in less than five minutes had it connected and working. So very easy.

I'm amazed at how much we've been missing by being tethered to cable! There's just a plethora of free tv and movies out there. The Roku essentially just gathers a ton of the options and puts them in one spot for you. You do have to activate most the big time channels through a paid service like DirectTV Now - TBS, NBC, Bravo, AMC, A&E etc. All require an activation and verification to watch vua the apps.

The remote is small, but feels sturdy and is simple to use. No getting lost in a jillion random buttons. My only complaint is the need for a second remote control for volume. We use sound bars for the 55 and 65" TV's and the Roku remote isn't set up for volume. Not a deal breaker by any means, just make sure you have another way to control volume. We're using the DirectTV Now cheapest option and the HULU LIVE beta for the first two months and then we'll keep the one that has been used most and drop the other. One thing I noticed immediately is with Roku (and the Fire Sticks) the 1080p picture on our big Samsung is much cleaner and prettier than when we had the cable service - we've used only the HDMI connection for years. I'm extremely pleased that we finally made the leap to streaming.

review_title: Works with Suddenlink perfectly. Increased signal stability and speeds
review_text:
We have Suddenlink cable, internet, and land line phone service and had been happy with our three year old router and their modem. Until we moved to a new house. The arris modem was dropping signal significantly every single day - we either had super slow or no connection for hours. I had the cable guys out here four times in 61 days to fix the problem. I was literally ready to just cancel Suddenlink and move to AT&T for internet, but decided to try this Nighthawk combo first.

It was spotted instantly by Suddenlink when I called to give them the new modem Mac address, so the connection was just a single phone call to start. No drama. I have 9 daily devices on WiFi and three TiVo receivers that connect via Ethernet or WiFi plus the land line phone. There's four Ethernet connections and two phone connections on the modem, plenty for our needs.

It's been almost three weeks and I've noticed an astonishing improvement in our initial connection and reliability. Rather than daily outages, we have had five total in three weeks and none lasted more than 15 to 20 minutes. Stability of the signal has improved and our speeds are double what they were with the arris modem - we're actually getting the high speed service we pay for. The router is also projecting the WiFi far enough that I no longer need to use a secondary extender to get WiFi by the pool and patio.

I like the Genie app with this. The ability to check channels, reboot the router if needed, and see which devices are online is very handy. I also like the clear, bright lights on the front. review_title: Beautiful picture, tiny eye for the remote control to aim at, works with Denon sound bar & wifi
review_text:
I bought this television (I double checked the exact model number to be positive that t I am reviewing the correct one) used at an estate sale in January and it's been used daily in our master bedroom every since. The color and clarity of the picture is simply wonderful. In comparison to our brand new Sceptre 55" 1080p tv in the living room and the 3 year old Samsung in the guest room, this Vizio has the prettiest picture and best refresh rate. The Samsung has the best native sound though without a sound bar enhancement.

This Vizio is our only Smart Television and I have a Firestick on the living room tv. As of today, June 16, 2016, the Amazon app and others are all working just fine through the television's remote control with the direct access buttons. Connecting this tv to our wifi network did take several attempts and I had to update the firmware twice before it would connect and hold the connection for more than 48 hours. (To be honest, I have no idea if the former owner every actually used the internet connection so it may not have been updated before I got it) Since January, I have had no trouble with the connection or streaming. We do have a super fast internet service and a dual band router with this tv as the only thing typically streaming on one band.

My one star deduction is the tiny receiver area for the remote control. If you are using the actual remote rather than a universal one for the cable box, you have to aim directly at the very tiny eye in the far left bottom corner and it can take a couple of tries to hit it just right from across a big room. This drives me nuts when I'm streaming from Amazon Prime and need to pause the show quickly or try to flick through the selections. However, I would totally buy another Vizio tv again in the future if the new ones are as good as this two year old used one has been - I've definitely gotten my hundred fifty dollars worth out of this one.

Overall, however, this is a very good keyboard cover and works perfectly with the older MacBook Air. Solid 5 stars.

review_text:
I own several pairs of earbuds. I just seem to accumulate them like I do my reading glasses -- several pairs in each room where I tend to use them. Most of mine are in the price range $20-30, so those are the ones I'm using for comparison. Based on that, these new Pioneer earbuds seem to be the best of that group.

I listen mostly to classical music with a smattering of other genres (folk, 1960s-70s rock, Broadway). These provided acceptable performance for all genres, but do seem to lack some low-end bass response. One of my test recordings is the Erich Kunzel/Cincinnati Symphony recording of Tchaikovsky's "1812 Overture" with cannons, and the low-end loss was noticeable. Still, the rest of the sound is excellent, and these will work just fine for my day-to-day listening -- music that I have going on in the background while working on something else. For serious listening, I'll use my over-the-ear headphones.

Good performance for the price. I like these.

review_title: Perfect for on-the-go journaling/blogging ... lightweight and portable, it travels well!
review_text:
I purchased this to take along on vacations so I could journal (and ultimately blog) about my journeys. The first test was just completed: a 2-week cruise around Alaska (Ketchikan, Endicott Arm, Juneau, Hoonah, Anchorage, Kodiak, Homer, and Sitka). I wanted a full-sized keyboard, portable, and easy to manage that would work with my iPad Pro.

I chose this for the size, the fact that it is powered via my iPad (rather than needing to be charged), and the fact that it's a wired connection via the lightning cable rather than Bluetooth. Nothing against Bluetooth, but not having to deal with pairing simplifies things a lot.

This performed beautifully! Connected easily, and no problems at all with performance. It has some nifty shortcuts, many I didn't use, but at least they're available. Despite being a full-size keyboard, the small size means I can tuck this into my carryon along with other necessities and it doesn't take up much space at all. It's durable, too -- the wire connector appears to be sturdy. I used this a couple of times per day to record events and activities, so it was in and out of my bag often. No problems at all.

It's coming along on my next adventure: a cruise around the North Atlantic (including Greenland, Iceland, and Norway) for 6 weeks.
