Overall, this is a solid 5-star item. Would happily purchase again if the need arises.

review_title: Small, but does what I need it to do ...
review_text:
Since my MacBook Air has only 2 USB ports, and I have a bunch of external devices and gizmos that need to talk to the Mac via USB, I set out looking for something that would allow me to attach multiple USB-connectable devices at the same time. One of the 2 MacBook Air USB ports is dedicated to my 1TB external hard drive, but I also have a wireless mouse, a 25-key midi keyboard that I use for composing music, and a few other things that I may not use every day, but that I want to be able to use without having to disconnect my mouse.

Saw this, read the reviews, and decided to give it a try. So far, we've been working together comfortably for just over a week with no hiccups or mishaps. I like the small size -- it's small and relatively "flat," so it stays tucked just behind my laptop on my desk without occupying too much real estate. I like that.

I have the wireless mouse "receiver" plugged into the end, my midi keyboard plugged into the first of the 3 slots on the side, and I can add anything else (iPhone for syncing, etc.) in one of the other two slots. This summer, I'll be using it with a USB-driven personal fan when the weather warms up (no air conditioning here in the Pacific NW). I did test all 4 ports, and they are all working just fine.

Very happy with it so far. If I start noticing any issues, I'll update this review.

review_title: Great sound in a little package ....
review_text:
I did a LOT of research before purchasing this little speaker. My needs were pretty simple: I wanted a wireless speaker that could connect with either my iPhone or iPad to use on the nightstand. I like to play music before I go to sleep, so it needed to be small, but have great sound.

Based on the reviews here, I finally decided on this one, and I'm happy to say it's PERFECT!

It charged quickly connected to my MacBook Pro -- about 2 hrs, maybe a little less. Turned it on, turned on the iPhone, went to the "Settings" on the phone, found Bluetooth, and there was the JAM XT. Selected it, and voila! they paired. Entire set-up took about 10 seconds.

I listen to a lot of classical music, so my first "test" was the Brahms "A German Requiem" -- lots of highs, lows, soft, loud, etc. Strings, voices, woodwinds, brass -- it's all in there. I listened carefully for distortion -- everything was set on "medium" volume -- and I'm happy to say I heard NO distortion at all. Everything sounded great -- nearly as good as my Bose system, but without the bass resonance.

OK, so I haven't had this very long (about a week), so its durability remains to be seen. But I'm impressed with the quality and style of this. If I notice any issues, I'll update this review.

Meanwhile, I can now fall asleep to great sounding music from a small-footprint speaker. And that's exactly what I wanted.

I bought my pair of Bluez 2S directly from AfterShokz company, and not via Amazon. Just like with so many things there are aspects to like and aspects to not like.

I will start with the negatives. If you are in a noisy environment, such as working out in an exercise room, the volume just is not loud enough or satisfactory at all. You need earplugs in the ears to get the satisfactory volume. Yes, earplugs. Of course, that defeats the whole purpose of buying headphones that do not go inside or cover your ears.

You can test this out by simply putting a finger in each ear and then you'll hear the remarkable level of volume change.

Because of the lack of loudness one can achieve in a noisy environment, I cannot recommend these (unless you want to buy earplugs and wear them at the same time).

The only other negative for me personally is the lack of a way to go back to a previous song, or repeat the currently playing song. (You can skip forward to the next song, but you cannot go back.)

The positives: These are comfortable to wear and very lightweight. The Bluez 2S offers the ability for decent call quality when using them to make calls. Microphones seem good (I have only tried this indoors, and not outdoors, so I cannot comment further on this particular subject.)

The Bluez 2S are very easy to operate.

In a quiet environment, volume is fine, and music quality is acceptable for this price point. (Of course you will not get the level of music quality or bass you'd get with a more expensive name brand headphones that go directly over the ear.)

So, for specific purposes such as cell phone calls where you want to keep both ears free, these are quite good indeed, offering good voice quality for both parties. (Pairing with my iPhone 5 and 6S went flawlessly.)

review_title: For My Specific Needs This Computer Is Perfect
review_text:
For specific circumstances, this Asus VivoMini UN62-M037M is perfect and wonderful. My specific circumstance: I wanted a computer to put next to my High-Def TV so I can play movies and TV shows, etc. My TV becomes the gorgeous computer monitor via the HDMI input. I have Ethernet right there, so I did not have to buy the additional WiFi adapter for the computer. I use a wireless keyboard and mouse.

This Asus has 4 USB 3.0 ports. I recommend this Asus model with the 4 ports instead of their model with only 2 ports.

I bought one 8-Gig RAM stick for $44 (Crucial CT102464BF160B via Amazon). I bought a 256GB mSATA drive for $103 (Crucial MX200 via Amazon). (I already had a wireless mouse [Logitech M525] and a wireless keyboard [Anker A7723].)

So, I spent about $435 total. (Luckily I already had a copy of Windows 8.1 I could use, plus a USB DVD drive. Of course, you can also install Windows via a USB Flash Drive.)

Opening up the bottom by removing the 4 screws is fast and easy. Installing the RAM and mSATA hard drive is also fast and easy.

I hooked up my HDMI cable direct from the computer to my TV and the rest went easy.

The Windows drivers are easily downloaded from Asus Website.

The computer is very quiet and small and nice. The i5 processor runs as expected. Boot times are fast. The Intel Video chip they provide is great at doing what I need it to: Provide a crystal clear picture to my TV, and allow me to stream high-def movies and TV shows from the computer.

For what I do and at the total price I paid, this Asus VivoMini is perfect. (With it seeming solidly built, I am hoping for longevity.)

review_title: I could hear no discernible difference in sound quality
review_text:
I use a $100 external sound card when DJ'ing because I want better sound than what the built-in laptop sound card offers. I notice a big difference.

I then was doing more research and read how the makers of these way more expensive USB cables claim they offer superior sound. So, I took the plunge and spent $50 for this Pangea Audio solid silver USB cable.

I seriously could not hear any difference between this USB cable and the $10 short USB cable I was using. For $50, I expected a perceptible difference, even if it was just a small difference.

I had others also judge...and they agreed with me.

From looking at and holding the cable, it does indeed come across as a quality cable. But again, I heard no difference in the sound...and I tested it with different genres of songs.

I would not recommend this cable. If you indeed have a great (and expensive) external sound card or a great DAC, my guess is you do not need to buy one of these $50 (or even more expensive) USB cables.

I give the cable 5 stars for build quality and 1 star for its inability to cause the sound from your laptop to either an external sound card or DAC to be noticeably improved. (So, I averaged it out to 3 stars.)

(I have not tested the much more expensive than this one USB cables, so maybe those do produce a perceptible difference?)

review_text:
This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. WD has gone to a lot of effort to make this drive world class.
Except for that little 12 inch USB 3.0 cable. Get yourself an extension cable and this drive is the Cadillac of external drives. The included software is icing on the cake for you to choose how sweet you will make your drive.

review_title: Nice earbuds but I decided swapped them out for Bose QuietComfort earbuds
review_text:
I went on the search for a set of ear buds that would stay in my ears better than my Airpod Pros but with the same level of Noise cancellation. It seemed like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and Bose Quietcomfort earbuds were the top picks in this space. After a lot of research i went with the Sony earbuds. Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation.

The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did.

After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great.

Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.

Bottom line - you get what you pay for.

review_text:
OK, take 2. My original review of this product got hijacked somehow. After writing it, I checked back a couple hours later and my screen name and original title were there, but my review got replaced with what seemed like some guy's journal entry. It had absoluterly nothing to do with this or any other product. Strange.

Anyway - as mentioned in my original posting, this review is more a condemnation or earbud headphones in general than the Sennheiser CX300-B, which I decided to try after my "over ear" style Sony noise canceling headphones went on the fritz. My past experience with earbuds was not good, although I had only ever tried the type that come with the iPod and not the "ear plug" type that go in the ear canal, like the Sennheiser CX300-B. However, having owned a pair of Sennheiser over the ear headphones back in the 70's, my impression of the company and their products was good. So, I decided to take the plunge. What a mistake.

After opening the package (no easy feat - damn sound welded plastic clamshells!), I popped on the medium-sized bud covers (appropriate for my size ears) and inserted them into my ears. I turned on my mp3 player and listened for a few minutes. The sound was adequate - nothing spectacular. I did notice they had decent bass and did block some external noise. I kept listening as I stepped outside to go to the store. I couldn't believe what I heard. Every step I took was amplified in my head - like a booming bass drum. Even the gentle bumping of the cord against my chest was amplified - a constant thump, thump, thump that was impossible to ignore. As it turns out, the very feature that blocks a modicum of external noise, also amplifies any sound that travels through the body. Even breathing is amplified! As I walked, it sounded as though I was listening to someone breathe over a PA system! I had hoped to use these while running, but there's no way that's going to happen. In fact, the problem with amplified sound is so bad, I won't use them at all.

I am very disappointed in this product and will never buy any ear plug style headphones again. I don't understand why anyone would sell them, let alone use them. They may have great sound reproduction, but the listening experience is totally ruined by the sounds that get amplified through the body. It amazes me that people buy similar style products that sell for hundreds of dollars. The only way you can enjoy the sound they produce is to sit perfectly still. I'm glad I only paid about $16 for these things. I won't return them because it'll be too much of a hassle - probably cost more to ship them back than I paid.

BTW - The photo of the product is misleading. The cord looks thicker than it actually is and there's no way it can be coiled as is shown in the photo. It gives the impression the cord is more supple and flexible that it really is. Also, one end of the cord is longer than the other. Not sure why this is, but the thinness of the cord makes it prone to kinking and tangling. In fact, since one side of the cord is longer than the other, it makes it even more prone to tangling.

Bottom line - steer clear of the Sennheiser CX300-B and all ear plug style earbuds.

review_title: When Power Goes Off, Firmware gets Corrupted, and Router will not work
review_text:
When the router is working ,it's awesome. Range, speed, and setup are very easy. However, just like a bad musical performance, when things don't perform well, that's what people remember.

Here is why I cannot' give the product 5 stars.

There have been two situations where the router lost power and the firmware got corrupted and I had to reflash the router to make it work. I have NEVER had a device EVER get corrupted firmware. What a JOKE! Probably corrupted data issue as nothing will bring a system down like bad data.

Google: Router Power LED Blinks Slowly and Router No Longer Works

So rather than issue a RECALL on the defective merchandise, they do the next worst thing possible and give you some funky software called TFTP to download and fool around with to get the router re-flashed. Well, I thought the re-flash would correct the corrupted firmware. I got news for them, IT DIDN'T. I was moving my Router yesterday while the cable guy was here and then when we tried to hook everything back up, I got the blinking light of death again. I knew it was going to be a hassle to get the firmware downloaded and reflashed, so I switched back to an older working router for the time being.

In my opinion, NETGEAR should have done a 2 things amongst other things...

1) As an interim solution, Made special re-flash software that made upgrades a breeze. A one click solution to read the router's make/model MAC address and current firmware, and auto-magically download the new one and install it while PRESERVING all existing settings. It should also remember the OLD mac address and use it when you were migrating the settings to a router with a new MAC address. If their software engineering department can't do that, they need to be replaced starting with the Manager.

review_title: easy set up, easy to add pics, has a lot of neat options, overall quite pleased.
review_text:
Frame is a tad slow to respond to the remote; that could be better. It isnt always slow, just sometimes it doesnt pic up, other times it is fast & perfectly fine. I think it has to do with distance from frame. Dont be too close!

They have a large frame with touchscreen available, so I would personally go with that unless price dictates otherwise. I like the remote too, just wish it responded faster and more consistently. I wouldn't want just a touchscreen. Option for either/both in one would be cool. Anyway.. I like this. It is my first frame. I have been kind of using our Echo Show, and sometimes just a computer screen. But I have wanted a basic frame, so here I am.

Basically plug it in, get it on the network, get the app, make an account, pair with phone, then select pics off phone to be loaded. Can choose up to 50 at a time. Very easy. Surprisingly so. I am tech savvy but impatient. This was pretty easy to figure out. Takes a few minutes to get them loaded.

Picture quality is quite good, and occasionally looks off. Thought that might be original source rather than the frame. All considered, all pics are quite clear and detailed.

if you have it set to full screen, then some pics may be cut off. If you have it set to the other option (cant remember the term), then the pics come up as you took them. Glad I figured this out because at first I had some that were cut off and it made me sad. Got it fixed very easily and all is well. YAY

Can set up calendar, weather, location, an alarm, play music, load videos. Can set time and make it a clock, can choose clock face. Can choose 12 hr or 24 hr format. Can create slide shows, decide on length of time, random or sequential or based on when taken. Very cool. Oh, and even incorporate music. Can label/add words/text too. Easy on, easy off.

Can operate basic stuff directly from the frame. Including very quickly rotating a pic. No need to use remote for everything!

Has headphone jack on back

It really isnt bad as an entry level frame. Would be nice as a gift if preloaded for someone. Now that I have been using this, I know what to look for in an upgrade. But this will certainly make do as i get to know it more and more. Ive only been playing with it for a day or so. The more I write about it, the more I like it.

I think pics can be emailed to this like Skylight subscription frame. Can let other people add photos.

Can also add photos/music/video via a SD/MC/SDHC, USB, USB mini, or thumb drive.

Needs to be plugged into wall receptacle.

Says in one of the product pictures that it can be wall mounted . I dont see how. It is a landscape mode item with a back portion to help it sit upright. It would not ever be flush with wall. I wouldnt buy it for that anyway. I got it for use on a side table so I can see pics of my dogs and cats all day long.

review_title: worth the try, gorgeous clear display, ease of use, fits my 7" wrist,
review_text:
It's pretty good, especially if you dont need a name brand. It has a beautifully clear display. Easy to install app and pairs well with no hassle. Has all the bells and whistles of name brand products. While I prefer fitbit due to familiarity.

I havent put it entirely through its paces. I noticed that it was registering nearly same heart rate as my fitbit sense. I havent it worn it long enough to determine blood oxygen. There is still a lot to learn. The learning curve feels a little clunky compared to my fitbit.

Has ability to connect to Alexa, take and make calls, music. Can make changes through app or scroll through the screen face.

The watch band fits my 7" wrist and feels comfortable enough. Typical silicone band. It is attached via pins, so I imagine it is possible to swap it out but not sure. I may try some old bands to see if it is doable. I'd also prefer for it to have a soft protective cover (bumper guard) to protect screen and edges.

I still prefer the ease of using a name brand, but this has a good looking interface. Main thing is to see how accurate it is. I think it has been fine for heart rate, steps, but will need more sleep time for seeing how well it tracks sleep and oxygen.

I dont rate on price, but I comment. This is pretty reasonable, but it looks like there are many similar products for less. So compared to a name brand of similar features this is a bargain. Compared to other no name generics, this is competitive. Some are easily $20 less. I noticed the price on this vacillates. I think I got it for $70, and have seen it as low as 35-40.

review_title: trusted brand, always holds up, lightweight hard cover, folds back, attractive, comfy in hand
review_text:
Great case. I have been buying Moko products since my first Kindle some 10 years ago. The cases last longer than the Kindle does, haha. I get the same style and same design-- I like what I like, and so when it came to choosing another case for my new Kindle Paperwhite Signature edition, I simply went with Moko again. Design and colors hold up too!

I noticed they [[ASIN:B09HCFFP63 have a listing for half the price]]. I wasn't immediately aware of the difference between that one and this one. It took a little poking around to determine that this is a hard cover (like all my others) and the other is more of a firm soft cover. I think either would be fine, but I really just wanted to go with what was familiar to me. I mention this in case you are also noticing the 2 products and are curious of the difference. I noticed one review over on the other page saying that the quality was different and they were disappointed. But what I concluded is that they were used to THIS product, and bought THAT product. It is two different products! Nothing changed! This is a hard cover and that is a soft cover. If all you do is keep your kindle at the bedside, then the other is just fine as a dust cover and added grip. If you tend to travel with your Kindle or are more likely to drop it or bump it, then the hard cover such as this is great.

It isnt heavy. The cover folds back. Adds just enough additional grip to feel much better than a plain/naked kindle.

Just pop the kindle into the cradle, and then that's it.

I do not have a wireless charger, but this is supposed to work with it without need to pop the kindle out. I trust Moko and will assume that is true if I ever get one.

review_title: ultra comfy, the most comfortable of any band I have ever used in 8 years of fitbit use
review_text:
Been wearing mine for a couple of weeks now, and I am very pleased. I only take it off to charge and to shower. Just a good fit and feel. I can customize how snug or loose I want it with ease. Very happy!

Two reasons that led me to ordering new Fitbit Sense bands:
1. I usually use the silicone bands, but the last set I bought weren't quite long enough leaving me fearful that I would lose my pricy smart watch. So I wanted a band that felt secure.
2. My last set of bands didn't have holes that made for a perfect fit. Always seemed like it was too loose feeling or too tight. It was irritating. I hoped to find a new band that offered a better fit.

As one with sensory issues, having a good fit is important. I don't care for elastic style bands (they stretch out, feel sloppy), but I began sniffing around them thinking that it would at least feel more comfortable over what I had been using. But then I stumbled upon these "Bcuckood Nylon Loop" wristbands. I saw that they arent stretchy (yay!) but that they do have a velcro closure. I was intrigued! I figured that would give me the option for a custom fit, that I can loosen or tighten with ease.. so I went ahead and ordered them.

Also chose them because they say they fit wrist sizes 6.3" to 8.7". My wrists are exactly 7", but all the wrist bands that only mention it fitting up into the 6-7.5" wrists aren't long enough when you consider that the band needs to overlap in order to be securely on (as well as fit over width of hand & thumb). I figured this was a winner when I saw 8.7"

These are GREAT. Very happy. Love the colors. Easy on, and for the most part, easy off. I have wide pals, so sliding this off means that I am really loosing it up to do so, but I have gotten used to it and it isnt weird.

The velcro are neat. They are in little disks. Really grabs the material securely. I really like how secure this band feels. I love the best off all how I dont feel like I am wearing a watch. This band makes my wrist feel free.

So far, no stink. But Ive only been wearing it a couple of weeks during the winter. So not much sweat to consider, and frankly I havent been engaging in sweaty exercise.

review_title: versatile velcro, cut to preference, hook on one side, soft latch on other, self gripping
review_text:
What can I say, it is legit brand name Velcro! One of my must have items alongside duct tape, twine, cable ties and the such. This is hook on one side, latch (soft) on the other. Slender. You have likely seen this attached to cables and cords on devices for cable management. Think of it as a soft cable tie, but instead of a fed locking mechanism, the "hook and latch" do their thing. Press and go. Makes for easy peasy cheap curtain tie backs.

Keep in mind that this is one long single strip of velcro. 45' of velcro. 3/5" width. It is double sided. Meant for self gripping. Other styles include non adhesive two separate strips, or two separate strips with adhesive. This is hook on one side, soft latch on the other. Simply bundle something up, then wrap this around. The overlap of one wide to another will lock it in place.

Useful as a means to attach things to hiking bags (when dont need, want a D-ring), or in something that goes around wrist or waist.

review_title: decent power bank, charges quickly, charges phone in good time, terrible solar
review_text:
Works fine as a power bank, just make sure you check your device as I often found it not charging. I had to wiggle the cord, or plug and unplug. Really annoying. Maybe it was my cord. Anyway, powered up my GooglePixel 6 from 54% to 81% in a reasonable amount of time. I didnt time it, but it wasnt as fast a typical quick charge, but it wasn't slow either. It was enough to make me feel comfortable to rely on this as needed. (4 stars)

Flashlight works (low beam, high beam, flash) . Not a super impressive light, something akin to flashlight feature on phone. (3.5 - 4 stars). Works in a pinch, like seeing it as an addition to the power bank.

Solar panel? eh, not enough to say it is worth it. Too weak. It never picked up any power even set in a sunny window. Next time I will try it outside and hope for enough sun. I want it to at least charge this up enough to be useful, otherwise, why pay for this feature? (1-2 stars)

Overall? eh, wish it worked better. Wish I wasn't influenced by a youtuber to pick one of these up. I did shop around a little, and nothing stood out as better, and the prices were all about the same. I'm going with 3 stars, it's "OK".

review_title: petite, light, digital display, front controls, remote w/ batteries, plug n play
review_text:
I'm very happy with this blu ray player. I was so pleased with an Arufuna DVD player, that when it came time to look for a BluRay player, I was very open to trying it from this brand again. I already have a huge, heavy blu-ray player, and I wanted something smaller, lighter, and easier to move around. The small size of this is perfect. I dont often watch DVDs or Blu-ray discs, but I want the option. We have a few smart tvs, and our main already has an old Blu-ray player, but I wanted something for our other tvs. I put a DVD player (by arufuna) in my spare room, and am using this in our smaller den. Now I feel like I can grab a DVD off the shelf and not have to always stream something.

10.2" x 7.7" x 1.3"

review_title: vertical laptop sleeve w/ option to carry it like a back pack. Attractive, functional.
review_text:
I see this as a vertical laptop sleeve with the option to carry it like a back pack.

I like that the back pack straps tuck away so flatly and completely that it looks like a sleeve and doesn't look or feel clunky. You won't notice the straps until you decide to use them. There is also a strap for sliding over luggage handle.

It fits my 14" laptop with a little room left over. When kept as a sleeve (and not opened into the bigger bag option), I can tuck my mouse and charging cord in with the lap top.

The interior is soft and padded and is about what I expect from a sleeve, maybe even more secure. No issues.

There are two front zipper pockets while it is in the sleeve configuration.

An option to unzip a compartment that makes it into a bigger bag (or backpack) then provides even more space and storage options. Including two mesh side pockets for water bottles or whatever. Additional storage isn't significant, but it is functional. Can easily be used as a day bag (pack some snacks, and few other essentials), maybe pushing it as an overnight bag (unless super minimalist), but it is definitely great as a sleeve that can be opened up to carry more treasures. Doubt I would have used this as my high school or college pack pack because I usually carried a lot, and I dont think this will carry much more than a book or two. It simply isn't a traditional back pack, but I dont think you would be looking at this if that is what you were after.

The material has a smooth canvas feel. Very clean lines. Minimalist look. I have this in wine red, and it a great color.

I like it, and it is much nicer, sturdier, and attractive than I expected.

Unless it falls apart on me soon, I see no reason not to give it full rating. If I experience anything else, I will be back to update.

"Slim & Expandable Design: Slim style for light travel and commute, 200% Expandability when more belongings and easily to switch between the both."

review_title: good little budget friendly MP3 player, no issues
review_text:
I bought this simply to play music, primarily mp3. I don't use any of the other functions, but it has several such as e-reader, FM radio, pictures, video, alarm, pedometer. Lots of extras if you like that sort of thing.

I just load it up with music from my computer, then either listen to music through a set of wired headphones, or I connect to a bluetooth speaker, or my main reason.. listening through speakers in my truck. It's an old truck with no current technology. I use one of those cassette adapters to play this music. Or when I borrow my husbands newer car, I use the bluetooth or more often, use an auxillary cord to connect. I never intentionally listed to it through the built in speaker. I like that there is that option despite not making use of it.

Since I use it primarily while driving, I needed to be able to get to the music without having to look at the screen or buttons. The only MP3 player I ever really loved was the old ipod classic circa 2005- so easy to navigate. I have yet to find anything quite like that, but at least this RUIZU Mp3 player is easy enough to navigate, so that makes me happy. It takes a little getting used to though.

For my driving experience, I have a made a couple of folders of music. Occasionally I just let the mp3 player shuffle everything I own. I have no idea if it skips a lot of music. It does seem to like to bring up a few of the same songs frequently. Overall I don't care.. I just want music playing.

This is my second Ruizu. First one of a different model lasted a year, then it began to not play right, or at all. So when it came time to buy another MP3 player, I looked at so many-- then circled back around to Ruizu since I was already familiar with it. The price makes it worth trying. I am pleased with this one so far. I have been using it for a few months now, no issues. Battery life is good- I don't need to charge it too often. It is providing me with music when I want it, and that is all I really need it for. If I learn anything new, or experience anything worth sharing, I will be back to do so.

review_title: slim profile, smooth tracking, plug & play connection, can charge & use at same time
review_text:
Slick, small. The main aspect that I like about this is not having to change the batteries. It seems to hold a charge for quite some time (I have been using it nightly for a couple of weeks straight out from box; have yet to actually charge it). I use it entirely with my lap top because I can't stand using the touch pad. So I always use a corded mouse or a cordless mouse. Usually the batteries last a good while, but it is extra nice to not even have to worry about them. When it comes time to charge I can still use it AND charge it by using the USB charging cable.

When not in use, the dongle is stored on bottom of mouse. It has a little magnetic port that it slides into.

Overall, it works perfectly fine. Smooth-- I use a colorful mouse pad most of the time, but sometimes solid black.
Can change DPI, so that will make a difference in smoothness and tracking. "Featuring 5 adjustable DPI (2400/2000/1600/1200/800)"

What I don't care for, and this is entirely a personal preference, is that it is very sleek and flat. I am used to a beefier mouse-- both a cordless for my lap top as well as a corded for my desktop. I am used to that hump in the middle, and this is rather flat. I don't have huge hands, but I have wide hands. So for short term use it is fine. For longer term use, it could be tiring on the hand. Since I use it with my laptop, and I usually only use it for a little while before bed to check out the internet or play a silly game, it is ok. But for more intensive activities, especially gaming- I need a mouse that fits MY hand better.

I do like it though for my short term use. Again, I really like that it is a rechargeable mouse. That is the selling point for me. So if you are ok with a slim profile mouse, this should be just fine for your needs. If you are used to a beefier mouse with that hump in the middle, you may not care for this for long term use.

review_title: good price, nice bundle size, works exactly as I need them too
review_text:
You know you are an adult when you get excited to add a big bag of zip ties to your home tool box. I have an assortment of zip ties in various sizes for various tasks. If you didn't know, it is better to go a little larger than what you think you need as the length indicated is entire length and not just working length. I just so happened to have had a need for the smaller size (6" or less) zip ties to secure some corners on a multi tier wire crate. I ratcheted them tight and trimmed off the excess. In all, I used about two dozen immediately. With a pack of 500 I should be set for awhile. Always better to have too many of these than not enough. I'll be using them for sure to secure snow netting. Not on the posts (need 10-12" ties for that), but to hold together the overlap going from one roll or piece to the next. Since a section of netting always gets blown apart at some point during the winter, I just head out with a handful of zip ties and put it back together again. So yeh, 500 seems like a lot, but when you have them you need a bunch of them.

The 6 inch size is also great for wire management in general, and just about any small sized securing needs.

No complaints. Happy to have them!

review_title: awkward design, hard to get used to, finding it irritating to use
review_text:
So, I have this backpack, and it is kinda weird. You have to see my pictures as it is a different style than what is pictured in the description. I don't really care for it as it is awkward to handle.

--It is a basic looking back pack. I like the bright orange in contrast to the black. That is likely the only feature I really like.
--The bag is deep. It measures roughly 21" long, this includes the top portion being unfolded, as that is usable space if need be. @17" wide
--The access to the main compartment is a velcro closure with adjustable hook straps for added security (and to keep added length folded down). Unlike many backpacks, there is just one slit opening across the top with velcro to close. Most backpacks have a zipper closure, as well as going a bit down the sides, for ease of access. I'm not fond of how my bag is styled in that way.
--Inside the great nylon cavern of the main compartment, it splits into several more compartments and pockets, including a lightly padded pocket.
--exterior pockets included two open side pockets that would be great to stick a water bottle in or an umbrella.
--two good sized compartments on the front- one zippered, one velcro flap closure.
--one rear zip pocket, as well as what appears to be a pass through strap of material- perhaps for use on a luggage handle?
--padded shoulder straps are comfortable. Straps include d-rings for clipping keys, or whatever to.
--overall feel is good

review_title: A very nifty back-up solution, but you'll need some items on hand before you can use it...
review_text:
THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. review_title: If you're a Frontier customer, or any other service for that matter, my review should help...
review_text:
I've been trying to get good coverage in my garage so the security cams and smart devices don't get dropped connections, or long wait times when I try to connect from my app. This is finally the one! Frontier uses and all in one gateway, Arris NVG468MQ. In order to use the Netgear as the main router, I would need Frontier's help to put the Arris in bridge mode. I'm not sure if they can even do this, and since I purchased my own Arris to save rental fees, I wasn't sure how much they'd be willing to help either. So I didn't bother to try, instead, I set up the Netgear router in AP mode. To do this...

1. Go to Frontier's admin to turn off all wi-fi modes. Turn off both 2.4 and 5.0 modes.
2. Connect ethernet cable from the WAN port of the Netgear Router, to any available lan port of your Frontier gateway. Turn it on.
3. Using your smartphone or PC, connect to the Netgear wifi using the credentials labeled on the Netgear Router.
4. That's it. You should be online with the new wi-fi, but you'll want to change some things such as the orbi's admin password, your SSID's, etc. When you launch a browser under this new wi-fi, Netgear's admin should pop up allowing you to login to change your credentials, if it doesn't, then use routerlogin.net or orbilogin.net.
5. Since you've disabled Frontier's wifi, all your connected devices at home no longer works. But if you change your orbi's SSID to the same SSID that you were using, all your devices will work again. Keep in the mind, the Orbi system allows 4 different SSIDs. So you can still create other networks with different security levels.
6. Place the Orbi Satellite where you need better coverage. Power it on. Go back to Orbi Router and hit the sync button, within 30 seconds, you need to go back to the satellite and hit the sync button as well. Once they sync, which is indicated by solid blue for a few minutes, all lights will then be turned off. So keep that in mind, when it's up and running, there are no lights on the orbi router, or orbi satellite. I'm used to seeing some sort of lights on router equipment, so when there wasn't any lights, I was wondering if it was working properly. As it turns out, all lights are turned off when everything is up and running properly.

Even if you're not Frontier, the process I laid out above, to connect the Orbi in AP mode, should be similar. Hope this has been helpful! This is 5-Stars all the way!

review_title: Frontier customers, this is plug and play...
review_text:
I did not get mine on Amazon, so this is not a verified review. I got mine on a famous auction site, but I'm hear to assure you this is plug and play. I was confused by the product photo saying you need a MEB1100. Basically, if you're a current Frontier customer, and you don't have and don't know anything about the MEB1100, and everything has been working fine in your house with just the Arris, then don't worry about the MEB1100. However, if Frontier set you up with both the Arris and the MEB1100, then I recommend buying both. You want the set-up to stay the same.

I do use moca adapters to bring internet to rooms with coax cable. These are the ones I use: https://www.amazon.com/Motorola-Adapter-Ethernet-2-Pack-MM1002/dp/B078HMDDVS/ref=sr_1_2?dchild=1&keywords=Motorola+moca&qid=1617140900&sr=8-2 With the Arris router, you do not need to put an adapter next to it. My connection is like this:

* Ethernet from ONT in my garage goes to WAN port of the Arris router in living room.
* Coaxial from ONT goes to a 4 way splitter, one line goes to the living room, I connect this line to the coaxial on the Arris.
* Coaxial line in my bedroom goes to the network coaxial port of my moca adapter. I then hook up an ethernet hub to the ethernet port of the moca adapter. Voila! That's how I bring ethernet to my bedroom.
* I do the same to the other coaxial lines in my home to bring ethernet hubs to those rooms as well.

This has been how my home has functioned. All connections were left untouched. I simply swapped out the Frontier Arris for this identical Arris. I then made sure to go into the new Arris admin and create the same wifi SSID with the same password as before. All your wifi and network devices will function as normal, no need to re-enter any passwords. I contacted Frontier, and they are sending me a box with pre-paid envelope to ship back their router, and I was assured I will no longer be charged with rental fees. I'm happy to report every customer rep I've talked to have been very nice and accommodating. The FCC ruling to allow consumers to use their own routers have been in effect since December, so I think they've been given a memo that they need to accommodate us, instead of selling us on why we should use their router, or say they cannot remove the rental fee. The process has been painless.

5-Stars!

And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.

review_title: Not just for displaying photos, I have some outside the box ideas...
review_text:
I've always thought photo frames are gimmicky, but FeelCare has changed my mind. The difference in using these versus turning a tablet into a photo frame is that it SIMPLY WORKS as it should. Getting a tablet to be a photo frame is quite involved and requires more maintenance. Also, this item actually looks like a picture frame! When you fire it up, it's actually running Android, a stripped down version that focuses just on being a photo player. The Frameo app allows you to beam photos to it easily. You can designate sleep hours for the frame so that it's not always on 24/7. I have mine asleep from 1 am to 8 am. Techies will turn old tablets into photo frames, but I think the main market here is for older people who are not techies. Great for parents and grandparents, but we'll be using it too and we're not quite grandparents yet.

Here are some outside the box ideas...

A joke on your friends:
--------------------------
Imagine your buddy come over to your house and looking at all the frames on your mantle. Smack dab in the center is a picture of his grandparents, or perhaps, his mom? LOL! He'll be like, "What the... why do you have a picture of my mom?" LOL! To do this joke, you need the frame to have only a few photos that's because it doesn't know how to display just 1 photo all day. It has to be in Slideshow mode 24/7. But you can select photos to hide. So if you have 5 photos, you can easily hide 4 of it, then it will only show 1 photo all day. If you have 200 photos, you would have to select 199 to hide. The joke is probably not worth that hassle. LOL! To pull it off, you also need to lower the brightness so that it matches the brightness of the regular surrounding pictures. And of course, hide the wires as best you can.

Card Magic Trick:
-------------------
I do card magic, and immediately I thought of a use for this frame. Have your spectator choose a card, then read his mind, then point him to the photo frame and say, "is that your card?" If you do Magic, you'll figure out plenty of ways to pull off this trick. This frame is pretty neat! 5 Stars!

review_text:
I read some of the reviews and concerns. Many are saying you need the original power adapter. My testing says that is NOT true. I plugged this cube into two separate charging hubs, not apple brand, and both scenarios worked.

You need a micro SD card (not included). Some of the questions in the Q&A shows that shoppers don't realize this. There is no built in hard drive in this cube, you provide the storage.

Turning off auto-sleep/auto-lock may get you through thousands of pictures in one shot. This is what I mean... I'm no stranger to trying out different back-up programs. The current program we use is from Plex. When the iphone is backing up to my plex server, the iphone doesn't know that plex is working, so it goes to sleep after about 50 pictures. When it goes to sleep, plex stops backing up. So I always turn off auto-sleep prior to backing up. With the Qubii, the iphone KNEW that it was working, so it "almost" never went to sleep. I said almost because after 4000 files, for some reason, the phone went to sleep. Still, this is much, much, better than the plex app. When I started Qubii again, it picked up where it left off and backed the remaining 1000+ files. But I did the test one more time to make sure! I cleared the micro sd card, and I reset the Qubii count. This time I turned off auto-sleep/auto-sleep on the iphone, and it backed-up the entire camera roll of over 5000 photos and videos in one shot! More trials need to be done to conclusively say this thing can't get through 5000 files without the auto-sleep disabled.

After backing up everything, you should remove your SD card from the Qubii and transfer them to a larger permanent hard drive where you store your collection. The next time you charge your phone, the Qubii will remember the photos it already backed-up even if those photos are no longer on the SD card. So you can always clear your SD card. For whatever reason, if you need the Qubii to back-up the same photos again, like I did when I was testing things out, all you have to do is RESET the Qubii count, which you can do in the Back Up Settings in the app.

Below are the two pictures showing you the scenarios in which I tested this Qubii. Both scenarios used third party charging hubs, but I believe I had the original apple cable. As with all products dependent on apps.. one Apple update can ruin everything. LOL! So these types of app products depend on the company to stick around, so that if Apple breaks anything, they can fix it with a new firmware update. Qubii was on Kickstarter, but only time will tell. As is, this is an amazing product.

The current program we use is from Plex. When the iphone is backing up to my plex server, the iphone doesn't know that plex is working, so it goes to sleep after about 50 pictures. When it goes to sleep, plex stops backing up. So I always turn off auto-sleep prior to backing up. With the Qubii, the iphone KNEW that it was working, so it "almost" never went to sleep. I said almost because after 4000 files, for some reason, the phone went to sleep. Still, this is much, much, better than the plex app. When I started Qubii again, it picked up where it left off and backed the remaining 1000+ files. But I did the test one more time to make sure! I cleared the micro sd card, and I reset the Qubii count. This time I turned off auto-sleep/auto-sleep on the iphone, and it backed-up the entire camera roll of over 5000 photos and videos in one shot! More trials need to be done to conclusively say this thing can't get through 5000 files without the auto-sleep disabled. After backing up everything, you should remove your SD card from the Qubii and transfer them to a larger permanent hard drive where you store your collection. The next time you charge your phone, the Qubii will remember the photos it already backed-up even if those photos are no longer on the SD card. So you can always clear your SD card. For whatever reason, if you need the Qubii to back-up the same photos again, like I did when I was testing things out, all you have to do is RESET the Qubii count, which you can do in the Back Up Settings in the app. Below are the two pictures showing you the scenarios in which I tested this Qubii. Both scenarios used third party charging hubs, but I believe I had the original apple cable. As with all products dependent on apps.. one Apple update can ruin everything. LOL! So these types of app products depend on the company to stick around, so that if Apple breaks anything, they can fix it with a new firmware update. Qubii was on Kickstarter, but only time will tell. As is, this is an amazing product.

review_text:
I was using the Harmony companion for the longest time, and before that, the Harmony 900. This Caavo is by far the best universal remote because it's so much more than that. Harmony is just a remote, it does not give you one unified user interface. If you've played around with a Smart TV's user interface, then you'll get the idea what this Caavo is all about. Except with Smart TV's, you still have to reach for your other devices' remotes, and if any device has voice search, it's only good for that specific device. The Caavo controls and searches all your devices! If I have a movie that's in my Tivo, that's in my plex, that is also available on Netflix.. all the choices are presented to me, so I can launch it from whichever device I choose. I have PLEX as my search priority, and it works beautifully. I was also a little nervous when hooking everything up because my TV is a Samsung from 2009, my Audio system is Sony from 2010. The Caavo has ZERO issues controlling everything.

My set-up.

Input 1: Tivo
Input 2. Fire TV
Input 3: Chromecast
Input 4: Currently Nothing
Optical OUT to my SONY AV system

My TIVO is set as the default. So when I push the power button on the remote. The Sony AV system comes on, tv comes on, and Tivo is what I'm watching! I was pleasantly surprised that it has all my Tivo controls because each button does double duty by short or long press. Let's say I want to watch a movie, I use the voice search to say BACK TO THE FUTURE, and since Plex is my priority, CAAVO gives me a list of choices with Plex highlighted. If it's in my tivo, netflix, prime, etc. it will give me all the options, but Plex will be highlighted since I set it as my priority. If I hit play, the Caavo switches input to my fire tv, launches Plex and auto-starts Back to the Future. And it happens fairly quickly. It's buttery smooth. If your preferred device to play Plex is on something else, say a Roku, you can set Roku as the default to launch Plex. If I fling something from my phone to the Chromecast, Caavo switches to my Chromecast input automatically. The voice search is perfect for youtube too because If you search something that doesn't sound like a movie, for example, How to Shop For a Miter Saw, the search results will show that there is no such movie, but included in the search results are youtube WEB searches, so you can easily play a youtube video on how to shop for a miter saw. LOL! Youtube is something I mainly do on my phone or pc because of the typing involved. But because of Caavo's voice search, we're watching it more on the big screen.

BTW, the voice recognition is terrific. It's pretty much on par with anything else out there. I've seen videos where some guy is complaining that he says Open Plex and it keeps giving him search results for DUPLEX. I don't know if Caavo has improved since his reviews, or if it just didn't like his voice, but I've never had an issue with Caavo not understanding what I said. Alexa, Google Assistant, etc. can also be integrated, but I don't see them as an efficient way to use Caavo, unless you lost the Caavo remote, then you can ask Alexa to turn on your tv I guess.

There is a slight learning curve, but it will be time well spent. And it will be easy to teach to your household members because it simply works. Lets face it, non-techies in the home will never touch your Harmony, right? I've used Harmony for 10 yrs, and nobody in my family touches it. They know how to use this Caavo!! This is a game changer!

July 17, 2019 UPDATE:
--------------------------
If you have Plex as your search default, I have a tip for you. The voice search will not understand funky spelling. For example the documentary "Comix: Beyond the Pages." The voice search will spell Comix correctly as COMICS, and so you will get zero results. But if you simply say "Beyond the Pages," the search engine will be able to find "Comix: Beyond the Pages" for you. Another quirk I ran into was "Mr. and Mrs. Smith." Even though the search engine spelled it exactly as my Plex has it, for some reason it didn't find this title. But if I just say, "Smith," it then pulls up the movie for me. So basically when you hit a snag, just use fewer words instead of saying the whole title. That's it! I really love this feature of the Caavo.

review_text:
At the tender age of fourteen, Davie Adams's life is ripped apart. His mother's loose ways leads to a series of events that leave him homeless after his she dies in his arms. Grief-stricken, Davie makes the decision to leave Blackburn and go in search of his father.

Davie could have returned to his grandfather's house but he can't imagine remaining in Blackburn and having to endure the pitying looks and talk about his mother. After his mother's collapse, Davie runs for help and finds Tom Makepeace. They get his mother situated in the back of his wagon and are getting ready to head to the infirmary but she passes away moments later. Immediately afterward Davie jumps from the wagon and runs into the woods. Everyone assumes he'll return. Tom even yells into the woods for Davie to come to his home when he's ready that he's welcome there. Davie has other plans though.

He does go to the Makepeace's home but it's only to spend the night in their barn. He hadn't expected anyone to see him but Judy, Tom's daughter and Davie's longtime friend spots him from her window. She goes out to see him and reassures him that his mother's body is taken care of and his grandfather will be just fine. Judy realizes that Davie has to do what he feels is right for him but she also knows that her feelings for him have gone beyond friendship.

Davie leaves the following morning with nothing more than the desire to leave his memories behind him. Life on his own isn't everything he thought it would be and his search for his father proves fruitless. For years Davie travels and holds many different jobs but through it all Judy and his life in Blackburn remain firmly at the forefront of his mind.

THE LONER is sure to pull at readers' heartstring. Spanning over an eight year time period, you get a lot of insight into the characters' personalities and backgrounds. I love that Josephine Cox doesn't focus solely on Davie and Judy's story, there are many other characters who possess stories of their own which add a feeling of realism to this storyline. Davie's journey of self discovery is the main theme and it's a story you won't want to miss. Josephine Cox is a gifted storyteller who knows how to keep readers engrossed page after page so that the doldrums of winter just disappear.

Chrissy Dionne (courtesy of Romance Junkies)

review_title: Synch your Phone With your Car Audio System
review_text:
This is a very nice product. I spend a lot of my time listening to podcasts while I do a 1.5 hr drive to work. In the past, I used to just sit my telephone in a cradle and turn the volume up, but at freeway speeds the ambient noise was enough to make it hard to hear the sound coming from the phone's speaker.

This product charges in your cigarette lighter and allows you to connect your phone to the car radio via bluetooth. You then have to pick a radio station that is not carrying a broadcast and set the control on the bluetooth FM to the same station. All of this sounds like a lot while I'm typing it out, but it goes quickly. However, I do highly recommend that you make sure the radio is set up correctly before you start driving. There are enough accidents caused by texting, and this does represent another potential driving distraction. If you set this item up while parked, it is very useful, but if you try to do it on the roll, then it could be dangerous...fair warning.

Once you have your phone connected to your car speaker system you can listen to your own music, podcasts, etc. It is a little bit of a problem when somebody calls you, however, because the device doesn't automatically un-pair when there is a call. I found I usually had to call people back if I got a phone call. Not a huge issue really.

There is also a mini flash card slot on this device so you could play your music directly from that.

Really a good product. I received a complimentary sample in exchange for an honest review.

The ad will still be out of the way at this point so it WORKS for this, just kinda adds one more step. Just a minor annoyance but still so much better than having youtube take advantage of me being in the shower and cramming 2 to 3 ads at me at once since I often don't wanna reach outta the shower to hit skip every couople of minutes.

Battery lifes decent. For the price, it's not bad at all. Again, I'd really just use this for the shower. Maybe outside around a pool even... But if you're not using it for the waterproof feature, I'd skip it- the sound quality isn't impressive at all.

Then just be careful that no one trips over the cord. (use brightly colored rope/ cord)

This is the best projector screen I've come across! For the price, it's completely worth it! I think because of the tripod legs that a lot of people wouldn't wanna keep this up full time in their house, for that you could just attach one to the wall possibly. That being said- the tripod legs don't actually stick out too far so they don't pose a huge tripping hazard.

review_title: Nearly flawless! Types very well! Holds a flawless connection to the computer, no cutting out!
review_text:
I'm a very fast typist so get angry when a keyboard can't keep up and quite often- a cordless keyboard can't keep up with fast-paced typing! This one can! I was very impressed by that and the fact that typing on it feels pretty natural!

The bad is that everything on the right is kind of jumbled together and there's no space around the arrows or enter key. Those keys also double as the page up and page down keys and they do work but the page scrolling that it gives is kind of jerky if you will. It jerks as it scrolls and it scrolls SLOWLY. I work from my pc and often I need to search thru hundreds of pages in a short amount of time. The included mouse works well but it's not great to scroll thru a lot of documents and my hand gets tired having to drag and drop the bar on the right... SO because of this sadly, I've gone back to my old keyboard which has the typical page up and down and it flawlessly scrolls up and down on a page VERY fast and without it jerking around while doing it. To some this might not matter and in that case- if you don't use the page up and down key then this keyboard is PERFECT. As I said the typing is natural. Very silent typing too which I LOVE.

The mouse works fairly well. I do a lot of work in bed so I use my sheet as a mousepad, the mouse has an issue with that sometimes and it's hard to get it to do what I want. I have noticed if I grab literally anything from a magazine to a pillow- it'll work as a mousepad though. Aside from that the mouse is great and works as it should!

Battery life- I've had the same set of cheap batteries in the keyboard and mouse for a week, they automatically shut off when not in use- no need to flip a switch! They seem very easy going on batteries because I use my computer for hours each day and after a month on some cheap batteries- that's impressive!

Wireless connectivity: I'm actually IMPRESSED. I have a pile of terrible wireless keyboards and as far as name brands go- Logitech has cornered the market on budget wireless keyboards it seems. That being said- I've yet to find a logitech keyboard that will keep a connection! They cut out non stop and miss key presses, it just makes the keyboards unusable! So I have a pile of their junk I need to donate... I've tried many other off brands and such and they all have the same issue, they cut out on and off and irritate me. This one triumphs over the others because the keyboard doesn't mess key presses even at a fast speed and that's certainly something!

At this price point, this set is 100% worth it! I think you'll be very impressed unless you need to use the page up and down buttons a lot!

A

I use these for work, 8 hours a day in a work from home call center. I have a large head and am a big guy. The sound is fantastic for voice communication, I would never use these for gaming, music or multimedia. The audio range is not good enough for those applications, it is great for voice. The microphone works beautifully and others can hear me clearly and crisply.

To say that these are "passive" noise cancelling is laughable. There is really no such thing as passive noise cancelling, it's just how much noise is blocked out by wearing the headphone. Do not take that into consideration when buying headphones, unless they totally cover the ear. You can hear everything going on around you.

The ear pads are pretty comfortable, much more than a foam ear pad on standard headphones. I do need to pull these away from my ears every now and then to restore circulation and reduce soreness. Durability of the pad itself is in question, but I have not had these long enough to figure that out. First impression is the pad might last 6-12 months using 5 days a week for work. To me the pads seem to be a weak spot durability speaking.

Overall a great headphone for work. If these had active noise cancelling and a more comfortable/durable ear pad, they would be perfect. I have no experience with microphone filtering yet.

review_text:
I have some very good cameras that take video, but they are large and heavy and getting them to do time-lapse is tricky. I wanted something to film the development paintings in my studio, and later in the season, in the field. So far, I am impressed. This kit comes with an external microphone, a remote control (uses aaa batteries--not included), two rechargable batteries, a charger and cable, a bracket, and a compact case with a belt loop. It does not include a memory card, so you will need to order one if you don't have one on hand. It accepts a variety of sizes (larger is better.) It will prompt you to format the card the first time you use it.

The camera is so small and light it fits in the pocket of my winter jacket. Its shape snuggles into the palm of my hand. It has a lot of features that take a while to explore. You can adjust the resolution and the asa, which is amazing for a camera at this price point. It also has a hot shoe, but you probably won't need a video light in most situations because there is one built in.

The viewing screen is bright enough to view in full sun and tilts for convenience. It shows you how much battery life you have and whether or not it is recording. So far, I haven't been able to tell what mode I am using by looking at the screen. I also need to figure out how to keep the date and time from recording, but that's on me. I'm sure there's an easy setting. I just need to find it.

If you want to film things closer than 2 meters, this isn't the camera for you. There's no automatic focusing. It's set at infinity. You can zoom a little. Of course, the wide angle setting has the greatest depth of field. I think the video quality is just fine for the Internet, which is why I ordered it and the built-in mic worked fine in my test videos.

The only thing I had trouble with was the single photo feature. It worked once, but when I tried it again, the camera locked up. I don't really need that anyway. I look forward to making time-lapse artist-at-work videos for my site with this nice little camera! For the price, it's amazing, and it's lots of fun.

Very nice filters! Arrived quickly in fine shape. I'll use them a lot for winter landscapes this year.

Both of the lens cap covers could stand to be attached via a nylon braided cord and it would be nice if the nylon bag could hold the accessories as well.

The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind. So, overall, I recommend this camera. review_text:
I admit, I haven't been a fan of Chromebooks in the past, but I decided to give this one a try. I have been pleasantly surprised. I like this little notebook/pixelbook is really nice. I like how light it is. It is very portable and will fit in a backpack, large purse or tote.

One of the reasons I didn't like these before, was simply because I didn't like Chrome as a browser. Now though, you can load a different browser on it, so I put Firefox...my preferred browser. It doesn't work 100% the way I'm used to, but it is close enough, and I have all my bookmarks from my other devices that use Firefox.

Another thing that has been improved is the size. The last one I had was really small. The keyboard felt cramped and I couldn't type on it properly. I kept hitting the wrong keys, because the spacial arrangement of the keys was too small. This one is great...very functional. My hands rest comfortably on the keyboard, everything is spaced logically for maximum ease of use. My only issue is a small one. I am a touch typist and don't like to look at the keyboard, even when first placing my hands on the keyboard. Most keyboards have a tiny dot, or something on the letters "f" and "j" so that you can find your "home row" without looking. There is a tiny raised bar at the leading edge of those letters, but they are almost imperceptible. I keep having to look down to make sure my hands are placed correctly. It annoys me to no end. I think I will find a way to modify those keys just for my own sanity's sake.

This Chromebook comes with no instructions...at all. Granted, it is easy to set up, you just open it and go, but then you have to figure things out by asking Google play (oh yeah, you need to have a Google account to use this) or Googling it. An example is, how the screen is displayed when browsing. Every website I went to was reading my device as if it was a cell phone. I was getting a slender column of content that was too tiny to read and only filled one third of the page, down the middle. I couldn't enlarge it, and couldn't read it. I had to Google the solution. It was a setting that I had to change to "view as desktop". Now, everything is oriented correctly...except for Facebook. It is still showing up weird and I don't know how to change it. All that is to say that you may encounter issues, and if you do, you will have to know how to do Google searches to find the answers.

At any rate, I like this Chromebook and will continue to use it. I recommend it for people needing access to the internet in a portable manner, but who want a larger screen to view than a cell phone. It is very portable, the battery seems to last a long time, and it is easy to use.

If you own a D70s and want superior night photography, this is the best flash in the world (good thing I ended up in the latter end of the spectrum).

If you just need some ports without the fancy HDMI, ethernet, and audio outputs save some money and get the Henrety hub.

review_title: Good features and powered by mains.
review_text:
While solar-powered cameras are convenient, I've found that they have too many compromises when it comes to functionality. In order to save on battery power, the software usually shuts down the camera when there is no activity. Usually, that means nothing gets recorded until the motion detector is set off. In addition, a couple of my solar cameras actually had firmware updates that made them almost unusable because the app can no longer wake the cameras up. This means that the only time I'm actually able to view the cameras are when there is actually motion to set it off.

This Reolink camera doesn't have those problems. It can be powered by a power adapter or power over ethernet. While this makes installing the camera more troublesome, it is worth it because I don't have problems like what I mentioned above.

In addition to solving this basic issue for me, I found that the Reolink camera is much more well-built than the solar cameras that I had previously. The camera mount is made of metal and the camera swivel mechanism is made of high-quality plastic.

The camera is pretty annoying during setup because it has a loud speaker that talks and talks until you finally pair it with your phone app but once done, the app runs like any other app that you might have used. It has controls for the pan, tilt, and zoom functions and it will show both of the built in cameras simultaneously.

Pop in a memory card and you have local recording capabilities with a nice timeline to control playback.

This is a high-quality camera that justifies its price.

review_title: Great concept.  A compact surge protector with a lot of options
review_text:
The TROND Flat Plug Power Strip Surge Protector is a great concept. Everything about it shows that some thought has been given to its design. Unfortunately, their choice of materials weren't as well thought out.

Some design concepts that attracted me to this surge protector is that it gives you 8 power plugs in a surface area that's just under 4 x 4 inches. The four plugs at the top are grounded while the 4 on the side are two-prongs. In addition, the wall plug is flat, giving you a lot of options as to where you can plug this product in. Finally, there are three USB-A ports and one USB-C port.

However, as I've mentioned, some design choices are questionable. As with many surge protectors, the USB ports are under-powered. The Type-A ports are not too bad at 5V/2.4A, but there is no quick charge capability. The Type-C is not PD, so your charging options are no better than the Type-A ports. You're stuck with 5V/3A with a total wattage shared between them at 14W or 3.4A.

My second gripe is with the build material. Compared to many power strips, the plastic covering this product feels quite cheap. It has a smooth texture and just feels... thin to the touch. The same plastic also covers the wall plug. In addition, the power wire is thinner than other power strips that you'll find. They feel more like the two-prong extension cords, except that it has three wires.

Now, I don't have proof that their choice of materials will be an issue at all, but it does give me pause.

review_title: Could be a little taller and more firm.
review_text:
I converted a small room in my house into a useful room where the floor is covered in Japanese Tatami mats. These mats are used for everything. Sitting, lounging, and sleeping. It's a different concept from Western style rooms where the furniture is based around sitting on a sofa or chair. In a tatami room, everything is lower by a couple of feet.

In the room, we have floor chairs that are great for lounging on but what makes it even better is the ability to do some work in that room. This laptop desk was just the thing. With a tilting top surface, foldable legs for easy stowing, book and cell phone holders and even a small drawer, this desk seemed to be everything we wanted.

I do have to say that it really is something that I love using, but because of how often I need it, the shortcomings jump out at me every time. Firstly, the tilting function is fairly useless because it can only tilt at predetermined angles and nowhere in between. The tilt is just too much because of how low the table is. Tilt the table and it is touching your lap.

The second problem is as I said, the height. If this was a couple of inches higher, it would be perfect. As is, my lap barely fits under it.

The last problem is that the table is wobbly from side to side. It's just not very stable. I can't put a cup on it. I'm forced to use a either a closed bottle or a shelf on the side.

While this will work for now, I'll be keeping an eye out for a better table if one exists.

review_text:
Feiyutech is a brand that I've come to know for their camera accessories. Generally, their products have great build quality and is well-designed. I've had problems with their app working with LG phones but once I upgrade, that wouldn't be a problem anymore.

The FeiyuTech Official SCORP-C Camera Stabilizer is a 3-axis gimbal made for DSLR and mirrorless cameras. All of the axis arms are metal with high quality plastic in the body. The motors are quiet and there are plenty of buttons that control most aspects of the gimbal. There's even a video made by Feiyutech that explains the buttons very well. This SCORP-C model does not have an LCD screen.

The accompanying smartphone app is used to upgrade the gimbal firmware and for finer adjustments of the gimbal such as the follow speed and horizontal calibration. Control of the gimbal itself is also possible, but it is easier and faster to use the buttons on the device. It really is a good thing that the gimbal is designed to be operated without the need to fuss with a phone and app.

A few USB cables are included with this gimbal, which is designed to control the shutter of the camera that you own. Unfortunately, my Lumix GX8 is an odd model that just isn't well supported, even by Panasonic themselves. None of the included cables worked for me so this gimbal isn't able to control my camera. Not a big problem, though. If I really need wireless control of my camera, I can probably work out some sort of phone mount and use the Panasonic app. Just be aware that Feiyutech's list of compatible camera might be a little limited. They publish a compatiblity list. Just search for the term "Feiyu SCORP-C Lens Compatibility List"

With that said, the gimbal stabilization is great. Once your camera is balanced (search youtube for "Scorp-C Balancing" to see a video demonstrating this process), the motors are very, very quiet and the various follow modes help to create smooth motion in your videos.

Recently, I'm helping my daughter record videos and this gimbal has really come in handy. My camera doesn't support in-body stabilization for video and the lenses I have do not have in-lens stabilization. Gimbals are the best answers for my camera's limitations.

review_title: Survived the wash, but I wouldn't suggest that you try it yourself!
review_text:
These Omidyi True Wireless Sleep Earbuds are my second pair because I accidentally threw my previous pair in the wash. Surprisingly, my original pair survived and this pair is now my backup.

Here is my original review:
These earbuds aren't bad at all, if you use earbuds to fall asleep. The advantages these earbuds have over wired ones are, of course, the wires. I used to go through wired sleep earbuds fairly quickly because I tend to pull on them quite a bit when I sleep. There are no wires to tangle here.

What makes these earbuds "sleep" earbuds are that they are much smaller than normal wireless earbuds (see my picture). They sit flush in my ears and don't protrude. In general, depending on your ears, these may actually allow you to lay sideways and still be comfortable. In my case, I can lay against my right ear without it hurting me but I can't do the same with the left. I often end up using only the right bud.

In terms of sound quality, due to their size, these earbuds will not be loud nor will they have great sound depth. The battery life also lasts about 5 hours due to their size.

I still really like these buds because I do like them more than wired ones but I don't use them any other time.
