review_title: These are NOT bone conduction headphones
review_text:
The only thing these headphones have going for it is a respectable battery life. Everything else is just a disappointment, unfortunately.

I've been trying to find a good but affordable pair bone conduction headphones because I keep a headphone on my head almost all day while I work and write my code but I end up shutting the rest of the family out and miss half of the conversations going on in the house. When I discovered open ear bone conduction, it seemed to be the perfect solution.

So far, I have not found a good one. The specific problems of this pair of headphones is that it is not bone conduction. It is a simple pair of speakers set next to your ear. There is no bone shaking going on. With bone conduction, you can put in earplugs and still hear the audio fairly clearly, with these, the sound is clearly muffled and hard to make out.

In addition, there is a half-second delay on these headphones meaning they are no good for watching videos. I have not experienced bluetooth delay in quite a few years so I wasn't expecting it. Further, there is no charging light, meaning there is no way to tell if they are charged or not.

Then there's the price they are charging for this thing. Everything is just NO.

review_title: Broken on first day.  Do NOT charge without first turning off the device
review_text:
I received my Tayogo Wireless Bone Conduction Open-Ear Headphones this morning and used it the entire day. While the sound quality isn't as good as a true on-ear headphone or earbuds, the advantage of a bone conduction headphone is the ability to keep your ears open to your surroundings. It was exactly what I needed.

It was a little bit odd to feel the bass vibrating my head at first, but I soon got used to it. I really did like this style of headphones.

At the end of the night, I plug the headphones in and I see the charging light come on. A couple of seconds later, it goes off and from then, I couldn't get any response from the headphone at all. No matter how long I try to hold the power button, it just won't turn on.

I realized that I forgot to first turn off the headphones before plugging it in. I believe that may be what caused the problem.

Quite disappointed to have a device work only for 1 day.

review_title: Lexar has good quality, but also a timed expiration
review_text:
I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.

There is ONE feature that sets this, and other Yi cameras apart, though. Install the Yiiot app through Alexa and you will be able to view the cameras if you have an Echo Show, FireTV, or Fire Tablet. Very nice.

review_text:
I hate to change the battery for the Ring Doorbell. It's one of the reasons that I didn't purchase those "stick up" cameras to put up around the house. I am not interested in having to change batteries every month. With that in mind, I set out to find a solar panel that works with my Ring Doorbell 2.

Looking at other listings, I saw that the ones that claim to work with Ring generate 5v, 3amps. I confirmed that this board also generates 5v, 3a (check my pictures) and took the chance to cut off the microusb connector that it came with.

What was exposed were two wires; red and black so there was no guess work necessary to figure out which wires would be positive and ground (usb usually has 4 wires). After stripping the wires, I screwed the wires to the back of the doorbell and crossed my fingers.

From my pictures, you'll see that the Ring app recognized the solar panel and also charged from 46% to 55% after one day in the sun.

Note: The wire is a little bit short so it may not reach your roof. I was able to get around this by soldering a longer wire from an old cell phone car charger.

review_text:
The rise of home automation devices means that many of us have a lot more devices that connect to our wifi networks. While most of those devices use the 2.4Ghz frequency while devices like phones, tablets, and firetv use 5Ghz to stay out of each other's way, it still means that there are so many more devices to manage in a network and all of them are attempting to talk on the network. Not to mention interference from neighbors and their many devices.

This drives the need for beefy routers with faster CPUs to manage all of the chatter and radios that allow many more simultaneously connected devices.

The NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-band Mesh System (SXK80) attempts to address these needs. Sporting the latest wireless Wifi 6 technology, most of the basic features that a router needs (QoS, DDNS, VPN), and 60+ device support, the SKX80 holds a lot of promise.

Unlike one of the upvoted reviews, I don't have a different AX system to compare this to so for me, this mesh router performs admirably. It is fast and has good coverage. In my time so far, I haven't had any dropped connections. Videos stream well and web browsing works fine. I don't normally do voice or video calls while walking around the house, but watching videos while walking seem to work well. My device will jump from router to satellite correctly and there is no disruption to the video playback.

review_text:
This usb type-c dock is very, very nice, but it isn't quite perfect.

First, a clarification for those who aren't versed on USB Type-C ports: There is a wide range of features that a Type-C port will support -- it's all up to the manufacturer. Just because you have a Type-C port, it doesn't mean you will be able to use all of the features that this dock provides. Unfortunately, you will need to dig into the online documentation or forums for your device to find out what you will actually get.

Windows PC -- Almost all Windows PC's will be able to use the SD/MicroSD reader, the Ethernet port, and the additional USB 3.0 and USB 2.0 ports. On my minisforum u700, this dock provides two HDMI ports and I didn't bother testing the VGA port. So on my PC and my laptop, I'm able to take full advantage of this hub.

LG V40 -- I'm on the T-Mobile service running their Android 10 rom. In this ROM, LG provided a little-know desktop mode similar to Samsung Dex that makes the phone work almost as well as a desktop PC. In this mode, the phone takes advantage of the SD/MicroSD card reader to transfer pictures and files, connect to your network through the ethernet port, and provide a large-screen experience through the HDMI port. Connect a mouse and keyboard and you have a great desktop experience. Plex and Netflix works extremely well in this mode.

Nintendo Switch support -- NO

My gripes about this dock: Being an 11-in-1 dock, this really should have a 3.5mm headphone jack, instead, they provided a VGA port. If your computer has a type-c port, would you really NOT have an HDMI monitor/tv to plug it in? Also, the lack of support for Switch means that I'd still need a separate Switch dock when travelling instead of having one dock that supports all of my devices.

review_title: I really wanted this to work for me...
review_text:
While this dolly is useful for rotating the camera around an object, I also saw this product as an option for cases where I did not wish to bring the slider track with me. I'd be able to have the dolly on a ledge and get panning shots for b-rolls.

Unfortunately, a couple of things made it a bad fit for me:
-- Difficult to place object in the center. Being that the dolly is not on track, it was difficult to get the dolly to rotate around the subject. When I placed the dolly far enough away from the subject to fit it all in the frame, I found that the subject would eventually become off-center or go completely off frame because it wasn't perfectly in the center. I ended up having to tighten the turning radius and place the camera fairly close to the subject to shoot a complete 360 pan successfully. This would be the same complaint I'd have about any other dolly that's not on a track, I would imagine.

-- Lowest speed too slow for the timelapse I wanted. I have a plant whose leaves close at sun down and open again at dawn. I wanted to get a timelapse of this while the camera did a 360 pan. I estimated the leaves to close over a period of 3 hours so I set up my timelapse. review_title: Affordable and adds very little bulk.
review_text:
This SmartShell case is not just a magnetic cover for the iPad Air. It has a hard shell that protects the back of the tablet. To me, this is preferable to the magnetic cover because of the extra protection. The disadvantage is that you will not be able to take the cover off easily like the magnetic cover. It adds about 1/8" to each dimension of the iPad which is a minimal as you can get and still have protection.

My kids dropped the tablet on its corner near the volume buttons from about 2 1/2 feet off the ground. The plastic around the volume buttons cracked (it's the weakest part of the entire case) but the tablet was fine. No dents or scratches. A little super-glue to seal the crack and the case was as good as new. Had it been the magnetic cover, the tablet would have had a pretty bad dent.

This case gives you the "tablet" stand capability of the magnetic cover while providing more protection.

review_text:
When purchasing a bluetooth mouse, or any bluetooth device, an important factor is how well it connects and how well it STAYS connected. After all this time, the industry still can’t make up its mind about how bluetooth works:
- Microsoft with their mouse and Sony with their controller that pair without the need of a code (which Android’s bluetooth stack doesn’t support).
- Mice and keyboards that will not reconnect after it wakes from sleep mode.
- To this day, bluetooth devices still can’t wake a computer from suspend state.
So when I get a simple bluetooth mouse for a good price, and it actually works as expected, I was happy.

For my review, I’m comparing the Bornd mouse to the [[ASIN:B006428K7I Motorola 89519N Bluetooth Mouse]] which I got in a set that included the [[ASIN:B004L9MBH6 Motorola Wireless Keyboard for Motorola ATRIX and XOOM (Motorola Retail Packaging)]].

With the Motorola mouse, its frequency somehow conflicts with the Motorola keyboard, resulting in sticky keys, as in “I’m having a good daaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay”. Conversely, the keyboard interferes with the mouse where the computer would actually lose connection with the mouse for a few seconds after typing, or lose connection completely.

What I liked about the Bornd:
- Pairing was simple using the button at the bottom of the mouse.
- Operating distance is about 5 feet, but this may be because of my computer’s bluetooth antenna
- Takes a single AA battery which lasts over a month of moderate use (2 hours per day)
- Mouse movement is good. No need to adjust mouse speed in the control panel.
- Accuracy is good. Editing images using Pixlr.com, I’m able to select precisely the parts of the image I need.

What gave me trouble with the Bornd:
- When you first put your hand on this mouse, you will not feel that it is very well built. The plastic is completely smooth and the mouse wheel seems to rattle when you shake it. I got used to it after a few minutes, though.
- The mouse reconnects with the computer most of the time, but sometimes it was necessary to turn the mouse off and on again after the computer reboots or if the computer was out of range for an extended period of time.
- Lately, I’ve been experiencing double-clicks when I click on the left mouse button once. I’m usually able to fix this by getting angry and slamming the mouse down a couple of times. This may indicate a build quality issue with this mouse.

In my specific case, the Bournd did not interfere with my Motorola keyboard at all and it seems the sticky key occurs only when the batteries on the keyboard runs low.

review_title: AWESOME ETHERNET SWITCH AND POWER SUPPLY!
review_text:
This powerful, silent, unmanaged Ethernet switch has 24 fast PoE ports (100 Mbps) that not only provide high speed internet (2 Gigabit Uplink) but automatically detects if the plugged in device needs power and, if so, how much!

I did thorough testing on this unit over the last several months and I am thoroughly impressed by the performance.

By utilizing the built in chip this switch will provide up to 30 watts to every Ethernet device connected (up to a total of 360 watts) but will not provide any power to devices that do not require power. I found that this switch works absolutely flawlessly.

Having the capability to provide ample internet speed and power at the same time makes this switch perfect for both business environments and as a hub for security systems.

I used this switch within my security system setup and mounted it within my security closet. I love that it is easily wall mountable but it can also be mounted within a rack with no problem.

I’ve tested my unit extensively using different security cameras and the results are nothing short of incredible. While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage utilizing this method as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

I have found this switch is rock solid and perfect for use as an unmanaged PoE switch for security cameras.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.

review_text:

This Cat6A nylon braided cable is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin flat nylon braided package contains aluminium foil shield, 4 shielded twisted pair (STP) of copper wires, with upgraded PVC protection for super fast transfer speeds.

The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. I love the nylon braided shielding on this cable - not only is it durable and will help the cable withstand damage but it just looks great.

I used this 25 foot cable to run between my router to my computer- a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

This has proven to be an outstanding, dependable Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love.

Besides getting an excellent 25 foot cable DBILLIONDA includes an additional 1.5 foot patch cable that is perfect for attaching switches to routers or similar connections.

This is a purchase that you’ll never regret. I’ve been utilizing several DBILLIONDA cables for a while now and I’ve had noting but outstanding results from them.

This is definitely a brand I recommend.

review_title: OK Cable Management Box - but Not for Bulky Power Adapters
review_text:
I have reviewed several similar products and while this could work for some I found the design of this cable management box needs a bit of redesigning.

The point of cable management is to keep your cables looking neat and tidy - this can help achieve that - as long as your plugs are relatively small. While there are four rotating outlets on the ends they are close together and depending on the size of you power adapter plug many will block the plug next to it. I found this was also the case with the outlets located on the top.

This is nearly always an issue with power strips of any sort but when you try to add a cover this becomes even more challenging.

This brings me to the cover design. The side wings expand and must be spread to the maximum width in order to unlock and lift the lid - and even then it’s not easy. This inner cover is thin and not very substantial. Once the other wings cover it that is protected but access is difficult.

Typically I am a big fan of Legrand products and find their designs innovative, helpful and user centric. I cannot say that about this product after testing it for a while.

In real world use I simply have too may power adapter plugs and USB powered devices for this to be a viable solution at my desk. I found it works ok for my entertainment center though I already had my plugs organized there.

In the end, I would recommend one of the more simple box style cord management systems. These allow the greatest flexibility and are definitely far less frustrating to use.

review_title: Decent TV Ceiling Mount - Could be Better
review_text:
We recently moved in to a new house and needed this mount to install a TV on our patio. I measured the VESA holes on our TV and knew this would work prior to ordering so that was not an issue.

This will hold a 55” Visio TV from a vaulted ceiling.

Installation is not as straightforward as I have experienced with other mounts though not terribly difficult either. The issues with installation really come from limited space to work to attach the parts together and there not being great instructions.

A few tips we found as we installed that will help you - first locate your ceiling joist stud to mount into. Then find the distance from the wall where your TV can swivel both left and right to the farthest point you desire - then mark your spot.

As with all mounting brackets you want to mount into a stud with as many bolts as possible.

In terms of use this works but there are features that just should be more user friendly. For instance if the height is in the highest position the cables will be pinched in place and can not be moved at all - the cable pass through should have a notch so this is not an issue as it is never good to have cables being pinched.

In addition if you want to either swivel or tilt the TV a hex key is required instead of being able to do this with a finger tightening knob like most mounts - this is definitely the worst design flaw in my opinion. This issue has left us unable to rotate our TVs mount that is “able to swivel” when we’ve had guests at our house due to not being able to locate the correct sized hex key. Ugh.

This mount works, but I would really only recommend it for locations where the user does not intend to alter the tilt or direction of the TVs screen very often.

There is limited tilt mobility but enough to adjust for viewing angle.

This is a decent TV mount for large TVs but could be better.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.

review_title: REALLY IMPRESSIVE WIRELESS WiFi CAMERA SET!
review_text:
I have been testing and reviewing WiFi cameras for the last five years. Over that time the industry has seen major advances which has led to incredible availability of high quality cameras at very reasonable costs. I have tested nearly 100 cameras and it takes a bit to impress me but I must say this set did just that.

I had no problem setting this camera up on my network. I set it both up after fully charging them in about a half hour with no issues.

Due to security precautions I never use cloud based storage in relation to WiFi cameras because that amount of constant data transfer opens your network to unnecessary hacking. The only cameras that I employ in my home allow for local storage - whether to a dedicated hard drive or individual micro SD held within each camera. This camera can hold up to a 128GB micro SD card. The card will over write the oldest data first - how much footage the card holds is dictated by the settings you select. Due to the fact these cameras only record when motion is detected a 128GB card will hold quite a lot and should suffice for 99% of people.

It’s important to know that by default the camera is set to record and save to the cloud. That can easily be reset in preference settings. In addition if you don’t install a micro SD card your camera will only capture still images when viewing - if you don’t have two extra micro SD cards order two when purchasing this set.

The camera provides a crystal clear 1080p footage and I found the motion activation very responsive. With my mesh WiFi network I encountered no lag in viewing - typically camera lag has to do with individual network properties rather than the camera itself.

The batteries in these cameras are phenomenal and actually last as long as is claimed in the listing. The battery’s life will be dictated by how often the camera is activated by motion but I have had both cameras installed and running now for over 2 months without having to recharge yet.

In my tests I found this to be an excellent budget friendly WiFi camera set that as long as you utilize the micro SD card feature is quite secure. Not having to run power cables is a major advantage and will allow these to be placed in far more places. The internal batteries are excellent and are sure to impress. The app is well designed, intuitive and easy to use even for beginners.

This is an all around excellent set of wireless WiFi cameras that I have recommended and do to you as well.

review_text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential. Unfortunately while the hardware has improved dramatically the software often has not - which is the case with this set.

The set I got did not come with a hard drive which wasn’t a big deal as I always have a few around. A suitable SATA Hard Drive can be purchased for $25-$400 depending on size and quality.

In terms of this system it should be clear based on the price - this is a budget system. That doesn’t mean it won’t work but these cameras are not going to pan, tilt or zoom (the lens is fixed).

If these are installed with this in mind they can still be very effective they just need to be positioned correctly.

For instance if these cameras were placed up high on a second floor overhang you would see an overview of the surrounding area but would not be able to zoom in to see facial characteristics. On the other hand, if placed on a porch a bit above head height you will have no issue making out the same. Placement is key.

In terms of wiring any POE (Power Over Ethernet) camera is excellent. The cameras are powered and transmit data over the same Ethernet cable. There are several advantages to these systems the most important is security as the cameras are not broadcasting wirelessly making them more difficult to hack.

The camera operation is excellent for the price. The images are clear and crisp and night vision operates without issue.

Where this set falls apart is on the software side - unfortunately this is often the case. The software is so non user friendly that it is almost unusable. I have used countless similar systems and this has to be among the all time worst software operating systems I have ever encountered.

There are countless glitches and bizarre, nonsensical methods for how it has to be initiated that it became comical as I worked through them all. I’ve actually used it as an example with colleagues as why a system must be actually set up prior to recommending it as on its face this appears to be an excellent value but the software unfortunately ruins what otherwise would be an excellent budget system. Unfortunately one depends on the other.

Due to the horrid software this set depends upon I would not recommend it. I can only hope the manufacturer would scrap the current software completely and rebuild with modern usability standards being their primary concern.

I have had the opportunity to review several products produced by WindTook and each of them have been well designed, manufactured from high grade materials with an excellent level of craftsmanship. This backpack fit that pattern in every regard.

There are dual mesh side pockets for holding a water bottle, umbrella or anything moist. Every pocket securely closes with zippers that are well made and have an 2” pull on each closure. All inner pockets are lined with a high quality polyester material. The bottom of the pack is protected by a polyvinyl covering. The right side has a built in charging USB charging port with a zippered pocket large enough to securely hold my largest power supply.

The back of the pack where the straps attach has as much padding as I’ve ever seen on similar bags - the padding measured it at approximately 1/2” thick. While this padding is thick it is designed to include ventilation so that is doesn’t cause a build up of heat while wearing. The center of the back area has an attached strap so the pack can be looped over the handle of a suitcase for ease of carrying when traveling.

The outer most pocket, on the front of the pack, measures 6” x 8”, is the perfect size for storing a wallet, keys, glasses or anything easy access is desired. The following pocket is designed for storing basic writing utensils - 3 locations for pens, a place for a calculator, a large sleeved area and a secured zippered area.

The one at the center of the bag is padded on both sides, has dual sleeves for sliding a tablet or small computer down in either side, and the front side has a small 5” x 7” zippered pocket at the top to secure small items. The rear most pocket is designed primarily for a laptop having additional padding on either side. I was able to slide my laptop in and out with no problem and it was secure while being carried.

If purchasing from e Dragon expect nothing in the way of customer support other than the absolute bare minimum required.

This is absolutely not a product I would recommend. Very disappointing.

review_title: Excellent updates on an already awesome light!
review_text:
I stumbled upon the IVISII brand a while ago and decided to give their products a try and I’m so happy that I did.

This upgraded IR-45 Ring Light Set by IVISII is exceptional. I purchased and have used their original IR-45 regularly for several months and was excited when I saw that they were releasing an updated model.

While many times the only option is to purchase high quality items a la cart or buy a lesser quality as a set I was so pleased with this set. Every piece in this set is constructed from high quality components and performs beautifully.

It comes with a light filter, a white softening filter, which snaps snuggly around the ring light and can be attached and detached with ease.

The set is complete with a standard 1/4” camera mounting bracket, a 1/4” mini ball head mounting bracket and a universal cell phone bracket. I’ve had no problems attaching and detaching all of my equipment repeatedly.

The light performs incredibly well. Due to the 19” size, it casts an immense amount of light. The new multi control knob is AWESOME- making adjusting the light output effortless - I can easily adjust the brightness of the bulbs from 1-100% just by spinning the dial and with a simple press of the knob’s center button, I have complete control over the temperature (or color of the light) from 3,000 Kelvin (soft white) - 5,800 Kelvin (Daylight).

Below the digital readout screen and the adjustment knob there are buttons with allow for the light to be synced with other lights so when this light is adjusted all of the others on that channel will automatically change as well. In addition there is a button that will step up the brightness in increments for quick adjustments when testing different shots.

This light can be synced with an optional remote control that IVISII offers. I purchased it a while ago with another set and would highly recommend it.

Due to the bulbs being LED the light weighs very little, produces no radiant heat and will last a very long time.

Unlike many photography sets that include a cheap, poorly made tripod, this set is complete with an excellent, sturdy tripod that will hold up for years.

The light and all of its accessories, except the tripod, fit within a great padded, easy to carry, case. The case has padding built into both outer sides and a middle divider. It is complete with heavy duty zippers, handles and an adjustable shoulder strap.

If you are looking for a light that will take your photography to another level, look no further. This is a set you are guaranteed to love.

Once again, IVISII hit it out of the park with this new and improved ring light.

I was a bit uncertain when I first got it, because the hinge seemed really tight and I was afraid I was going to break it, but after a few uses, it loosened up enough that it no longer worries me. This case is useful for a number of different reasons. The keyboard is easy to type on and very quiet, so if you are trying to take notes in class or work without disturbing someone, it is very appropriate for that.

The keyboard lighting is awesome, giving you ten different colour options and three different settings for each colour, as well as letting you go without backlighting at all, if you choose to do so. Some of the colours are unique, like pink and aquamarine.

The different ways you can spin the ipad whilst using this make it convenient for a lot of different situations, although mostly I use it in laptop or tablet mode. The case feels relatively well built and the set up is so easy that you don't need any technical know how to do it. The instructions that came with it were simple and easy to follow and I have had no issues with is so far.

The battery life is easy to check, since there is a button just for that, and the colour of the case itself is an exact match for the rose gold of the ipad I bought.

My only real complaint, is that it is somewhat difficult to get the ipad out of the case once you have put it in, without feeling like you are either going to damage the device or the case itself. perhaps there is an easier method to do it and I just haven't discovered it yet. Otherwise, this is a great product and if it endures m abuse for a year or so, I will consider it to have been well worth the money spect on it. It certainly beats having to drag around and extra keyboard and separate stand everywhere I go when I want to work on the fly.

review_title: Big pack, holds equipment & change of clothes, sturdy but cumbersome
review_text:
This pack can hold a lot of luggage, at least a couple of days worth, as well as electronics & work gear. I had this pack for weeks while 2 trips got canceled & I thought it was too big for regular work. When I finally put it up against my regular pack, I was surprised that the profile was about the same. It is still pretty thick with space for clothing as well as office electronics & supplies. It fit easily under the seat of an Embraer 175 (picture) fully loaded & extra-stuffed with a jacket but it had to go in the overhead on an EMB-145.

The straps are comfortable but it is not something I wanted to wear as a backpack a lot while it was fully stuffed. The bag has a strap for hooking around the handle of a roller bag which worked well. It has compression straps & a compression zipper. Almost all of the zippers go behind the compression straps which makes accessing any of the sections a bit of a pain.

The center section has a large, expandable area where clothing can be packed. In the summer I could probably pack this bag for a 2 day trip & still carry my laptop, peripherals & supplies. I used this for a January trip to Milwaukee & needed the extra space to carry winter clothing. For this trip I was able to pack a change of clothes & toiletries (along with my work electronics & supplies) in the backpack & leave my roller bag in the car when I changed hotels

This is a great travel bag for gear & clothing but it could be more practical. It is thick even without clothing inside, I had to carry a smaller backpack for my laptop & supplies to take into accounts. It only has two outside zippers on the front which access internal pockets. There is no place on the outside for a water bottle or easy access to things a traveler would use to stash pocket items while going through security. I tried several different arrangements & I'll probably figure out better & more efficient ways to use it on future trips.

Then move your unit to half way between your modem/wifi hub and the "dead" spot in your house or whatever. It will help, just don't expect lightening speed if your internet is not lightening speed or if everyone on your block is using cabled internet just like you.

review_title: Customer service is 6 stars I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to ...
review_text:
Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!

review_title: It's good for packing, but lacks support
review_text:
I like how much you can fit into this bag, it's got a uniform box shape instead of the classic tapered backpack (narrow at the top and wider at the bottom). The advantage to this is that it can fit more things inside while still fitting into the guidelines for under-seat storage on a flight. The downside is that it doesn't look as nice when worn- this is a function over form design.
That's fine- the problem for me, however, is that this bag lacks the rigidity I was expecting to protect the contents inside. In fact, the bag actually ships folded over on itself, that's how flexible the material is. I'm used to there being more of a backing to protect, say, a laptop in the rear pocket. As it is now, the laptop is what holds the bag's shape. I actually think I'd rather stick to my older backpack which was more stylish and protective when I travel, but this will come in handy when I need to fit more things in carry on.

review_title: Great for video calls and music, or BT
review_text:
Wireless headphones are great, but I have a love/hate relationship with using Bluetooth on a PC. When using the mic with headset profile for calls, the audio gets routed totally differently than regular stereo sound (A2DP), which gets confusing if multitasking and playing sound while also using the mic. And then there's the delay/lag etc that usually comes along with Bluetooth from a Windows desktop. But that's why I love the USB dongle here!
Plug the little USB bit in, and it detects the headphones like an alternate sound card, full blown crystal clear stereo audio, even if using the mic! And the mic can be extended or retracted, something I love since I lost the removable mic on my old headphones.
But, if I want to use it with my phone or tablet, I can revert to standard Bluetooth and connect that way on my Android devices. The price is a little bit steep, but the quality is there, this is a well designed and well made product that works as intended so far. I'm impressed.

Rather than the pigtail style adapters I've used in the past to bring my much lamented headphone jack back, this plugs in with a very sturdy connection and simply extends the phone in a way that I find much more aesthetically pleasing and easy to wear in a jacket

The one thing I'm disappointed about, since it says it in the description, is the lack of fast charge capability. This says it supports PD charging, but I tried it on my OnePlus with the OEM charger and it did not work. That's ok, I figured the "Warp Charge" VOOC that OnePlus uses isn't compatible, so I tried a standard PD charger. That didn't work either. Odd, because it specifically says it should. So removing one star for that, but I'm loving the TRS/TRRS detection! It's about time I found one that did that correctly!

review_title: Solid product, better than other meshes
review_text:
First of all, Wifi6 meshes are the way to go!
I'm coming from a TP-link Deco product as my Wifi 6 mesh, and I can honestly say this is much better as far as actual internet service goes. The TP-Link was very good, much MUCH better than a router + extender for coverage in my home, but certain devices seemed to drop connections when in between nodes. Most devices were fine, I just figured it was because they were too old to be fully WiFi 6 compatible, but now I'm seeing with this Dlink mesh that even devices I thought weren't so compatible can WORK FINE!
A few things I don't like:
- Set up and controls aren't as cool and refined as the TP-Link app. This is all web based like the traditional DLink routers of yesteryear. Don't get me wrong, no reason to fix what aint broke, but after using the TP-link Deco app, I think I'm spoiled by it. It would alert me whenever a new device hopped on to the network and give me real time stats and updates. And making changes was easy too. I wish this had that.
The Dlink setup here was a little slower and less intuitive, and you lose out on some of those live features.
- The units seem to take a long time to boot back up after disconnection. That means when there's a power outage or you just need to reboot in case of a problem, it could take a few minutes longer for everything to work again.

That being said, it works REALLY well once it is all up and running, which is really wonderful. There are enough ports for 3 hardwired ethernet connections as well as a dedicated yellow port for the modem (other devices like the TP link focus on wireless and make you use one of the 3 plugs for the modem). It's also a bit slimmer than other mesh systems and I like that the light in front turns off when it is set up and running which helps keep things looking tidy and unassuming (the TP-link nodes had a glowing light that was on all the time and was distracting when hiding on, say, a bookshelf or kitchen counter).

All in all, I'm really happy with the performance of this and I would highly recommend it.

review_title: Good music player with streaming apps. Sort of Android, but not necessarily what you think
review_text:
Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:75569821202ef0194cf65687a61f63d]] This is a fully featured 11th Generation Intel laptop in a tablet form factor. I love Windows on a Tablet, I've been a fan ever since the original Lenovo Yoga convertibles and Microsoft Surface tablets went mainstream.
The only problem I've had with those Windows tablet concepts is that sometimes you encounter applications that were designed for a mouse and keyboard rather than a touch screen. And that's what makes Windows 11 so great: You can finally run Android Apps thanks to built in virtual machine support. This is the first time I'm trying a Windows 11 Tablet, and I have to admit there's some initial setting up to do to get Android app support working (you can't just download an APK like I was expecting to). But once you do, it's pretty awesome and works the way I imagined and expected!
I'm not familiar with the brand Alldocube, but I have to admit the iWorkGT is actually pretty solid, has good build quality and an excellent display for the money. Since you are running an actual X86 Intel CPU, you're going to get a powerful experience compared to an anemic ARM processor like a traditional tablet would have, but the trade off is it will need to cool itself off like a laptop sometimes. That means vents and fans, which you will feel in your hands.
And this leads me to the cons:
There is NO CASE included with this product in the box. And since it is not a major brand like the Microsoft Surface, finding third party cases are going to be difficult if not impossible. Alldocube does sell 2 keyboard style cases which are interesting, however they are sold separately and not cheap! Sure, this is a lot less than a Surface, but at least a surface has plenty of after market cases and holders for every style and budget. I can't help feeling like it should have come with at least some sort of basic protection case. Even the Surface at least gives you the kickstand to stand it up, with this you have a portable computer that can get warm in your hands and nothing to really hold it in or stand it up with. You NEED to purchase one of their cases here.
The other con is that I did notice some strange behavior at times- the tablet wouldn't charge the first time I used it until I turned it off and rebooted. Another time the sound didn't work, and also wouldn't come back until I rebooted. That second time could have been due to the Android virtual machine being set up (it was right after trying it for the first time) and hasn't come back since, but I feel like it is worth mentioning sometimes there are quirks. But overall my experience has been positive and I enjoy using it, I just really strongly recommend getting one of their keyboard cases.

review_title: Comparable to much more expensive watches.
review_text:
Wow, these inexpensive fitness tracker watches have really come a long way! I've used WearOS, Fitbit, Galaxy and Amazfit brand watches, and usually find the cheap ones are cute for my kids but not very accurate or full of mostly gimmicky features.
This one actually looks and acts a lot like a cheaper version of my current Amazfit GTS3 watch. The way the menu works, the way the app works... it's all very familiar. Granted, this watch does not have the high resolution OLED display that my Amazfit does, but the display is capable of vivid colors and looks great!

The accuracy is surprisingly spot on, I even tested my heart rate with this and other smartwatches I own since usually there's a lot of discrepancy, and it often lined up exactly. Steps were interesting- most smartwatches don't count steps unless you move for more than a few steps at a time (disregarding a step here or there as an error). This one goes a step further and actually refused to count steps I made unless I was WEARING THE WATCH! I'm not sure if this is a attempt to prevent cheaters from shaking their watch or something, but I noticed it would not count any of my steps when I held it in my fingers, but when I put it on my wrist, it counted! Perhaps there is a proximity sensor on the back of the watch, I'm not sure. This might be a problem for those who occasionally put the watch in a pocket or something to get steps if, for example, pushing a shopping cart (since your wrist doesn't move, pushing strollers and carts tend to not count anyway- one workaround is to put the watch in a pocket but that might not work now).

Another thing I wish it had is a better notification system. Certain apps which aren't in their list of known notifications won't work correctly (Google Voice, for example). But that's true of all cheap tracker watches. It also can't install apps or extend functionality like the more expensive ones. There is definitely a reason my regular watch costs 5-6x as much as this one, but for what it is on a budget, honestly, it's pretty amazing!

review_title: Big upgrade from my last Samsung TV, perfect for cord cutters!
review_text:
I have been using a previous generation 1080p LED Samsung TV mounted to my wall with a Firestick for entertainment, as well as some older game systems.
I knew that the newer display panel would have some advantages other than more resolution, and that the smart-TV functions would be an upgrade, but I had no idea how much of an upgrade it would be!

First of all, I obviously no longer need a Firestick. This TV has everything built in, and even has stick-style remote included so if you're used to that, this will be very familiar. All the streaming services I wanted are there, however I was nervous about some apps like Plex not being available since I have a Plex server of my own library and I didn't think it was such a popular mainstream thing to do. Sure enough, Plex IS an option and it performs flawlessly! The TV even has a browser built in, really making it feel like there's no reason to keep the Firestick around.

Not only that but it actually has a lot of built in live content straight from Samsung. Personally, I'm a cord-cutter and no longer subscribe to cable TV or even bother with local broadcast. I've been streaming only for years now, so I was surprised to find that Samsung offers me what appear to be live channels I can tune in complete with a guide like a cablebox. Some of the channels even have things I might be interested in, however I might look into disabling this feature since the idea of cutting the cord was partly to prevent my kids from mindlessly watching things "because it is on".

Since the menus are run on the TV itself, everything displays and moves at glorious high frame rate 4k resolution, which is awesome. Part of the problem with a high hz and resolution TV is that there usually is not a lot of content that takes advantage of all of that. Most of the time you're watching content only available in 1080/30p at best, unless you are lucky enough to find something available in full 4k and high frame rate. The menus and UI clearly do and you can see and feel the difference- navigating on this is a pleasure. review_title: Fantastic for editors on the go!
review_text:
If you're familiar with Samsung's other portable SSD drives (T5, regular T7, etc), you expect this to be a product that will deliver on speed and portability.
And it DOES.
Working with media production (video, photos, music, etc) on the go, having a super fast external drive is a necessity. I'm actually quite impressed at the speeds I'm getting off this. My office desktop workstation has a 14TB internal drive plugged directly into the motherboard for working on video edits, and this tiny marvel is almost 10x the speed, even as an external plugged into a petite USB-C port! That's incredible. And the new rugged design means I can slip it into a backpack or gear bag and know it will hold up.

Note for drive shuckers: Unlike the T5 and other older SSD offerings from Samsung, this does NOT have an mSATA inside anymore. It used to be worth it to buy an external drive on sale to strip for the SSD inside and upgrade your computer's internal drive with. Not with this product, the internal design is a single board with the memory chips, USB interface, etc, all on one board. But it's excellent at what it does!

review_title: Efficient mini-PC, but still no USB-C
review_text:
I love mini PCs and I've collected a few of them for different projects. The Celeron chip isn't a speed demon, but combined with Intel's GPU it is fast enough to drive 2 HDMI displays quite well, and like most other mini PCs out there, it has enough RAM and storage for light media consumption and internet tasks.
But there are few things that stand out with this model:
- This one is FANLESS. Without moving parts whirring, this actually manages to stay completely quiet while running.
- Also since the body is the heat sink, it doesn't need space for airflow and is therefore more compact as well.
However, not all of those changes are positive:
- There is no upgrade option for the storage like other mini PCs. Some of the popular boxes out there have an access door to add your own sata SSD drive for additional storage. This does not.
- The fanless design also sometimes means that in hot environments (such as attached to the back of a large TV display sign), there is no way to cool itself off other than throttling the processor. Most of the time this doesn't mean anything, but like all fanless computer designs it is extremely possible the unit will need to slow itself down to prevent overheating if used for extended periods of time. A fan unit has alternative ways to cool itself off at least.

But the biggest disappointment to me personally, is the lack of USB type C ports. It looks like this has one, but that look is deceiving. The port is just a PD input to run the unit. I actually like that it is using a standard instead of the circular DC ports that other mini PCs use, the PD power port is plentiful these days and you can use most laptop and other standard PD chargers to run this device. However, it still does not work as a standard USB-C for peripherals that are compatible with one. To be fair, most of these mini PCs I've tried oddly lack a type C port as well. I can't really detract any stars for that, but I got excited for a moment that this would have one only to see it is the power port.

These are excellent for listening to audio in a noisy environment such as an airplane or bus. I wasn't expecting much out of the noise reduction system at this price point but it was pretty decent. review_title: Solid high end Android head unit, and WIRELESS ANDROID AUTO IS POSSIBLE (with beta firmware)!
review_text:
I bought an Atoto F7 standard last summer, and while I loved the features for the price, there were some shortcomings that made me want to try their higher end S8 editions instead. I got a chance to swap it out for an S8 Ultra, and I'm very impressed so far.
Let me tell you, I had my reservations about a phone/tablet OS running as a car stereo, but Atoto has done an incredible job making this as smooth and user friendly and FEATURE PACKED as you could ever imagine. Android Auto works of course, if you want to use your phone connected to the display. Even better, WIRELESS Android Auto works as well! They don't advertise this since it is in beta as of the time I'm writing this, but after asking Atoto customer support about it I was given access to the new test firmware and it works surprisingly well with my Galaxy S10 phone. All I have to do is press the Carlink button on the screen, my phone can stay in my pocket, and within 10-15 seconds the Android Auto connection is displayed on the car screen as if I had plugged it in. It also has an excellent Bluetooth audio input for the microphone, which is something I struggled with on the F7 I purchased previously. My car has a convertible roof that creates extra wind noise on the highway even closed, and callers can hear me just fine! But of course, the biggest pro is the ability to run Android apps directly on the head unit without needing to connect my phone.
I preloaded offline maps for most of NY/NJ in Google Maps, so wherever I end up I can navigate home (even if I don't have reception up in the mountains), all without needing my phone connected. I can also stream youtube and other apps (for the passengers, obviously!) as well as install all kinds of cool automation tools and car diagnostics thanks to a bluetooth OBDii plug I already owned.

It's not without a few caveats, however. Some things to be aware of:
1) The unit has a 5 minute delay when shutting off. This is apparently to avoid data corruption in case of a power cycle (key removed and restarted, such as for example if restarting the car). If you plug anything into the USB ports, you'll see them still on and drawing power for a solid 5 minutes after you've left the car. My wireless charger, for example, continues to be lit up and charging if I use the head unit's QuickCharge port built in. Any other peripherals such as remotes or volume knobs, etc, will remain illuminated for those few minutes. While most apps (built in music player, youtube, etc) are able to receive the signal to stop playing when the power is shut off right away, third party apps (such as some podcast or other streaming music players) actually CONTINUE TO PLAY during this 5 minute delay unless you paused/stopped them before removing the key. It's only a few minutes, and the truth is I usually play podcasts from my phone streaming, which DOES shut off right away since the Bluetooth connection is severed immediately when the key is removed. However I was surprised to find out it didn't stop everything immediately and they don't tell you this in the instructions at all.
2) If you are using Wireless Android Auto / Carplay, it creates a wifi ad-hoc connection that your phone connects to. With Android Auto, this can take a pretty big hit off your battery, but it is worth it to not pull your phone out on a small drive. However, due to the 5 minute delay I mentioned earlier, you might find that your phone is still connected to the car for a few minutes after you've left if you are in proximity of it. My car is parked just outside my office window, so I was surprised my phone wasn't connecting to my office wifi at first, then a few minutes later the car finally shut off the wifi and my phone was able to connect to the local network as expected. That delay, once again, was a little bit unexpected since at first I did not understand what was wrong.
3) Bluetooth and Android Auto volume are not consistent. For some reason, when connected with Android Auto, the volume is louder. So if you switch between them you'll have to adjust. Again, none of these are deal breakers, but things I found odd.
4) Bluetooth streaming has limited control over track. This is the one that surprised me the most since the less expensive F7 is superior in this regard. For those who know about Bluetooth profiles, there's the streaming stereo profile which gives you some ID tag metadata, and then there's AVRCP, which is the part used for remote controlling the playback. It seems that if you're playing audio from a phone, you are only getting the first profile, and not the AVRCP one. I've included a picture to illustrate the difference. With track control like you get on a dedicated bluetooth headunits, it shows the duration of the file being played, and you can even scrub through it by holding the forward and reverse buttons (like you would on an old school CD player). I listen to a lot of audiobooks so I like seeing how far into the file I am. But on the S8, it just shows the name of the file and artist/title, and then dancing lines to the audio levels. To be honest, the dancing lines are kind of distracting as well, but I can just hit home to go back to the main screen and not look at them. There's not much point in staying on that screen if I don't get track duration info anyway.

All in all, I think these setbacks are largely due to the way Android works and was designed as an OS. Atoto has had to customize a lot of things to make it work as a head unit, since things like receiving a Bluetooth stream (remember, phones and tablets running Android transmit to OTHER speaker systems, the system itself wasn't designed to be a receiver!) and going into a specialized "sleep" that shuts off all critical functions when you leave (all radios and apps running shut off) yet starts back up within 2 seconds when you turn it back on, etc (this is not regular sleep which still runs background operations- you don't want to come back to a dead battery! but powering off completely means you have to wait longer for bootup)... I think these limitations are reasonable. Atoto support has been amazing and incredibly responsive, whenever I had a question or concern, they got back to me within 24 hours which is more than I can say about radios I've owned from Pioneer and Sony in the past.
I think with time and software updates, they can eventually find clever ways around most of those caveats mentioned above, in which case I'd update this review to 5 stars. For now, I'd say this is a solid buy for what you get, I don't think a better iteration of this product with these features exists yet today. The sound quality is better than my stock Toyota ever was (even using the JBL amp it came with), and all in all I'm super happy with it so far.

review_title: Amazfit is still the best value!
review_text:
I've owned and had the opportunity to try out many different brand of fitness tracker watch, from Fossil/Wear OS, to Fitbit, Apple, and many of the cheapo brands too. I've said this before, but generally you get what you pay for, aside from the Amazfit brand watches. These and the Xiaomi Mi band series always impressed me, punching way above their paygrade. This latest edition just continues that legacy.
To be clear- there are some pretty neat features and apps that Wear OS / Apple OS will offer that this won't, but for the money this is the best value and user experience.
For starters, everything about the user experience here feels premium for the money. The battery life on this is killer. I charge it about once a month, maybe 2x a month. Granted I turn off features like lift-to-wake, but my experience with Apple and Wear OS devices needed charging daily in comparison.
The display is beautiful- a very vivid OLED, with very responsive touch screen. The animations are fluid and feel premium, and the display is large enough to easily read notifications and even responses from Alexa! That being said, this model lacks the speaker that the Pro model does, so while I can ask Alexa questions, I have to read her answers. I also can't answer calls since there is no speakerphone, however I can silence the ringer if I don't want to take it.
The sensors are improved over the series 2, however the functionality is mostly the same. In fact, if you have a GTR or GTS2 already, one might argue that this is a lateral move and not necessarily an upgrade, aside from one major new feature: With the new Zepp OS, Amazfit is going to allow mini-apps that can be installed on the watch. THIS is the big thing that is missing compared to other name brand smartwatch devices. So far there are only a handful of mini apps in their "store" and arguably not anything I particularly was looking for, but there is talk of an API being released for third party developers. Who knows, maybe we'll even get some basic games or other nifty features coming soon. I still have my GTS2 which I love as well as this, but I'm holding on to this for the potential app development in the future. Can't wait to see what Amazfit does next!

This latest edition just continues that legacy. To be clear- there are some pretty neat features and apps that Wear OS / Apple OS will offer that this won't, but for the money this is the best value and user experience. For starters, everything about the user experience here feels premium for the money. The battery life on this is killer. I charge it about once a month, maybe 2x a month. Granted I turn off features like lift-to-wake, but my experience with Apple and Wear OS devices needed charging daily in comparison. The display is beautiful- a very vivid OLED, with very responsive touch screen. The animations are fluid and feel premium, and the display is large enough to easily read notifications and even responses from Alexa! That being said, this model lacks the speaker that the Pro model does, so while I can ask Alexa questions, I have to read her answers. I also can't answer calls since there is no speakerphone, however I can silence the ringer if I don't want to take it. The sensors are improved over the series 2, however the functionality is mostly the same. In fact, if you have a GTR or GTS2 already, one might argue that this is a lateral move and not necessarily an upgrade, aside from one major new feature: With the new Zepp OS, Amazfit is going to allow mini-apps that can be installed on the watch. THIS is the big thing that is missing compared to other name brand smartwatch devices. So far there are only a handful of mini apps in their "store" and arguably not anything I particularly was looking for, but there is talk of an API being released for third party developers. Who knows, maybe we'll even get some basic games or other nifty features coming soon. I still have my GTS2 which I love as well as this, but I'm holding on to this for the potential app development in the future. Can't wait to see what Amazfit does next!

review_text:
This is a great toy for a kid who's interested in science! It's essentially a kid's digital camera that can record stills and FHD video onto a memory card, however you can pick either a macro lens (microscope) or telephoto (telescope) with the press of a button. I thought this would be more interesting than the stand-alone microscope option, however now that I've tried it, I think the microscope is a better product. The telescope isn't all that useful- for starters, at the sort of telephoto distance you'd use here, it's nearly impossible to hold the thing still enough to avoid a blurry photo or shaky video. Also, the white balance is ridiculous and seems to lock onto the K-value of sunlight only, making everything just look bad.
The macro Microscope, on the other hand, is really nice. The end of the lens barrel lights up with LEDs to illuminate your subject, and that ensures the color white is really white as well. Also at short distance, it is easier to hold it still and you can get some really interesting pictures and videos of things so magnified as to make it seem like something else entirely.
Switching between the modes isn't all that intuitive, my kids seem to have trouble swapping them every time. The unit also doesn't have the highest build quality, feels like a cheap plastic kids camera. For the price, I was hoping for something a little bit better.
That being said, my daughter loves the microscope part and wants to take it to school to show her teacher. She has thanked me multiple times for it. I can't complain too much, she has fun with it and it does work. I just know it COULD have been better.

review_title: A huge step up from the original Portal!
review_text:
We've been using an older first generation Portal and like it very much. I was not expecting to be so impressed with this one, but wow have they managed to improve almost everything about the original! It still has the very cool zoom-and-pan style camera feature that follows the subject, as well as all the fun filters and of course my kids' favorite, story time... but the polish and style of this unit is really premium. The speaker is fantastic and LOUD if you want it to be. The clarity and bass rivals my bookshelf speakers so well, sometimes the kids play music off it and I could have sworn they were using the speakers in the living room. But the biggest improvement over the previous generation is the ability to run off battery power and move around. The "portable portal" honestly makes so much sense, I wonder why the original stationary style ones came out first!
Make no mistake, it is NOT a tablet, it is not thin and won't fit in an attaché case nicely. It is wedge-shaped making it stand easily at an ideal angle, and even has a cut-out handle to pick it up and carry it to a better location for video chat. This is great for bringing it to wherever my kids happen to be congregating currently, and it can be put back up on the shelf when done to charge. Like the original Portals, it has Alexa built in and can act as an Echo for most things, however it is very tied into Facebook's ecosystem. That means that although it seems to run something akin to Android behind the scenes, this is NOT going to offer a standard App store, and even things like Youtube are not available for it (licensing issues with Google I'd suppose). However there is a browser, and you can navigate to YouTube and play it from the website just fine, although a proper app would be much easier to navigate. It does have Plex support, which I found interesting since I have a Plex server. I never thought I'd find Plex available where Youtube is not! Meanwhile, between Youtube in the browser, Amazon Music through Alexa and content on Plex, there are plenty of ways to make it a music streamer on that glorious better-than-it-should-sound speaker. And the camera works just as well if not better than the OG Portal!
Calls over FB Messenger or Whatsapp work well, and of course the camera / mic not only have a switch to toggle, but the camera has a physical cover that can slide over the lens in case you don't trust Facebook not to snoop. But that's another story.
All things considered, this is a solid product.

review_title: Works if you need, but jumpy
review_text:
I wanted to like this mouse. There are so many things I like about it better than my other wireless mouse- the design is more ergonomic and comfortable to hold, the buttons are easy to reach (if you're a righty at least!), and I like that it doesn't have a glowing red dot on the bottom, I'm assuming it uses IR or something invisible to humans. Although, to be fair, it does make it hard to determine if the thing is powered on or not!
At first I loved it, the scroll wheel is good, even the modes to control the dpi were a pleasure to cycle through. But then it got... jumpy. Like, sometimes I would move the mouse and it would feel like it paused and had to catch up all of the sudden. Movements didn't seem to mimic mine in real time. I do a lot of video editing and have to shuffle clips around with precise movements, I found this inconsistent behavior really unsettling to work with and needed to go back to me old boring flat mouse. If you don't have a mouse or just want to make browsing easier on a chromebook or something like that, it's good in a pinch, especially for the price. But sadly it is not reliable enough for moderate to heavy users in my opinion.

review_title: Great kid friendly tablet, parent approved!
review_text:
I actually just had an opportunity to try the pink version of this tablet, which you can find under a different listing here. It's an identical tablet from the same brand with a different colored case outside. Which is a GOOD thing, because I actually really like the tablet underneath, and the case it comes in!
It's not cutting edge hardware, but its fast enough to do anything kid related easily. The cameras aren't great, but again- at this price you shouldn't expect them to be Galaxy S or iPad camera. But the actual user experience is pretty good despite the cheap price tag.
For starters you get Android 11 out of the box, which is pretty incredible to find on an inexpensive device. It also comes with some pretty excellent kid software that parents can use to control and offer fun, entertaining and educational games and apps.
The case is the best part, however, as it is thick and "kid proof", as they say on the box. There's a stand that be adjusted or used as a handle, and overall gives you something substantial to hold onto. The only thing I'm not crazy about is that the case makes the holes and buttons a little bit difficult to reach/line up. The case is very thick, as we already said, so sometimes plugging in, say, a USB OTG plug with a keyboard is a little difficult to line up in the hole. And the power button isn't in a great place for little fingers to find quickly. But these are minor details, it is still a pretty great tablet that will work well for kids.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:ef18b2bc61d2bf43363a5f3d51e2b5d8]] This is a pretty great tablet geared for kids. Inside of the "kid-proof" case is an Android 11 powered tablet with a comfortable-to-read 10" display, much better than the 7" Kindle Fire tablet that my kids used to use before this. It has the standard Google play store, yet still comes with plenty of parental control tools and a pretty great suite of software for kid friendly use (something I really liked about the Kindle OS).
It even comes with a USB OTG plug so that you can plug in accessories like a USB sticks, a keyboard or barcode scanner, etc.
The only thing that bothered me a little bit is that the case makes the buttons and USB port a little bit difficult to line up. To turn on and off the power, for example, you need to find the on button next to the volume buttons, which isn't immediately easy for a kid to find. I can imagine younger ones especially hitting every other button first. And the OTG adapter had some trouble fitting in the hole cutaway since the port didn't sit exactly in the middle of the case. The cameras were also cheap-phone quality, but then again I never expect good camera performance at this price range.
That being said, it does an excellent job at what it is designed to do: Be a kind friendly tablet that parents will be happy about.

I have a similar LED light with a Bowen's mount that is much bigger than this one, so I was a little bit hesitant to believe this would be as bright as they claim. However, they must have had some major progress in the field of LED brightness and/or cooling, because they somehow managed to shrink this thing down! The light by itself is going to be far too harsh since it is a tiny dot emitting all the light at once. With a good diffuser using the industry standard Bowen's bayonet, you're good to go!

Part of me still thinks perhaps this will overheat on account of being so compact without a big cooling system, but so far it is not failed me! I wish it would let me adjust the color, but it is permanently set at 5600k. That's ok as I'm used to similar lights in that range as well, and it is a good color to blend with natural light.

review_text:
I've been hired to do a lot of live stream jobs since the pandemic, and that usually means my trusty laptop with OBS installed + Magewell HDMI to USB adapter + camera/tripod. If they need multiple cameras, I need to lug along my Blackmagic ATEM box and have that do camera switching before the Magewell. It's a lot of equipment to set up, worth a LOT of money, and that's not even counting the internet connection, which sometimes I need to supply via cellular hotspot device.
This unit replaces ALL OF THOSE. I can't even begin to accurately describe how incredibly versatile of a tool this is, but considering the price of all that equipment individually, this is a STEAL at the asking price. Sure, OBS might still be able to pull more complicated tricks that the UI here can't, and the ATEM switch can support more cameras (including SDI cables), but most of the time this is truly all you need and even then some! And there is so much value in the simplified hardware setup here.
The unit seems to run a customized UI over Android, and I was able to do some live multi-cam switching with minor effects on Youtube live using the built in Cat5 port. I am blown away with how capable this is. The only downside is there's a bit of a learning curve since it is a very niche product and offers a LOT of functionality, so you have to familiarize yourself with the features and how it works. But once you do? This is an excellent tool for any streamer. Highly recommended!

review_title: Its an OK tablet if you can get it cheap.
review_text:
There are dozens if not hundreds of off-brand Android tablets available these days. Some of them are impressive for the money, some of them have stand-out features like USB host ports, removable batteries or IR blasters... and some of them are just boring run-of-the-mill standard fare. This is one of the latter ones, unfortunately.
The screen size is nice at 10", but the resolution is a paltry 720p at that size, which makes the pixels more noticeable on fine text and graphics. If all you want is something to play games and watch videos on, the display is fine, but if you want the large screen for an e-reader or for pixel-peeping details in graphics, the resolution will quickly feel too low. The processor is not terribly fast, although it holds up decently if you're not multitasking a lot. That being said, the 2GB of RAM won't hold up to a lot of multitasking anyway. The cameras are pretty terrible, too. If you need a device for a zoom meeting and having good lighting, having a bad camera is better than no camera, but don't expect to take pictures worth keeping. Like, at all. Pictures look almost like old flip-phone era quality. And beyond that, there are no stand out features that add value to it. There's a TF slot, but that's not rare. Supposedly there is a SIM slot, however there is a lot of conflicting info in the paperwork re: whether this device is WiFi only, and I wasn't able to determine any cellular functionality.
At the end of the day, it's a good bargain tablet with a decent sized display. You can do basic Android tasks, play some light games, watch some videos, etc, and if that's all you want it for, it'll get the job done. BUT... keep in mind that there are alternatives like the Kindle Fire and brands like Lenovo's M10 which are pretty close to the asking price on this and have a far superior user experience. So it sort of makes one wonder why someone would choose this device over those. If you can get this for significantly less than those models (perhaps if it goes on sale), I'd recommend it as a toss around tablet. But the value is really hard to find at the moment.
