review_text:
Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.

I didn’t like the fact that the Toshiba lacked some normal features that you would see on a normal TV like being able to adjust the aspect ratio. Crazy. It also came with extremely limited app storage and you couldn’t delete half the apps that were taking up the limited storage. So far the Google TV operating system seems faster and easier to use. The picture is gorgeous. I don’t have cable, so I rely on digital OTA channels or streaming channels. You run this calibration holding the remote at chest high and the TV plays some sounds that sounds like space invaders and the remote records them and adjusts the sound accordingly. The TV was easy to set up, although the whole linking of the Google accounts and all the other things they want you to sign up for was a bit of a chore. I opted out of some and kept others. Your mileage may vary. The table top stand is the easiest to install that I’ve ever seen, you just plug it into the bottom and there it is. No dealing with screws or anything like that. There are a decent number of HDMI inputs and two USB ports, so that’s a plus. Finally, while it says you need to people, I didn’t have two people and it was not that difficult to handle the TV. You do need to be really careful not to press on the LCD, which is a given for any TV. But the TV only weighs less than 30 pounds so it was easy to carry. All in all, it’s a really nice TV. I think it’s a little pricey, but you’re paying for the Sony name. And it does appear to be excellent quality.

review_text: I tried to love these cameras but they've let me down several times now.  Their motion detection is erratic at the best of times and since there's no ability to continuously record to an sd card or anything else, if the the motion detector doesn't catch it, it's not recorded. Worst of all, the whole system has a tendency to randomly go offline where it stops communicating with the cameras and nothing gets recorded. After the neighbors annoying free-roaming dogs set off my Wyze cam for the 20th time today it suddenly occurred to me to wonder why I wasn't getting Blink alerts. So I checked, and lo and behold, I wasn't able to connect to any of the cameras, and apparently hadn't been connected for at least 18 hrs based on the last stored clips. But there's no indication of any problem on the aggravatingly bright leds on the hub, they look like everything is peachy. I had to unplug the hub for a few minuted then reconnect. Not so convenient when you're not home, which is when you most definitely want your cameras to work. This is the second time this has happened and I'm done. Returning these.

review_title: Garbage.  If you want something twice as loud, 100 times better made and will actual bass, get a Kaboom! box.
review_text:
Low quality workmanship Knobs will clearly not last long, the speakers are screwed inside into what seems to be dense cardboard.

Horrible rattling/distorted sound at upper volumes. Use plain useless sound quality past about 75% for some songs.

Max volume level equivalent to a 40w JVC Kaboom! box turned half way up, so about 20w, not sure what type of "math" was used to call it 1000w.

Sound is *extremely* directional, as in, there is about a 400% gain in level if you stand to the side rather than in front. So it doesn't "fill" the room, just the sides.

No bass to speak of. Just wild distortion and horrible rattling.

Bluetooth seemed to work pretty well, but it basically allows anyone to "take over" the stereo while you have it plugged in and override wired sound.

The unit doesn't always turn on, you have to turn the sound source on, turn it on and off a few times, while unplugging and plugging the sound and power cable in between and pressing the only button (standby) inbetween for it to both actually power on and then realize and auto-select the sound source (since you have no way to do so yourself).

It looks striking and nice, the LED's glow rather well, and as pretty as you'd hope, with the rd adjusting & dancing to the music and the blue kicking in when there should be loud bass beats, so you can ate least see it even if the stereo can't handle any.

I've bought & used Pyle's stereo 8" and 10" powered, fully enclosed systems before (PPHP898A & PPHP1037UB). While their bass is pretty low, they are infinitely better designed, better made, drastically louder, and at least don't rattle, distort, and start wildly vibrating around on top of the surface you put them on.

I went with this because the the above two didn't have much bass and weren't easy to fly with, and the JVC Kaboom! keeps getting weaker and weaker with each new release and I need a good loud portable stereo to fill a bar sized area. I'd take one of the weakest/newest Kaboom! boxes over 10 of these though.

Also one the speakers on this ripped itself out of place and started jumping around inside the box on the first night of use. All four of my Kaboom baoxes, one being from the original series from the early 90s, still works great. It's just been covered with hundreds of spilled drinks. This thing didn't last a night.

review_title: Very good basic case, with excellent belt loop design. Fits camera 4.2 x 2.4 x 1.4 inches perfectly.
review_text:
This case cost just under $6 when purchased a few days back. As is my practice when purchasing or accessorizing an expensive item (in this case, the Sony HX20V camera), I did fairly exhaustive research prior to making the purchase. (Other cases on my shortlist were the LowePro Apex 20 and the Lowepro Rezo 30). My main interests were portability and protection. I wanted to be able to store one extra battery along with the camera, inside an efficient case that would allow for belt-carry and had a dual-zipper design to allow for the wrist strap to be used while the camera is inside the case. This case meets all those requirements. The fit is snug but not tight around the camera, and the zippers have protective flaps along the inside edge to protect against scratches on the camera. The front pouch, which has a velcro flap is pretty small, but will accommodate the extra battery. The dual zippers can be closed at the middle of the case with the wrist strap coming out between the heads of the zippers. This facilitates carrying the camera by the wrist strap if desired, while still benefiting from the case's protection in the event of bumps or falls. The padding sewn into the case is firm and seems like an adequate buffer against minor knocks. One feature I really like is how the belt loop works. The belt loop extends from the upper back edge of the case, and snaps in place at the bottom back edge. Instead of being a single piece of material that extends from the top to the bottom of the case, it is an actual loop. The upshot is that you can run your belt through this loop, and leave the bottom connection unsnapped, so the case essentially hangs about two inches below your belt line. I find this to be much more comfortable carrying method than having it flush against my belt, where it would be crumpled against a jacket waistline, or creating a bulge at the belt line. Originally I had planned to order a carabiner in order to achieve this same result, now that will not be necessary. If you are looking to travel light, you will be well served by this case. It is an outstanding value. Note, the approximate dimensions of the camera I have are 4.2 x 2.4 x 1.4 inches.

UPDATE, 2/20/2013: The case has proven its worth already. A couple days ago my wife sitting in the car and carrying the camera on her lap, in its case. When we arrived at our destination, she got up to exit the vehicle, forgetting that the camera was on her lap. The case tumbled to the ground just outside the car. After dropping from a height of about two and a half feet or so onto concrete, there were no ill effects noted.

review_text:
I have four of these now. They work really well, and consistently. As long as they are plugged into a power outlet, the clock continues to run, and the thing plugged into it goes on/off at the times you set. When I'm away, I use them on my lights. When I'm home, I use them on kitchen appliances to ensure that they are off during times I don't use them. You can also just set them to 'on' when you're home, or store them for the next time you need them.

It's a little counter-intuitive the first time you set it up, but, once you get the hang of it, it's very easy.

Unlike digital timers, you don't have to worry about small power outages. The only problem I can foresee is if there is a long outage, then the clock will be wrong and it will be going on/off at different times. However, compared to not working at all at the slightest outage, I feel that this is a very minor drawback.

review_title: Wait for the next version.  An unexpected and serious disappointment.
review_text:
I found Bose's latest wireless headphones to be a fairly serious disappointment, which was surprising and frustrating after having bought 5 or 6 pairs of headphones over the years, along with speakers and a Wave Radio. I *like* Bose products.

Let me start with the positive, to be fair.

1. They sound great.
2. They stay in my ears. (A feature Apple did not think to include with their glorious AirPods.)
3. The Bose connect app on the iPhone is slick and useful.

The negatives.

1. They are very big and jut from my ears in a way that looks comical. I've seen other people compare them to the bolts on Frankenstein's neck, but for the ears. Actually, though, it's worse than that, because their weight makes them droop. So I'd describe the look as more Frankenstein Eeyore. If you have hair that covers your ears, you will probably be ok. But I am close to bald, so I can't really wear them in public. Since I bought them to wear during my workouts at LA Fitness and while coding at work, the fact that they make me look silly is a show stopper.

2. Given the look issues, I'd love to wear them when I listen to music on my computer at home, but they don't pair properly with Windows 10. They have a voice profile and a music profile. No matter how I fiddle with my PC, based on advice from the various threads on Bose's support forums, I cannot get the music profile to activate. The reason this is a problem is that the voice profile only plays music in one ear, and at far reduced quality. Like it's-being-piped-to-your-ear-through-Satan's-toilet quality. Bose's suppport forums have various threads about this, and it's clear that some part of Bose's software group either doesn't get it or is trying to avoid publicly stating that they can't fix the problem. They claim it is Windows or software differences on various PCs, but my Apple AirPods work fine as do Bose's SoundSport Wireless headphones (though they lack a mic, so the scenario is somewhat different).

3. I wish there was a way to hear audio in both ears while making calls. You can do this with the AirPods.

review_title: Great For Stationary Position, Not Great For Traveling
review_text:
This is the kind of stand you get when you want to set up a station at a table or desk. It is heavy and not easy to transport if you need to pack it to go with you to the library or other places.

HEAVY
This is a very heavy and sturdy laptop stand. I can also use my S6 Galaxy Tablet on it. This is heavy duty and not easy to throw around.

COOLING
This has to take up a USB port on your laptop or plug into a USB outlet in the wall or power strip. It will be great in the summer or for someone really into gaming.

POSITION
This stand needs to be raised so high that I use my ergonomic keyboard with it that is cordless and has a USB dongle. It works great for that. I also find that it is good for doing Zoom calls or other conferencing if needed. I can have the camera at a good angle, and continue my work from the keyboard if needed.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great stand for having at a desk or table. It is good for a larger heavy laptop for gaming, or even my larger tablet works on there. Be prepared to use with USB or bluetooth keyboard.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is not quite as portable as I was thinking it would be, but I can get something else to take with me. For home use, this is great especially this summer when I need to do a lot of business work on my laptop.

review_title: I Am VERY Frustrated With This- You NEED A USB Port/Outlet To Use It
review_text:
Our antenna rotor broke and for 3 years we have been waiting for new chips to come through so we could get another one. It has taken WAY too long. I got this to help with the problem in the meanwhile. What I got was MORE problems.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a blister pack. It has a long cord and a double tail plug on it. The idea is that you put the plug into the antenna spot on the TV and the other is a USB port that you put into your TV. There is a sticker to put this on the wall and instructions.

HOW THIS WORKS
I have had no end of frustration with this thing. We do not have an OLD TV but we do not have any USB ports in this that work with the antenna. The outlets are such that I can not fit ANY adapters into the plug to use an adapter for the USB. The cord from the USB to the intersection where the antenna cord is is very short- only 13 inches. Put that together with the other cord for the antenna which is also about 13 inches and you can not spread them tightly so you only have about 22 to 24 inches tops to get from the TV on the wall down to a USB outlet if you don't have USB on your TV.

I TRIED TO MAKE THIS WORK
I have tried many different USB adapters to get this to work and none of them will work with this unit. I am frustrated and have spent so much time on this, I am giving up. I really wanted this to work, but despite this being an HDTV, it just isn't working out with this unit. I guess we will have to go without antenna TV on that TV longer.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you have USB available on your TV and an antenna hook up, this might work for you. If you don't have a USB port that will work with this unit, you will have to have an available plug that has USB conversion in it, or USB on a power strip that is not more than 24 inches away from the antenna jack on the TV to make it work. You can also use an extension cord and adapter, but honestly, it is a lot of expense for a unit that might or might not work as you like.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. I can not give this a terrible rating like I want to in my frustration. To be fair, three stars is about right. I do not like that it does not come with adapters or alternatives for TVs. Most people who watch antenna TV do not always have the newest equipment. We happen to have this TV that needs the hookup. We have another TV which is newer but the picture is not that great and we already have it set up with another antenna hookup.

I would like this a LOT better if it came with a streamlined USB plug adapter for the power outlets.

UPDATES
If by some miracle, I can find a USB adapter that will fit in this situation and actually WORK, I will update this review and reconsider the rating. For now, it stays as it is. I have put enough time and resources into trying to make this work.

review_title: Nice Strap, But Very Stiff, Hard To Store, Doesn't Smell Like Leather
review_text:
I have a camera that is very hard to find a decent strap for. The loops on it are squished oblong loops and almost no rings of straps will fit through them. (Canon Powershot G7X Mark ii). I was looking for a strap so I could use my camera, and finally found this one. It was any port in a storm for me, so let's see how it is working out.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes folded up on a round tube package. It is rather creative and distinctive. The price is very high ($75 at the time of this review) so this is appropriate looking for a classy gift.

HOW IT WORKS
I simply threaded the loops through the camera holes and the attached the round snaps to the strap on each side. Thankfully they work hard, so they stay in place. I don't plan to take it off often so that should not be an issue over time.

LENGTH
I got the regular length and it is perfect for my use.

PERFORMANCE
I like this strap in that it is soft near the neck and sturdy in use. I am not fond of the fact that it is so STIFF with no easy way to wrap it around the camera or fold it for storage in a small case. It is kind of cumbersome actually.

IS IT LEATHER?
I am not sure if this is full grain leather or bonded leather. It does not smell like leather so it might be bonded leather which many technically call leather. It is lined with soft synthetic fiber lining though, so it will not scratch the neck or skin

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice strap, sturdy and nice looking. It is very stiff, however to work with and that makes it cumbersome when moving my camera around or storing it.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. This is nice, but it is nowhere near worth $75. I would say perhaps $40 or so would be a good price. It is a nice strap and it works for my camera, but it is also frustrating at times to work with.

review_text:
I do a lot of work on sewing machines and electronics that need to be sprayed with air often. I was having a hard time with canned air working right or stopping working before it was gone. Then I saw this. I am never going back!

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a combo vacuum/blower. It has a clear blue top on it for catching dust and dirt, and then it is removable so that you can blow air on things with a simple switch on the side. There is a small hose extension for focused air flow.

CORD
This charges with a USB /micro USB cord.

VACUUM BRUSHES
This comes with two brushes. One fits on the extension bar and the other fits in the top of the clear blue catcher container.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
VACUUM
Honestly it is okay as a vacuum, but I have other vacuums that are cordless that I prefer. The only thing that this excels at for me is keyboard and other very fine cleaning. I don't find the suction as great as I would like and the blowing air from the vents is so heavy it blows things around as I move with the vacuum.

AIR BLOWING
For blowing, that is another story. This little gem is fabulous. I take the blue top off and put the switch at the blowing and it empties out my sewing machine bobbin area beautifully. It also blows out keyboard and other areas of the laptop that need cleaning.

CHARGES
I have used this since I got it for several weeks and it has not needed to be charged again. I only use it as needed, so it is probably going to stay charged for a while. It only took a little over and hour to charge when I got it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Nice to have as a little vacuum, this excels at blowing air. It is rechargeable so no need to buy any more cans of air that don't work or end up breaking. This is something I have wanted for a long time. I am thrilled to have it.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is fantastic. I absolutely love it. My husband is going to get one for his business too. He ain't touchin' mine! (grins)

review_title: Cord A Bit Stiff, But Works With My Newer Laptop And Older Devices
review_text:
I have a new laptop which has a couple of USB-C ports. The problem is that I need to have some more USB 3.1 ports for hard drives that I move around, thumb drives, and some other devices. This hub really brings some help in that area.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This device is a hub that sits on the table top (you will be hard pressed to balance on your lap). It has enough from for 3 USB devices, as well as another USB-C port so that you are not losing the USB-C port you use to hook it up to.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
The operation is simple. You plug this hub into the USB-C port and then add the other devices as you need them. The transfer rate is decent- not SUPER fast, but it is comparable to my older desktop so I am not that concerned with it anyway. The ports all seem to work well.

ANY PROBLEMS?
The cord that comes with this attached to the unit already is very stiff. It makes it so that the hub does not even want to sit flat on the table top which can be frustrating at times. Other than that, it works pretty well.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For expansion on a newer laptop that uses mostly USB-C ports but you want to use older USB type A 3;1 devices, this is a perfect solution. It enables me to use hard drives, flash drives, and even a DVD-CDROM player as well on it. Transfer rates are good and solid.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This does what i needed it to do and I am satisfied with it. I did wish the cord was a little less stiff, but at least it is not cracked or broken, so I can not complain.

It comes in a beautiful gift box which has cushioning and the typical Santana design to it. The speaker itself is pretty heavy so it is not something you toss in your backpack and run off with. It needs a bit more care than that.

This has a USB charger that will take about 4 hours to charge it up with. There is also a connection where you can get a FAST charger from the company, but you have to contact them for it. The charging cable comes with it just need a USB outlet. The directions warn to only use the original cable that comes with this to charge or there might be damage to the speaker. The voltage must be 5V with current rated at 115A.

CAN THIS RUN WHILE CHARGING?
I do not see in the instructions warnings against this, and it does work while plugged in.

PLAY TIME
This speaker runs out of juice pretty quickly. If you want it to last the entire time of 10 hours, I highly suggest you not put the volume up past 30%. Any higher and the battery time runs down pretty quickly. At 60% you are at the edge of running this down pretty quickly- as in 4 or 5 hours play time only.

PAIRING
I have had no issues pairing this with tablets or phones using Android. Just like when you turn the power on, it says PAIRING in a very loud voice so you will know when it is in pairing mode.

The volume button on this is tricky. If you are not thinking and just quickly press the volume once, instead of it getting slightly louder, you will skip a track. You have to press the volume down and not let up if you want the sound to go up or down depending on the button you press meaning +/-.

CARD SLOT
This speaker can also work off of a TF card (also known as a microSD card). You just have to change from bluetooth mode to card mode using the MODE button.

IS THERE AUX CAPABILITY?
I have an old MP3 player that has higher quality recordings than anything new I have. That only uses AUX and it works great with this.

PAUSE / PLAY
You can pause or play music with this using the MFB button

Let me tell you, this thing ROCKS. I mean it. This speaker is fabulous. Not only does it work great out of the box (after being fully charged) but it sounds better and better as you break it in. It fills the house with music that is great quality and does not have interference or any lag issues either.

I have to say that this speaker is one of the few that I have used which does a beautiful job of intense bass, balanced clear highs but the mids are not muffled at all. It is impressive and what I thought a speaker always should be.

This allows you to add one other speaker to the system so you can have them in two places. I do not have another Europa speaker at the moment I can test that with.

review_title: Great For Certain Uses, Not If You Plan To Carry It A Lot Unless You Have A Case
review_text:
I have had a need for an additional storage solution for my laptop which will enable me to back up files, and transfer between desktop (my workstation) and my laptop when necessary. My goal is to have it as an alternative mini hard drive, so to speak. Let's take a Look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a tiny Jumpdrive, for those who have never used one, it is similar in appearance to a dongle that you use for wireless keyboard or mouse in the USB port. It does not have a case and the packaging is rather difficult to open.

WHAT IS THIS FOR?
This is designed not to carry with you all of the time like some of the flash drives, but to use almost as a mini hard drive and keep it in your laptop or even desktop if desired. It will keep your files handy, has a pretty fast transfer rate, and has a decent amount of storage, depending on what kind of files you plan to store on it.

WHAT ELSE CAN YOU USE THESE FOR?
This can also be theoretically used to keep in the car as a way to play music on your sound system via USB port. I have not been able to do that yet as I have had some issues setting up the right format. I am not sure how security will interact with that..

DOES THIS HAVE SECURITY ON IT?
This drive has a program called ENCDataVault Lite. That will allow you to encrypt your files and have them accessed with a password you set up in case you lose your drive at least your files will be somewhat protected unless it is a hacker who finds it.

HOW IS TRANSFER RATE?
I have used this in a USB3.0 as well as USB2.0 port and both worked well.

DOES THIS FIT TYPE C CONNECTION?
You can not use this in a type C port so please check your laptop or desktop prior to purchase to be sure you have an actual USB port to use this in that is not already being used.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THIS
This drive should come with a tiny case on a keychain or with at least a loop handle on it so that you can put it somewhere safe and not lose it. It does not come with that. Something this small needs to have a colorful case to make it harder to lose. I know that the idea is to have it stay in the unit you use it on mostly, but sometimes you have to take it out and it needs a case.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a tiny drive. It is meant to use in either a car sound system (USB port), on a laptop or desktop that you plan to use it on regularly, and not be moved around constantly. It does not come with any kind of case at all to store it in when not in a port. It does have encryption which is a big plus to theoretically protect files in case of loss.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. The performance is top notch. The fact that this does not come with a case is worth removing a star. Ideally it would not be a problem most of the time, but I still think that it needs protective COLORFUl case for those times you need to remove it from a port and take it from one place to another.

review_title: Expensive To Get Paper, But Worth It For Some Applications
review_text:
We have had Polaroid cameras in the past when they resurrected them for a while, and they were okay, but you wasted a lot of pictures that did not turn out too great. Let's take a look at this.

WHAT IS THIS SMARTPHONE PRINTER LIKE?
This printer is really handy. It is small, easy to carry, recharges well, and is easy to work. It comes with a USB charging cord, instruction book, and a small roll of paper/film. 10 is the number that came with the one I got.

WHAT IS THE ADVANTAGE OF THIS PRINTER?
Although this is a similar idea to the old Polaroid cameras, the difference with this one is that you get to choose the pictures that you want to print, instead of having to print whatever you take.

DOES IT WORK WELL?
This printer worked great. It is not hard at all to print with and we had no trouble with it.

INSTRUCTION BOOK
The instruction book is easy to follow and use.

QUALITY OF PHOTOS
I am enclosing a photo we took and printed with this printer. It is small and easy to keep handy, but still a great photo to put in a tiny frame as a magnet on the refrigerator, or framed for a small desk area. There are plenty of other things we can do with it, but those are just a few ideas.

WHAT DID WE USE IT FOR?
Our kids went to a pretty big march/event not too long ago and they were able to take a quick photo of them and their friends and print everyone a small copy as a memory to hang on to (especially since 1 of them was not too into tech stuff).

IS IT WORTH IT?
The replacement paper is not cheap, but it is doable if you make sure to keep it handy and only use it for special photos. This only comes with 10 so it is easy to blow through that in one sitting. It is nice to have handy, but only if you use it wisely.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a good quality instant print photo to help quickly capture a photo you take with your phone in print, this is a nice little printer. It is easy to carry and store, but it does take expense to keep printer paper handy.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS although it is more like four and a half. I would think this would come with a bit more paper to get you started with it, but not enough of a pain to take a star off at this point.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this a lot.

review_title: Decent Stereo System, But Could Be Better For The Price
review_text:
(WARNING- This is an IN DEPTH review of this stereo to help anyone interested in making an informed buying decision. If you prefer a more brief summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE)
------------
In my house there is a variety of quality of audio items. There are those who really don’t seem to care what kind of quality, as long as it is not too bad. Then there are those who really want to hear definition of sound but they can tolerate lower quality. Then there are those who are so sensitive to audio that they will go on in great depth to analyze and evaluate anything related to stereos whether it is the CD player, bluetooth player, headphones, speakers, and fine tuning of sound.

This stereo system was picked to replace a very old Onkyo which is hanging on, but not for long. Let’s see how this measures up.

WHAT IS THIS STEREO LIKE?
First of all, the write up when I had the opportunity to get this stereo said it was a mini stereo system (different than it is now). I expected it to fit where my other stereo system is which was also a condensed system. Boy was I surprised. This system is a LOT bigger than I expected it to be, but still will fit where I wanted to put it although much tighter than I thought it would.

This system has a CD/bluetooth base to it. There is a dial which is rather large on the front that deals with volume. The CD player has the usual controls on it and there is only an FM radio, no AM. There is an infrared remote which has all of the controls you would need to run the stereo.

LIST OF CONNECTORS
FM Antenna terminal
Line 1 and 2 terminals
Speaker light terminal
Speaker out terminal
USB input on front
Headphone jack on front

MEASUREMENTS
Receiver: 11 x 11 13/16 x 5 5/8
Speakers: 12 x 10 3/4 x 16 5/16
Speaker cords approx 2 ft

HOW DOES THIS UNIT PERFORM?
The CD drawer in the bottom right corner operates about average as far as loading and reading. When playing a CD there were not any problems. As far as the equalizer goes, there are only five functions (one is flat- ewww). For this price there should have been more or customizable options.

The equalizer options sound okay, but the two that we choose most often for a variety of music is jazz and rock. Pop, flat, classic seem lack luster for all of the CDs we tried including classical, rock, country, jazz, hip hop, etc.

Despite limitations, the sound did separate well on one of our CDs which has very muffled and quiet background noise at the beginning of a song that we have never heard clearly before.

SOUND QUALITY
The highs come through pretty well, due to the two tweeters per speaker. The mids and lows depend on the music. They tend to suffer more. It booms but not overly clearly. This is more of a mediocre sound that is designed to pump at very high volumes such as for a party. This is not high fidelity sound if that is what you are looking for.

SPEAKER LIGHTS
Although they are interesting at first, the lights seem kind of odd. For the price, it should have had better options. You can choose colors that stay on and do not blink or change out of seven choices. You can choose to have it flash and change color continuously, or you can choose to have the lights flash fast and change continuously, or you can flash the light in white. None of the settings go in time with the music.

You can also opt for no lights on as well. The lights do connect to the speakers by a second wire- it is not in with the speaker connector.

BLUETOOTH
The bluetooth took a while to recognize on the phone. We used android. Once it was paired, many types of music from old to new tracks, and older songs were not as clear or loud as newer tracks. As far as decoding from the bluetooth, it sounded pretty good and did not drop once.

RADIO
The FM sound on this was good and no complaints. Reception was pretty standard, nothing remarkable, but not horrible either.

REMOTE
Remote has to be pointed directly at the receiver. There were a few times where we had to press buttons twice because it would not pick up the signals. The remote itself is black and very small, which makes it easy to misplace. Marking it with neon paint is something we are going to do to make it harder to lose.

PROS
Nice and loud
Picks up highs very well
Bluetooth and CD player in one both work well
Two tweeters per speaker is nice

CONS
Remote very small
Lights sometimes are annoying
Wires are way too short- speakers can not be separated to put in corners of room
Speaker wires are proprietary to the receiver with special attachment (can not use other speakers)

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to have a good middle of the road stereo with nice separation of highs and decent sound, you might like this one. The lights and loud capacity also make this a great party unit if you like to fill up a large room or house with sound. Remote works okay , but speakers can not be separated very far. Due to proprietary speaker connections, the only way to change that would be to splice the wires if you are good at electronics.

RATING
This stereo is rather high priced for what you get. It does not have any bass boost, or customizing options for the equalizer. The sound is loud, but not overly high quality. Although this is not a bad unit, it really is not jaw dropping either. I want to give this THREE AND A HALF STARS due to the price and what you get for it. Unfortunately there is only a choice between four and three stars.

I will update in the future to indicate if the cord is still performing well after an extended period of time.

review_title: (SUPPORT  & COMPARE TO SAMSUNG)Excellent Tablet For the Money, But Don't Get Rid of Your Laptop
review_text:
(SEE END FOR UPDATED COMPARISON TO SAMSUNG GALAXY 4)
I have ready many reviews on tablets, and have found most of them to be why a certain tablet is better than another to the nth degree with all kinds of technical jargon which really just pits one expert against another. As a person who tutors people who are not technologically savvy, I am going to review this tablet from the point of view of someone who has not had one before and whether or not this is a good choice if you want to get one.

I have been told by several business people and those who claim to be very tech savvy that they have gotten rid of their laptops except for occasional spreadsheet work in their offices or at home. Can you get rid of your laptop by getting a tablet like this? Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS TABLET LIKE?
SIDE SWITCHES
This tablet is around the size of an ipad mini or a Kindle. The on off switch is on the upper right hand side (with screen facing you) and below it is a rocker switch just below the power switch. There is a space between the two buttons which will allow for elastic bands should you want to get a case for it that has them. That will make it so that the tablet will not be turned on and off by accident. The power button has to be pushed and held for a moment before the unit turns on.

SCREEN
The tablet screen is shiny which can be annoying, but that is the nature of the beast.
The touch sensitivity is excellent- I did not find any problems with response time or lag.
The orientation changing when you turn the screen around is also well set. It works nicely and is not overly sensitive.

INPUT
To input into the tablet, you have a choice to either type or speak what you want the tablet to do. I have to say that this tablet responds very well to either set of input. After working with several i-pads, my daughter constantly raves about how this Acer tablet is superior in the way it responds to input with the microphone than the i-pads are. I have not had any problem with typing into this tablet beyond what I normally do on any unit. The microphone occasionally mistypes a word, but it is not nearly as bad as I expected it to.

Response time of the tablet is excellent. I am quite impressed with how quickly it responds to input without lag or difficulty.

APPS
I have put a few apps on this unit which tend to be popular with tablet users. Sketchbook Pro is one of those apps. I really like it. The response time is good, and the app seems to work well on this tablet. I also love the radio app which allows you to listen to radio stations in the area or around the country. With a case that folds into a stand, it is a great panel to use in a room where you want to listen to the radio.

Quite a few apps that come in the tablet already are handy and easy to use. The screen is quite intuitive and easy to use.

INTERNET USAGE
This tablet is wi-fi accessible to the internet which means that you can not go out in no-man's land to use it like you can an android phone, but you have to be near a wi-fi station to use it.

The wi-fi response time is excellent- although it does occasionally lag when the signals get weak- something that all wi-fi units will do.

Android is a Google engine so everything you do will be monitored by Google or you will be using something they have designed to get where you want to go. You can find other ways to purchase apps if you don't like the Google store, however, such as Amazon.

This tablet comes with McAfee virus scan which is not a huge deal, but I am not sure how to replace that yet, should I desire to do so.

CAMERA
I am not a big advocate of phone and tablet cameras. This one has a decent camera to use on the back, and an adequate camera on the front of the camera to use for Skype which is pretty much all you need. If you want a really nice camera, buy one. For quick pictures to capture something you want to show someone, then this will be fine.

PROS
Easy to hold
Screen responsive
Speech recognition works well
Good fast performance
Boots up quickly
Clear screen makes reading books nice
Good colors for photos on the screen (better than laptops)
Power button hard to accidentally turn on or off
Learning is pretty intuitive for first time users

CONS
Wi-fi only
Not as easy to use as laptop for extensive typing
Can be a bit clumsy to use at times (the nature of tablets)
Start up literature is a bit underwhelming for first time users

THE BOTTOM LINE

CAN YOU GET RID OF YOUR LAPTOP?
Can you get rid of your laptop to substitute this tablet? My answer would be no.

Even if all you did was go on the internet to wander through web sites, using a tablet is a bit cumbersome if you want to do any kind of extensive writing. If you use the microphone, it will probably be pretty accurate, but you will still have to use the keyboard to correct what is used.

For occasional internet usage, watching videos, movies, and reading books, this tablet is fabulous. I think it works beautifully. I would say that it is just as nice as other more expensive tablets and you will invest a lot less money in it.

If you want a tablet and do not want to pay a fortune for it, this is the way to go. The Acer Iconia A1-830 is an excellent value and I use mine a lot. I just could not substitute it completely for my laptop. I prefer to have a choice in my browser, features, and fine tuning or replacement of parts should I desire to do so.

I do find that having the tablet helps a lot when I want to quickly do something on the internet and don't want to boot up my laptop. This tablet is pretty quick and I like it. If you are a tech fanatic and have to have the biggest and best, you might find fault with this tablet, however. It is worth a test run in any case.

UPDATE 3/4/2015 SAMSUNG GALAXY 4 (8 inch) vs ACER ICONIA A1-830
I have had quite a chance to get to know this tablet over time and also to use a Samsung Galaxy 4 8 inch tablet in comparison both on its own and with a keyboard. After working with both tablets, I have to say that I still prefer the Acer over the Samsung and here is why:

-Acer has slightly smaller screen area, but is easier to work on
-Acer has the return and menu buttons incorporated into the screen instead of on the side so it rotates with screen
-Acer surface is less shiny and has less glare
-Performance of Acer is the same as the Samsung in terms of speed
-Wifi of Acer is as good as the Samsung
-keyboard of Acer is much easier to use than Samsung (the one in the screen)
-set up of the Acer is much easier and user friendly
-voice commands on Acer works MUCH better than on the Samsung
-Samsung speaker is a bit nicer than Acer, but I use a bluetooth speaker for best sound anyway.
-Samsung battery does last a bit longer than the Acer, but the frustrations of the Samsung still make me prefer the Acer.

All in all, I have to say that I have tried to honestly look at both tablets and give them a fair comparison and I still like the Acer better. The price is better and the ease of use is better too. The microphone on the Acer seems much more responsive than the Samsung. The screen of the Samsung is a bit more dense in terms of pixels and color perhaps, but the glare is more annoying. I also get very irritated at the side buttons on the Samsung. They are static (stay put) and when the tablet is on its side, it is way too easy to hit a button that screws up what I am trying to do on the Samsung. This is especially true when I am trying to type something and is VERY frustrating.

There is one thing about the Samsung that I really wish the Acer had and that is longer battery time. The Samsung does run a little longer than the Acer without having to recharge. The speaker on the Samsung is a bit nicer, but with my portable bluetooth speaker as my main source of listening, I don't find that to be a problem for me.

So, after time and the chance to use the Acer and the Samsung so I could compare them, I still really like the Acer tablet better. Because I do a lot of graphics work and computer work, I still would not get rid of my laptop or desktop, but I do save a lot of time using this tablet when I want to look up quick information and cruise the internet.

UPDATE March 2016
I wanted to take a moment to update you concerning this device.

As time has gone on I have enjoyed using the Acer Iconia A1-830 very much. It is a nice tablet for an affordable price.

HAVE I HAD PROBLEMS?
A few.
-tablet went nuts as if a baby were in charge of it and had five Redbull drinks first. I rebooted and cleared out some programs and all was fine.

-I could not move my information from my device to my PC- this was solved, but it has taken a lot of research, effort and time. The support at the Acer site is rather pitiful to be honest. That is one thing that I will say about this, is compared to Samsung, Acer does not support their devices as well as they should, but then again, the price is a lot less too.

IS THIS STILL WORKING?
Yes., I use it daily and it still is working. I keep the HD less than 60% full as I do with most devices as they tend to work best that way. I find that it connects via wi-fi at times when other devices in the house do not. I also find that the battery wears down a lot less quickly if I turn off location and even wi-fi if I don't need it.

NO UPGRADE PAST KIT-KAT 4.4.2
There will be no upgrades to Lollipop or beyond, so if you want a more modern unit, then try for something new.

MY REVIEW STANDS
I now have a Samsung Galaxy Tab S2 that I am using and it of course passes the Acer by a mile, but then again, it is a much more expensive machine too.

review_title: Great Tablet, A Few Idiosyncrasies But Still Like It
review_text:
I have been using Wacom tablets for so long, I can not begin to tell you. Perhaps it would make a difference to say that my first tablet I got was before Painter hit the market when it was developed by Fractal Design.

My most recent tablet was a workhorse- the ArtZII Tablet which was a pro version graphics tablet. I never had trouble with it and it worked with everything, including most games, believe it or not.

Unfortunately, the drivers began to malfunction so much with WinXP that I was forced to get a new tablet. If I could have gotten a serial to USB conversion adapter, I probably would still be using it if I had a driver to use with it.

The Intuos5 Touch Medium Pen Tablet is a wonderful tablet. Thanks to the previous reviewers, I did not even attempt to use it until I got the clear plastic cover for the pad to keep my pen from wearing down the nibs. I am SO glad I did. Now I feel like I am at home like I did with the ArtZII pad.

WHAT I USE THIS WITH

I like to use this pad with handwriting added to documents to sign things.
I use this for Corel Painter
I use this for Corel Graphics Suite X5.
I use this for general mouse uses when I don't need to use a lot of words on a keyboard.

WHAT I LIKE

The touch feature is helpful when I want to turn a page in Painter just like I would in real life
I like the responsiveness of the pen
I like that the screen can be made larger or smaller with my fingers.
I like that the light goes on in the screen to remind me that it is on.
Auto keyboard that pops out allows me to do minimal typing and not have to grab my keyboard

WHAT I DON'T LIKE

Silly, probably, but the round programming spots on the left side drive me nuts. They are not marked, and I just can not get into them yet.
I don't like that every time I grab the tablet near the round rubber area, it sends the screen coming in- but it does go away okay
The screen changing from one direction to another does not always work smoothly. Sometimes it gets stuck

A FEW MORE COMMENTS

I have not really tried programming this pad at this point as I have had not had the opportunity to do so as of yet. I usually am in such a hurry to do some photo work or graphics or sign something that I grab, do what I need and move on. I hope to study it more in depth in the future and use it even more than I do now.

The programming in Corel Painter X3 seems to work beautifully with this pad which I very much appreciate. The touch levels are fantastic and I feel the closest that I have ever been to using natural media on a computer than I have ever been in the years I have worked on computers with natural media programming- as I said, that is quite some time now.

The pen stand is kind of annoying, I am not sure why they set it up that way, but it is something I can live with. The pen itself is comfortable enough to work with and relatively easy to operate without too much thinking or reading of directions.

I will update this review as I learn more about this system and let you know how I like it. So far, I am quite happy with it, and have had no crashes or lockups while using it. The drivers load up well and I don't seem to have any difficulties.

I am using Windows 7 on a system I recently built so am just getting to know it better.

He has very large hands, and I have medium hands and both of us find this mouse comfortable and easy to use. It is a simple straightforward mouse without tons of bells and whistles, but it is solid.

I highly recommend this mouse!

review_text:
This is a NAS drive, suitable for prosumer or professional NAS units. The concept of being a NAS drive is that if the drive encounters a read error (which happens every once in a while with any disk drive), you don't want the drive to take a possibly long detour into rereading the data and applying its error correction algorithms to recover the data correctly. Rather, you want the drive to give up quickly, and allow the remaining drives in the RAID array to reconstruct the data. So that means "fail early, fail often." The reason for this behavior is that if a drive in a RAID array takes too long to respond to a read request (while doing error correction), the NAS device might decide that the drive has failed, and fail it out of the RAID array, requiring a spare drive to be added needlessly to rebuild the RAID array.

However, my trouble was that Amazon's packaging was completely inadequate to protect the drive during shipment. I was astonished that anyone would ship anything like that, especially a delicate piece of machinery. The drive does seem to work, but I'll have a better idea of that over time.

There are two more considerations for NAS drives. You want to pay attention to whether the drive uses native 4k blocks, and probably all drives in your array should be the same in that respect. And some NAS devices are designed for one or the other. Seagate makes both conventional and 4k-native drives, and the product descriptions aren't clear in this respect. Do a search on the drive's model number and you can learn this information.

Also, consider whether the drive uses conventional magnetic recording (CMR) or shingled magnetic recording (SMR). For typical desktop use either is ok. For NAS use, you should always use CMR drives. Again, doing a search on the drive's model number should help you figure out what kind of recording method is used by each particular drive.

review_title: Great sound, good design, could be better
review_text:
This product and the similar [[ASIN:B004CQNTF6 Sennheiser CX 880i Premium Ear-Canal Headphones with Microphone & Smart Remote]] earbuds have great sound. The 880 has the integrated volume control, and the 880i has the iPhone/iPod compatible mic/volume attachment. (Even though that product is designed for iPhone/iPod, the mic and pause button -- but not the volume buttons -- work with my Blackberry Bold 9700.) There are numerous thoughtful details in this product, and a couple of significant shortcomings which I'll describe. Overall, this is a very excellent 4-star product.

Pros:
The sound is just great. You can get earbuds with better sound, but it won't be cheap. I listen to all kinds of music including many genres of popular music as well as classical, and the sound with all is very smooth. The highs are very open and clean. Some listeners may prefer to slightly boost the midrange. The bass, including the deep bass, is solid without using any bass boost. I hear a small peak in the mid-bass. I make very *slight* adjustments in my iTunes equalizer to make the already great sound a bit better.

The fit will depend on how well the included selection of tips fit your ears. In my case, I found tips that fit very well. They stay put very snugly, and they're very comfortable even for longer listening sessions. The shape of the ear pieces is angled, and that works out very well. The way the cord exits the ear pieces is also pretty good.

These are designed to be good for noise isolation, and Sennheiser pulls this off really well. Note that noise isolation is different from noise cancellation, but the end result is very similar. With both, you don't hear outside noises and you can play the sound at lower volumes (which helps to protect the ears). In my experience, noise isolation works better at higher frequencies, and noise cancellation works better at low frequencies (like airplane noise). I've already used these earbuds on one flight, and I'm happy enough that they'll find a home in my travel kit.

Speaking of the travel kit, the included case is surprisingly well designed. I love it. And the little cleaning tool really does help to keep the ear pieces clean, along with the well-designed diaphragm covers.

Cons:
As other reviewers have mentioned, there are significant microphonics issues with the cord. This is disappointing, since the sound is otherwise so excellent. I've found I can eliminate most of this problem by stuffing the middle of the cable inside my shirt a bit, so there's less loose cable to rub on my collar. That works pretty well. Still, a different material for the cord could solve this better.

Also, the cable feels a bit fragile, especially where it joins the earbuds themselves. I've been using this less than a month, so I don't know how this will fare in the long term.

On balance, these are easily the best earbuds I've ever had. I'm finding new joy in listening to music when I'm out and about, or late at night when I don't want to disturb the rest of the family.

*** UPDATE ***
Six months later, and I'm still very happy with these earbuds. There's one problem I've grown very tired of -- If you don't put them away properly in their case, the cord gets badly tangled. It takes much longer than it should to untangle these guys. Also, the plug end has become noisy where it attaches to my MP3 player. Same problem on 2 players, so it's the cord for sure. Not too bad yet that I want to return it; not sure if it will get worse over time.

review_title: Great sound, but design is a bit awkward
review_text:
First of all, these speakers sound just great, they really do. I'll echo the comments that the cords are an awkward design, depending on where you place them in relation to your sound source and listening position.

The power on-off button is on the top of the subwoofer, but the volume up-down control is on one of the satellites. And the sub's level control is on the sub itself. Aside from just plain being a bit weird, it means you're going to have to keep both the sub and one of the satellites within easy reach. Also, the cord that connects to your sound source is attached to the sub (as is the power cord); combined with the controls on the sub, this is just plain awkward. I'm using these speakers at work, and I have the sub on the floor under my desk. I'm controlling the volume from iTunes, so that's cool. But it would be very annoying if I had to be using the speaker's controls all the time.

A minor annoyance is the shape of the metal legs for the satellites. They are sturdy and look nice, but they take up much more space on my crowded desk than I'd like. Other speaker systems use more vertically shaped satellite stands, which take up half the space. These satellites are much more squat.

I also have one of the better Logitech 2.1 systems, which also sounds great. But Logitech puts all the controls on a little control unit that you can keep in easy reach. (And also has a headphone output too.) That's a much more convenient design. But between the two, the sound of these Altec Lansing speakers is superior.

Here's the dealmaker for me -- the bass control on the subwoofer can be turned all the way down, so the sub isn't putting out any sound at all. This is a great feature because it lets me play just the satellites late at night, and I'm not disturbing my housemate in the adjoining room.

I ordered the 'RALENO LED Video Lighting Kits With 75inch Light Stand, 1 Durable Handbag And 2-Pack 384 LED Soft Video Light, Built-in Lithium Battery 3200K-6500K Video Lighting Kits For YouTube Photography Shooting' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts.

I ordered this kit to add more lighting options to my photography gear. My first impressions were that this kit is pretty complete in the sense that you get two lights with A/C power cords, stands for both lights, two shoe mounts and a decent carry case. With that said, I was not so impressed with overall quality of all included items. However, for all that you get in this kit, I am still quite impressed. Although this kit isn't of the best build quality it most definitely has great value with all that is included. The lights themselves are smaller than I had expected and the highest brightness setting isn't as bright as I hoped, yet it still has a place, and has come in handy many times to ad a bit more lighting to some of my projects.

I love that it includes the soft case and that the lights themselves have screens on the back that will actually show the color temperatures as well as the brightness level. I have more expensive lights that just have knobs on the back to adjust these settings with no easy way to know what color temperature you are at. This in-of-itself is a huge bonus as far as I am concerned. With this set I an easily select the exact color temp for each light to match. The stands are pretty basic. They are lightweight and easy to set up and take down. I am not so impressed with the quality of the Hot Shoe adapters as they are hard to solidly tighten the angle down without feeling like I am going to break the plastic knobs. They do function however, and I do appreciate that they included these, otherwise you would not be able to adjust the angle of the lights. The soft carrying case is decent and does have some padding if you don't throw out the included foam inserts.

Overall I find this kit to be effective, and have found that even though I may criticize many aspects of it, I do find myself using it quite often because of how convenient and easy to use and set up. There is most definitely value to this kit and I think that it would make a great lighting starter kit as well as a kit to ad more lighting options to your current lights. I hope that this was helpful.

review_title: Nice, but not amazing for the price.
review_text:
I ordered the 'Malektronic Interstellar Premium Wireless Noise Cancelling Over-Ear Headphones' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I am no audiophile, but I do love a good quality headphone that is built well and sound good. Sounding good or even great is really subjective depending on personal preference. For the going retail price of these Malektronic Interstellar Premium Wireless Noise Cancelling Over-Ear Headphones, I really expected much more than what I personally find these to be. I'll break my experience and thoughts into a few main points that stood out to me.

Comfort - These are comfortable but they don't fit as snug as I would have liked. I have a small head for a 54yro male, and even on the smallest adjustment setting, they just don't hug my ears like I would have hoped for such an expensive set of headphones.

Noise Cancelling - yea this is a big one for me right hear (see what I did there). I am not at all impressed with the Noise Cancelling in these headphones for the price. I mean it's OK, but I have ANC wireless earbuds that do a much better job for about the same price. There are only two settings. ANC On and ANC Off. For me, It's really hard to tell whether I've turned it on or off. There is no indicator like others I have that would either beep or greet you with some kind of prompt letting you know which mode you are in (there are voice prompts when you turn them on or off so why not anything for ANC modes). In fact the only way I can truly tell that it's on or off, is to pause the song and push the ANC button at which point it's pretty clear. However, and with that said, I do notice that when it's on, the music almost sounds more heavy on the Bass. It's almost like the Bass is supposed to give that "ANC" feel. Remember, I am no audiophile but this is just my observation.

Sound - Now I can say this, and that is that these do sound good until you get close to max volume. At which point they just don't hold up to the volume. Not that they get really loud but if you have the ANC on and you are listening to a heavy Bass song, they tend to bottom out just a tad. It's not bad but again for this price point, I would have expected better. The highs are nice but even better when ANC is off. Mids are there and probably sound good in either mode really. Another thing I noticed is that if you take these off while the music is still playing at full volume, they sound like they are rattling and sound a bit distorted. However when you put them back on, there is no distortion like I noticed with them off. That was kind of strange.

Micro USB charging - I always have to point this out. It's 2020 companies and USB C should be the standard any more in my opinion. Just saying.

Build Quality - They aren't the worst I have seen or tried but at this price point they are not the best either. They are pretty much plastic although fairly solid.

Buttons - The buttons are hidden/covered near the edge of the ear pads and they took me a while to figure out where they are, but after using them for a while, I actually like the fact that they look to be buttonless.

Looks/design - These really do look nice both on and off. They don't look cheap which is nice, as I have some others that just look ugly and I refuse to wear haha. The design is well thought out and I do love how they fold flat and compact into the very nice hard case.

So with all that said, I do like these headphones. They sound pretty good. The ANC is meh but they are comfortable besides not fitting as snug as I would prefer. Build quality is decent and I do love they way they fold up and store nicely into the included hard case. Thank you for including this Maletronics! Micro USB charging is a bummer but they also can be used wired with the included cable if you forget to get them charged up. Battery life is not bad. 30hrs might be pushing it if you like to listen to them loud and are always using the ANC. I have yet to test that fully as the longest I generally go is maybe an hour at a time. So for me the battery life is fine.

Overall, I really want to love these, and I actually do like them a lot, but I am just not that "Wowed" at this price point. I have other brands at or around this price point that I like better. Now maybe I got a dud pair and that very well could be, but I don't dislike them. They are nice and I plan to keep them around as a back-up pair. I hope that this was helpful.

review_title: Great gimbal with a few issues.
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:139d076ab53a69b4c9863743d4ea0df8]] I ordered the ‘MOZA AirCross 2 Stabilizer 3-Axis Handheld Lightweight Powerful Gimbal for Camera Up 7Lb Intuitive Control Panel Intelligent Features Advanced Shooting Modes 12h Battery Life Beyond Your Imagination’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

First off I would like to let it be known that this is my very first camera gimbal. With that said, understand that I am not very savvy when it comes to gimbals. I am fairly new to filmmaking and videography. Now that you know that this will not necessarily be a super technical review, I will share some of what I have experienced thus far with this gimbal.

I ordered this originally to use with my Canon 60D DSLR. From the Moza website, I did find the 60D listed as a compatible camera, so I figured that this gimbal would work which it, it but not exactly how I had expected. The 60D is a DSLR camera which is a bit on the heavy side and I did find it a bit tricky at first to get the camera to balance correctly. Once balanced, the gimbal did work, though I could tell it struggled. I have since read and watched many reviews with even lighter cameras, and users have stated the same thing. The Moza AirCross 2 is rated for a max weight of 7lbs and my 60D comes in at 2.7lbs with the EF 17-40mm L lens, so there really shouldn’t be an issue. Yet when checking the gimbal it showed all axis at or near 100% which means that the gimbal is working hard to handle the camera weight even though it’s nowhere near the max weight advertised.

Since then, I have upgraded my camera to the Canon 90D (yes another DSLR). It’s slightly lighter but not by too much. I am still using the EF 17-40mm L lens which, in-of-itself is a fairly heavy lens. It’s probably the heaviest yet the best glass that I own. This has made little to no difference in the Moza AirCross2 working hard on all axis however it does seem to handle this set up a bit better. See attached video and note that I had added a small microphone to the camera which turned out not being set up right on the new camera. So the balance was slightly off for the recording yet the gimbal worked. There was some slight shaking in the footage but overall I was happy with the performance. Again, being an ameture at this I am just happy to have a working gimbal haha.

Now for some other issues. First I cannot get the 90D mounted and balanced to where the Roll axis bar won’t hit the Pan axis bar when trying to do a full Roll. This is a real bummer. I am not sure if it’s something that I am doing wrong or this is just the way it is with this particular camera. Second issue I have had is that the Moza AirCross2 comes with a plethora of cables to hook up to your various cameras. It was trial and error for me on both cameras to find which one I was “supposed” to use. Eventually it seems that both (60D and the 90D) seem to do better with the Micro USB cable yet again, I am not positive which I am “supposed” to be using. I could not find any documentation that stated what cable should go with what camera. Third, I thought that I would have more control over the camera with this gimbal. I understand not having all the options available for the 60D, but I figured there would be more options that I could control the camera with on the 90D. All I can seem to do via the gimbal on the 90D is control the video record button. For the 60D I was able to get the camera to autofocus and take a picture but that's about it. Even with the very nice App that you can download for the gimbal, there isn’t a whole lot that I can get to work to control either camera. Again I would have thought the 90D would have been more compatible seeing as it has both WiFi and Bluetooth capabilities. I do plan to do more research as there may be settings on the camera that I need to enable.

On the plus side of things, this is a nice quality gimbal. It is a bit heavy with my camera mounted but it feels solid. The App is nice although I have not used it to its full potential as of yet. The included foam hard case is very nice and keeps everything safe and tidy. Everything fits snug. Some parts more than others but nothing is going to be flopping around inside. The footage taken with this gimbal is so much smoother than if I were to try and take it all hand-held. Even running looks great (to my untrained eye). Again see attached video.

Overall, I am both disappointed and quite happy with this gimbal. Disappointed that it’s not all I had hoped for, yet very happy to actually have a working gimbal. It’s been a huge learning curve for me and I really want to give this gimbal a 5 star rating. However I feel that with the advertised max weight being an issue for me and others much more savvy, that takes one star away. Plus the fact that the Roll axis bar hits the Pan axis bar when the camera and gimbal are balanced is annoying. For that I won’t dock a star, as this may be user error. I would just say that if you own a mirrorless camera then this would be great for you. If you own a heavier DSLR, you may want to look at spending a little more for one better rated for the extra weight.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:13857efa3820e6eb7b02a0a8943823dd]] I am reviewing the ‘AODELAN Camera Wirless Shutter Release Timer Intervalometer for Canon EOS 800D, 200D, 80D,750D, 650D, 600D,1300D, 1200D, 90D, M6 Mark II, 6D Mark II, 7D Mark II; Fujifilm X-T3; Olympus E-M1 Mark II‘

I have been looking for a wireless shutter release for my Canon 60D for quite some time now but haven’t been able to decide what kind to get. There are quite a few out there from basic to full featured like this one seems to be. Most of what I shoot is landscape or product photos but I would like to do more in the line of Time-Lapse, Wildlife and Night Photography. This Aodelan looks to have a bit of everything that I needed. So far I have only used it for product photography and I used it briefly with a Time-Lapse. During that little bit of testing I found that I could only set the remote to take a total of 199 images and set intervals. I set it for 199 shots at 10 second intervals but was cut short by rain hitting my gear and only ended up with 149 shots. (See attached video) There really should be a way to set it for much longer as 199 shots compiled into a Time-Lapse is only a few seconds long. I am still learning this device so hopefully I can figure out if 199 image is truly the limit. If so, this is very disappointing..

As for the Wireless Shutter remote, it functions perfectly for my needs. I am able to set the shot up and wirelessly trigger my shutter with the remote from quite a distance, which will be perfect for capturing the Hummingbirds that frequent my kitchen window feeder. I will be able to set up the shot outside and trigger the shutter from inside the house when the Hummingbirds are in position. Night photography will also be fun to try, as I can now remotely trigger the shutter using Bulb mode without causing any camera shake. You can also use this kit wired and only need to plug the Transmitter into the Remote port on the camera, but personally I will mainly be using this kit Wirelessly.

The quality and features of this kit are really nice. Both the Transmitter and Receiver are made of what seems to be a good quality plastic. Both devices take 2XAA batteries which were not included. Battery life seems to be good thus far and I would imagine that my newly installed batteries should last a good long time.

Though I am still learning this kit, I did notice that when trying to take continuous shots, it seems to limit the camera from shooting as fast as it is capable of. This isn’t a huge deal (because this isn’t what I plan to use this kit for) but I thought it worth mentioning.

Other than the 199 shot limit when shooting Time-Lapse I am very pleased with the overall performance and quality of this kit and think it is good value for the money.

*Update - I just found the setting that will allow unlimited shots during the "Timer" mode. This will allow you to take as many shots as desired for Time-Lapse photography. This is really nice though I do wish you could limit it to a higher number than 199. How about 999? lol

[[VIDEOID:7bf3152b4f75f13e38ced1bc81135156]] I ordered the ‘Falcon Eyes F7 12W RGB Led Light,with Honeycomb Grid and Softbox,CRI 97,2500K-9000K Adjustable with Magnet Adsorption Function, OLED Display,Multiple Scenario Mode’ for review and would like to share some of my thoughts.
So I have tried several different pocket lights similar to this one and I must say that this FalconEyes F7 is my absolute favorite. It’s just so versatil with so many options. I so appreciate the 1 inch OLED display on the back because of the info it provides. This kit includes a silicon light diffuser and a silicon honeycomb attachment which directs the light without bleed off. The kit comes with a USB C charging cable (Yay) ,a soft protective zippered case, cold shoe attachment and an adjustable mounting bracket. On the back of the unit it has a helpful HSI (or as I call it - RGB) light chart guide. This shows the spectrum of Hue settings that give you a base number when looking for a particular color. The frame of the light has built in magnets that can be used for mounting to a metal surface.
The Falcon Eyes F7 pocket light has three modes. First mode lets you adjust the light from 9000K (cool) way down to 2500K (warm). You can adjust the brightness level in this mode. Second mode is the Scenario or Scene mode which lets you choose from 20 different pre-programmed lighting effects such as White Strobe Light, Flashing Red Warning light, flashing police car, Lightning, ect. I really don’t use this mode often, but they could be fun and useful for videos. Third mode is HSI mode as I mentioned before. You can adjust the HSI color you want, and adjust the Saturation of the chosen color. This is a great mode for both video and photography. See attached video for a demo of the modes.
The Falcon Eyes F7 build quality is amazing compared to other pocket lights I have. It’s built with a solid aluminium alloy frame, a USB C charging port for fast charging.
Overall, the Falcon Eyes F7 is an incredible Pocket Light. It’s so bright and very versatile. The Build quality, numerous features and the invaluable included accessories make this a handy tool to add to your photography and videography bag.

I have a variety of Pocket lights and this one tops the charts for compact size, brightness and features. It has three modes to choose from. The first is the basic White light mode where you can adjust the temperature from cool 8500K to warm 2500K. From this mode you can also adjust the brightness. The second mode is the HSI or as I call it the RGB mode. This mode allows you to change the color of the light. From this mode you can also adjust the saturation of the chosen color as well as adjust the brightness level. The third mode is the effects mode which has 9 different pre-programmed flashing light modes. From this mode you can also adjust the brightness level of the effect. The third mode I rarely use, but it is a fun one to have and I will eventually use it for videos.
